title.zh: 卷八十四 列傳第四十四 鄧琬 袁顗 孔覬
title.en: Volume 84 Biographies 44: Deng Wan, Yuan Yi, Kong Ji
title.raw: 卷八十四 列傳第四十四 鄧琬 袁顗 孔覬 Volume 84 Biographies 44: Deng Wan, Yuan Yi, Kong Ji

sentences.zh: 鄧琬，字元琬，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Deng Wan, styled Yuanwan, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan, whose courtesy name was Yuanwan, came from Nanchang in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖混，曾祖玄，並為晉尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: His founding ancestor Hun and great-grandfather Xuan both served as Directors of the Personnel Section in the Imperial Secretariat under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His founding ancestor Hun and his great-grandfather Xuan had both been Directors of the Personnel Section in the Jin Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖潛之，鎮南長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qianzhi was Chief Clerk to the General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qianzhi had served as chief clerk to the General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 父胤之，世祖征虜長史，吏部郎，彭城王義康大將軍長史、豫章太守，光祿勳。

translations.literal: His father Yinzhi was Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians under Emperor Shizu, Director of the Personnel Section, Chief Clerk to the Grand General under Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, Administrator of Yuzhang, and Household Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yinzhi had served Emperor Shizu as chief clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians and as Director of the Personnel Section, and later as chief clerk to the Grand General under Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, Administrator of Yuzhang, and Household Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 琬初為州西曹主簿，南譙王義宣征北行參軍，轉參軍事，又隨府轉車騎參軍，仍轉府主簿，江州治中從事史。

translations.literal: Wan at first served as Chief Clerk of the Western Section of the provincial staff, as Acting Aide on the Northern Campaign under Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, then as Staff Officer, then followed the princely establishment to become Cavalry Aide, then establishment chief clerk, and finally Supervisor of the Secretariat of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wan began as chief clerk of the western section of the provincial staff, then served Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan as acting aide on the northern campaign, became a staff officer, followed the princely establishment as cavalry aide and then as its chief clerk, and finally rose to supervisor of the Jiangzhou secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖起義，版琬為輔國將軍、南海太守，率軍伐蕭簡於廣州，攻圍踰年，乃克。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu raised the righteous army, he commissioned Wan as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Nanhai, leading troops to attack Xiao Jian at Guangzhou; the siege lasted more than a year before the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu launched his uprising, he commissioned Wan as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Nanhai and sent him to lead troops against Xiao Jian at Guangzhou; the siege lasted more than a year before the city fell.

sentences.zh: 以臧質反，為江州刺史宗愨所執，值赦原。

translations.literal: Because Zang Zhi rebelled, he was seized by the Inspector of Jiang Province Zong Que; he was pardoned when an amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi rebelled, Wan was seized by Jiangzhou inspector Zong Que but was released under a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 琬弟璩，與臧質同逆，質敗從誅；

translations.literal: Wan's younger brother Qu joined Zang Zhi in rebellion; when Zhi was defeated he was executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's younger brother Qu had joined Zang Zhi in the rebellion; when Zhi was defeated, Qu was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 琬弟環亦坐誅。

translations.literal: Wan's younger brother Huan was also executed by association.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's younger brother Huan was also put to death by association.

sentences.zh: 琬在遠，又有功，免死遠徙，仍停廣州。

translations.literal: Wan was far away and had also rendered service, so he was spared death and exiled to a distant place, remaining at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wan was far away and had also rendered meritorious service, he was spared execution and exiled to a distant post, where he remained at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，得還，除給事中，尚書庫部郎，都水使者，丹陽丞，本州大中正。

translations.literal: After a long time he was allowed to return and was appointed Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Gentleman of the Arsenal Section in the Imperial Secretariat, Commissioner of Waterways, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, and Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was permitted to return and was appointed Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Gentleman of the Arsenal Section in the Imperial Secretariat, Commissioner of Waterways, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, and Chief Rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，車駕幸歷陽，追思在藩之舊，下詔曰：「故光祿勳、前征虜長史鄧胤之體局沈隱，累任著績。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming, when the imperial carriage visited Liyang, the emperor recalled his old ties in the princely establishment and issued an edict saying: 'The late Household Minister of the Imperial Clan and former Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians Deng Yinzhi was of a composed and reserved bearing and achieved distinction in successive offices.'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming, when the emperor visited Liyang, he recalled his old ties from his years in the princely establishment and issued an edict: 'The late Household Minister of the Imperial Clan and former chief clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Deng Yinzhi, was of a composed and reserved bearing and achieved distinction in successive offices.'

sentences.zh: 朕昔當藩重，首先佐務，心力款盡，弗忘於懷。

translations.literal: When I formerly bore the weight of a princely establishment, he was the first to assist in affairs, exhausting his heart and strength in loyal service—I have never forgotten this.
translations.idiomatic: When I formerly bore the weight of a princely establishment, he was the first to assist me in affairs and gave his heart and strength in loyal service; I have never forgotten this.

sentences.zh: 往歲息璩凶悖，自取誅翦，沿恩及琬，特免釁戮。

translations.literal: In years past my son Qu was violent and rebellious and brought execution upon himself; extending grace to Wan, I specially spared him from punishment for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: In years past my son Qu was violent and rebellious and brought execution upon himself; extending grace to Wan, I specially spared him from punishment for the offense.

sentences.zh: 今可擢為給事黃門侍郎，以旌胤之宿誠。」

translations.literal: He may now be promoted to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, in recognition of Yinzhi's long-standing loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: Wan may now be promoted to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, in recognition of Yinzhi's long-standing loyalty.'

sentences.zh: 明年，出為晉安王子勛鎮軍長史、尋陽內史，行江州事。

translations.literal: The following year he was sent out as Chief Clerk to the Pacifying Army under Prince of Jin'an Zixun, Interior Administrator of Xunyang, and acting administrator of Jiang Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out to serve Prince of Jin'an Zixun as chief clerk to the Pacifying Army, as Interior Administrator of Xunyang, and as acting administrator of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝狂悖無道，以太祖、世祖並第數居三以登極位，子勛次第既同，深構嫌隙，因何邁之謀，乃遣使齎藥賜子勛死。

translations.literal: The Deposed Former Emperor was violent and lawless; because both the Founding Emperor and Emperor Shizu had been third in birth order among brothers when they ascended the throne, and Zixun's place in the succession was the same, he deeply nursed suspicion and, following He Mai's counsel, sent an envoy bearing poison to command Zixun's death.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed former emperor was violent and lawless. Because both the founding emperor and Emperor Shizu had been third among brothers in birth order when they ascended the throne, and Zixun stood in the same place in the succession, the emperor deeply nursed suspicion; following He Mai's counsel, he sent an envoy bearing poison to command Zixun's death.

sentences.zh: 使至，子勛典籤謝道遇、齋帥潘欣之、侍書褚靈嗣等馳以告琬，泣涕請計。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, Zixun's chief clerk Xie Daoyu, quartermaster Pan Xinzhi, attendant scribe Chu Lingsi, and others galloped to inform Wan, weeping and begging for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, Zixun's chief clerk Xie Daoyu, quartermaster Pan Xinzhi, attendant scribe Chu Lingsi, and others galloped to inform Wan, weeping as they begged him for a plan.

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「身南土寒士，蒙先殊恩，以愛子見託，豈得惜門戶百口，其當以死報效。

translations.literal: Wan said: 'I am a humble scholar from the southern lands who received extraordinary favor from the late emperor and was entrusted with his beloved son—how could I spare the hundred mouths of my household? I must repay this trust with my life.'
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, 'I am a humble scholar from the south who received extraordinary favor from the late emperor and was entrusted with his beloved son. How could I spare the hundred lives of my household? I must repay this trust with my life.'

sentences.zh: 幼主昏暴，社稷危殆，雖曰天子，事猶獨夫。

translations.literal: The young ruler is benighted and cruel, and the altars of state are in peril; though he is called Son of Heaven, in truth he is a lone tyrant.
translations.idiomatic: The young ruler is benighted and cruel, and the altars of state are in peril. Though he is called Son of Heaven, in truth he is nothing but a lone tyrant.

sentences.zh: 今便指率文武，直造京邑，與群公卿士，廢昏立明。

translations.literal: I shall now lead the civil and military officials straight to the capital to join the assembled lords and ministers in deposing the benighted and establishing the enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: I shall now lead the civil and military officials straight to the capital to join the assembled lords and ministers in deposing the benighted ruler and establishing a worthy one.

sentences.zh: 」景和元年十一月十九日，稱子勛教，即日戒嚴。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jinghe, acting on an order in Zixun's name, martial law was proclaimed that same day.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jinghe, acting on an order issued in Zixun's name, martial law was proclaimed that same day.

sentences.zh: 子勛戎服出聽事，集僚佐，使潘欣之口宣旨曰：「少主昏狂悖戾，並是諸君所見聞。

translations.literal: Zixun came out to the audience hall in military dress, assembled his staff, and had Pan Xinzhi orally proclaim the decree: 'The young ruler's madness, violence, and perversity are all matters you yourselves have witnessed.'
translations.idiomatic: Zixun came out to the audience hall in military dress, assembled his staff, and had Pan Xinzhi orally proclaim the decree: 'The young ruler's madness, violence, and perversity are all matters you yourselves have witnessed.'

sentences.zh: 顧命重臣，悉皆誅戮。

translations.literal: The great ministers entrusted at the deathbed have all been put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers entrusted at the deathbed have all been put to death.

sentences.zh: 驅逼王公，幽辱太后。

translations.literal: He has driven and coerced the imperial princes and humiliated the empress dowager in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: He has driven and coerced the imperial princes and humiliated the empress dowager by keeping her in confinement.

sentences.zh: 不逞之徒，共成其釁。

translations.literal: Lawless men have together brought about these offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Lawless men have together brought about these offenses.

sentences.zh: 京師諸王，並見囚逼，委厄虎口，思奮莫因。

translations.literal: The princes in the capital have all been imprisoned and coerced, cast into the tiger's maw with no means to strike back though they yearn to do so.
translations.idiomatic: The princes in the capital have all been imprisoned and coerced, cast into the tiger's maw with no means to strike back though they yearn to do so.

sentences.zh: 身義兼家國，豈可坐視橫流！

translations.literal: My duty embraces both family and state—how can I sit by and watch the flood sweep all away!
translations.idiomatic: My duty embraces both family and state—how can I sit by and watch the flood sweep all away!

sentences.zh: 今便欲舉九江之眾，馳檄近遠，以謀王室。

translations.literal: I now intend to raise the forces of Jiujiang, dispatch proclamations near and far, and act for the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: I now intend to raise the forces of Jiujiang, dispatch proclamations near and far, and act on behalf of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 於諸君何如？

translations.literal: What do you gentlemen think of this?'
translations.idiomatic: What do you gentlemen think of this?'

sentences.zh: 」四座未答，錄事參軍陶亮曰：「少主昏狂，醜毒已積。

translations.literal: No one in the four quarters answered; Recording Officer and Staff Officer Tao Liang said: 'The young ruler is benighted and violent, and his wickedness has long been accumulating.'
translations.idiomatic: No one in the hall answered at first; then Recording Officer and Staff Officer Tao Liang said, 'The young ruler is benighted and violent, and his wickedness has long been accumulating.'

sentences.zh: 伊、霍行之於古，殿下當之於今。

translations.literal: Yi Yin and Huo Guang acted thus in antiquity; Your Highness should do the same today.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin and Huo Guang acted thus in antiquity; Your Highness should do the same today.'

sentences.zh: 鄙州士子，世習忠節，況屬千載之會，請效死前驅。

translations.literal: The gentlemen of this humble province have for generations practiced loyalty and integrity; moreover, this is an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years—I beg to give my life as vanguard.'
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of this province have for generations practiced loyalty and integrity; moreover, this is an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. I beg to give my life as vanguard.'

sentences.zh: 」眾並奉旨。

translations.literal: All accepted the decree.
translations.idiomatic: All accepted the decree.

sentences.zh: 文武普進位一階。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials were all advanced one rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military officials were all advanced one rank in office.

sentences.zh: 轉亮為諮議參軍事，領中兵，加寧朔將軍，揔統軍事。

translations.literal: Liang was transferred to be Advisory Staff Officer, placed in charge of the central guard, promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, and given overall command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was transferred to advisory staff officer, placed in charge of the central guard, promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, and given overall command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 功曹張沈為諮議參軍，統作舟艦。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhang Shen was made Advisory Staff Officer and put in overall charge of building ships.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhang Shen was made advisory staff officer and put in overall charge of building ships.

sentences.zh: 參軍事顧昭之、沈伯玉、荀道林等參管書記。

translations.literal: Staff Officers Gu Zhaozhi, Shen Boyu, Xun Daolin, and others assisted in managing documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers Gu Zhaozhi, Shen Boyu, Xun Daolin, and others assisted in managing documents and records.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守沈懷寶、岷山太守薛常寶之郡，始至尋陽，與新蔡太守韋希直並為諮議參軍，領中兵，及彭澤令陳紹宗並為將帥。

translations.literal: The Administrators of Nanyang Shen Huaibao and of Minshan Xue Changbao were on their way to their posts when they first reached Xunyang; together with the Administrator of Xincai Wei Xizhi they were all made Advisory Staff Officers in charge of the central guard, and together with the Magistrate of Pengze Chen Shaozong they were appointed generals.
translations.idiomatic: The administrators of Nanyang, Shen Huaibao, and of Minshan, Xue Changbao, were on their way to their posts when they first reached Xunyang; together with the administrator of Xincai, Wei Xizhi, they were all made advisory staff officers in charge of the central guard, and together with the magistrate of Pengze, Chen Shaozong, they were appointed generals.

sentences.zh: 初，廢帝使荊州錄送前軍長史、荊州行事張悅下至盆口，琬稱子勛命，釋其桎梏，迎以所乘之車，以為司馬，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Deposed Emperor had ordered Jing Province to escort downriver the former Chief Clerk of the Vanguard Army and Acting Administrator of Jing Province Zhang Yue as far as Pankou; Wan, acting in Zixun's name, released him from his fetters, received him in the carriage he himself rode, and appointed him Marshal, with the additional title General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the deposed emperor had ordered Jing Province to escort downriver the former chief clerk of the vanguard army and acting administrator of Jing Province, Zhang Yue, as far as Pankou. Acting in Zixun's name, Wan released him from his fetters, received him in his own carriage, and appointed him marshal with the additional title General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 加琬冠軍將軍，二人共掌內外眾事。

translations.literal: Wan was promoted to General Who Conquers Champions; the two men together controlled all affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was promoted to General Who Conquers Champions, and the two men together controlled all affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍俞伯奇率五百人出斷大雷，禁絕商旅，及公私使命。

translations.literal: He sent General Yu Boqi with five hundred men to go out and cut off Dalei, forbidding merchants and travelers as well as public and private missions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Yu Boqi with five hundred men to cut off Dalei, forbidding merchants, travelers, and both public and private missions.

sentences.zh: 遣使上諸郡民丁，收斂器械。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to the various commanderies to levy militia and gather weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to the various commanderies to levy militia and gather weapons.

sentences.zh: 十日之內，得甲士五千人，出頓大雷，於兩岸築壘。

translations.literal: Within ten days he obtained five thousand armored soldiers, marched out and encamped at Dalei, and built fortifications on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he obtained five thousand armored soldiers, marched out and encamped at Dalei, and built fortifications on both banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 巴東、建平二郡太守孫沖之之郡，始至孤石，琬以沖之為子勛諮議參軍，領中兵，加輔國將軍，與陶亮並統前軍。

translations.literal: The Administrators of the two commanderies Badong and Jianping, Sun Chongzhi, were on their way to their posts and had just reached Gushi when Wan made Chongzhi Zixun's Advisory Staff Officer in charge of the central guard, with the additional title General Who Assists the State, and together with Tao Liang he was given joint command of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The administrators of the two commanderies Badong and Jianping, Sun Chongzhi, were on their way to their posts and had just reached Gushi when Wan made Chongzhi Zixun's advisory staff officer in charge of the central guard, with the additional title General Who Assists the State, and together with Tao Liang gave him joint command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 使記室參軍荀道林造檄文，馳告遠近。

translations.literal: He had Recording Officer and Staff Officer Xun Daolin draft a proclamation and dispatch it swiftly to inform the near and far.
translations.idiomatic: He had recording officer and staff officer Xun Daolin draft a proclamation and dispatch it swiftly to inform regions near and far.

sentences.zh: 會太宗定亂，進子勛號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong settled the turmoil, Zixun was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the privilege of an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong settled the turmoil, Zixun was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and granted an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 令書至，諸佐吏並喜，造琬曰：「暴亂既除，殿下又開黃閣，實為公私大慶。

translations.literal: When the order arrived, all the staff officers rejoiced and came to Wan saying: 'The violent disorder has been removed, and Your Highness has also been granted the Yellow Gate—this is truly a great celebration for public and private alike.'
translations.idiomatic: When the order arrived, all the staff officers rejoiced and came to Wan, saying, 'The violent disorder has been removed, and Your Highness has also been granted the Yellow Gate. This is truly a great celebration for public and private alike.'

sentences.zh: 」琬以子勛次第居三，又以尋陽起事，有符世祖，理必萬克。

translations.literal: Wan considered that Zixun's place in the succession was third, and that he had raised arms at Xunyang, matching Emperor Shizu—victory was logically certain.
translations.idiomatic: Wan reasoned that Zixun stood third in the order of succession and had raised arms at Xunyang, matching Emperor Shizu's own precedent—victory was logically certain.

sentences.zh: 乃取令書投地曰：「殿下當開端門，黃閣是吾徒事耳！

translations.literal: He then took the order and cast it to the ground, saying: 'Your Highness should open the Duan Gate—the Yellow Gate is a matter for petty men like us!'
translations.idiomatic: He then took the order and cast it to the ground, saying, 'Your Highness should open the Duan Gate—the Yellow Gate is a matter for petty men like us!'

sentences.zh: 」眾並駭愕。

translations.literal: All were struck with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: All were struck with alarm.

sentences.zh: 琬與陶亮等繕治器甲，徵兵四方。

translations.literal: Wan, Tao Liang, and the others repaired weapons and armor and levied troops from all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, Tao Liang, and the others repaired weapons and armor and levied troops from all directions.

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史安陸王子綏、荊州刺史臨海王子頊、會稽太守尋陽王子房、雍州刺史袁顗、梁州刺史柳元怙、益州刺史蕭惠開、廣州刺史袁曇遠、徐州刺史薛安都、青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固、湘州行事何慧文、吳郡太守顧琛、吳興太守王曇生、晉陵太守袁標、義興太守劉延熙並同叛逆。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Ying Province Prince of Anlu Zisui, the Inspector of Jing Province Prince of Linhai Zishang, the Administrator of Kuaiji Prince of Xunyang Zifang, the Inspector of Yong Province Yuan Yi, the Inspector of Liang Province Liu Yuanhu, the Inspector of Yi Province Xiao Huaikai, the Inspector of Guang Province Yuan Tanyuan, the Inspector of Xu Province Xue Andu, the Inspector of Qing Province Shen Wenxiu, the Inspector of Ji Province Cui Daogu, the Acting Administrator of Xiang Province He Huiwen, and the Administrators of Wu Commandery Gu Chen, Wuxing Wang Tansheng, Jinling Yuan Biao, and Yixing Liu Yanxi all rebelled together.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Ying Province, Prince of Anlu Zisui; the inspector of Jing Province, Prince of Linhai Zishang; the administrator of Kuaiji, Prince of Xunyang Zifang; the inspector of Yong Province, Yuan Yi; the inspector of Liang Province, Liu Yuanhu; the inspector of Yi Province, Xiao Huaikai; the inspector of Guang Province, Yuan Tanyuan; the inspector of Xu Province, Xue Andu; the inspector of Qing Province, Shen Wenxiu; the inspector of Ji Province, Cui Daogu; the acting administrator of Xiang Province, He Huiwen; and the administrators of Wu, Wuxing, Jinling, and Yixing—Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and Liu Yanxi—all rebelled together.

sentences.zh: 先是，廢帝以邵陵王子元為冠軍將軍、湘州刺史，中兵參軍沈仲玉為道路行事。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Deposed Emperor had appointed Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan General Who Conquers Champions and Inspector of Xiang Province, with Central Guard Staff Officer Shen Zhongyu as Acting Administrator on the route.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the deposed emperor had appointed Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan General Who Conquers Champions and inspector of Xiang Province, with central guard staff officer Shen Zhongyu as acting administrator on the route.

sentences.zh: 至鵲頭，聞尋陽兵起，停住，白太宗進止之宜。

translations.literal: When he reached Quetou he heard that troops had risen at Xunyang, halted, and reported to Emperor Taizong what course should be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Quetou he heard that troops had risen at Xunyang, halted, and reported to Emperor Taizong what course should be taken.

sentences.zh: 太宗以子勛起兵，本在幼主，雖疑其不即解甲，不欲先彰同異，敕令進道。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong held that Zixun's raising of arms was fundamentally directed at the young ruler; though he suspected that he would not immediately lay down his arms, he did not wish to reveal division first and ordered him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong held that Zixun's raising of arms was fundamentally directed at the young ruler; though he suspected that Zixun would not immediately lay down his arms, he did not wish to reveal division first and ordered him to advance.

sentences.zh: 信未報，琬聞子元停鵲頭不進，遣數百人劫迎之。

translations.literal: Before a reply arrived, Wan heard that Ziyuan had halted at Quetou and would not advance, and sent several hundred men to seize and welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Before a reply arrived, Wan heard that Ziyuan had halted at Quetou and would not advance, and sent several hundred men to seize him and bring him in.

sentences.zh: 乃建牙於桑尾，傳檄京師曰：

translations.literal: He then raised his standard at Sangwei and transmitted a proclamation to the capital, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then raised his standard at Sangwei and transmitted a proclamation to the capital, saying:

sentences.zh: 陽六數艱，雲雷相襲。

translations.literal: The yang sixth brings repeated hardship; cloud and thunder follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The yang sixth brings repeated hardship; cloud and thunder follow in succession.

sentences.zh: 高皇受曆，時乘雲轡，頓於促路。

translations.literal: The High Emperor received the mandate of Heaven and for a time grasped the reins of cloud, yet was halted on a narrow path.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor received the mandate of Heaven and for a time grasped the reins of cloud, yet was halted on a narrow path.

sentences.zh: 文祖定祥，係昭睿化，翦於中年。

translations.literal: The Civil Ancestor fixed auspicious signs and bound himself to enlightened transformation, yet was cut down in midlife.
translations.idiomatic: The Civil Ancestor fixed auspicious signs and bound himself to enlightened transformation, yet was cut down in midlife.

sentences.zh: 二凶縱禍，三綱理滅，宗王俯首，姑息逆朝，枕戈無聞，偷榮有秩。

translations.literal: Two villains unleashed calamity and the three bonds of moral order were extinguished; the imperial princes bowed their heads, indulging the rebellious court, unheard though they slept upon their spears, yet still enjoying rank through stolen glory.
translations.idiomatic: Two villains unleashed calamity and the three bonds of moral order were extinguished. The imperial princes bowed their heads, indulging the rebellious court: unheard though they slept upon their spears, they still enjoyed rank through stolen glory.

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝釋位泣血，糾義入討，投袂戎首，親戮鯨鯢，九服還輝，兩儀更造。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu relinquished his place and wept blood, rallied righteousness and marched to punish the rebels, flung aside his sleeves at the head of the army, and personally slew the great monsters; the nine domains regained their radiance and heaven and earth were remade.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu relinquished his place and wept blood, rallied the righteous cause and marched to punish the rebels, flung aside his sleeves at the head of the army, and personally slew the great monsters. The nine domains regained their radiance and heaven and earth were remade.

sentences.zh: 而穹旻不惠，棄離萬國，皇運重替，嗣王荒淫。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven was unkind, abandoning the myriad states; the imperial fortune turned once more, and the successor king was dissolute and licentious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven was unkind and abandoned the myriad states. The imperial fortune turned once more, and the successor king was dissolute and licentious.

sentences.zh: 孤以不才，任居藩長，大懼宗稷，殲覆待日。

translations.literal: I, lacking talent, bear the weight of a princely establishment and greatly fear that the altars of state will be destroyed any day.
translations.idiomatic: I, lacking talent, bear the weight of a princely establishment and greatly fear that the altars of state may be destroyed any day.

sentences.zh: 故招徒楚郢，飛檄京甸，志遵前典，黜幽陟明，庶七廟復安，海昏有紹。

translations.literal: Therefore I have gathered followers in Chu and Ying, dispatched swift proclamations to the capital region, and intend, following the ancient precedents, to depose the benighted and elevate the enlightened, so that the seven temples may be restored to peace and the line of Haihun may have a successor.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have gathered followers in Chu and Ying and dispatched swift proclamations to the capital region, intending, following ancient precedent, to depose the benighted and elevate the enlightened so that the seven temples may be restored to peace and the royal line may have a worthy successor.

sentences.zh: 豈圖宋未悔禍，弑亂奄臻，遂矯害明茂，篡竊天寶，反道效尤，蔑我皇德，干我昭穆，寡我兄弟，恣鴟鴞之心，蹈倫、穎之志，覆移鼎祚，誣罔天人。

translations.literal: Who could have thought that Song would not repent of its calamity, that regicide and disorder would suddenly arrive, that they would then falsely harm the bright and flourishing, usurp the heavenly treasure, turn against the Way and imitate past crimes, despise our imperial virtue, violate our ancestral temples, leave our brothers few, indulge the heart of the owl, follow the ambitions of Lun and Ying, overturn the sacred vessel of state, and deceive both Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have thought that Song would not repent of its calamity, that regicide and disorder would suddenly arrive, that they would falsely harm the bright and flourishing, usurp the heavenly mandate, turn against the Way and imitate past crimes, despise our imperial virtue, violate our ancestral temples, leave our brothers few, indulge the heart of the owl, follow the ambitions of Lun and Ying, overturn the sacred vessel of state, and deceive both Heaven and man.

sentences.zh: 藐孤同氣，猶有十三，聖靈何辜，而當乏饗。

translations.literal: Though they hold me in contempt, among those of the same breath there are still thirteen; what crime have the sacred spirits committed that they should lack offerings?
translations.idiomatic: Though they hold me in contempt, among my brothers of the same breath there are still thirteen. What crime have the sacred spirits committed that they should lack offerings?

sentences.zh: 昔隆周弛御，晉、鄭是依；

translations.literal: In former times when prosperous Zhou relaxed its rule, it relied upon Jin and Zheng;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when prosperous Zhou relaxed its rule, it relied upon Jin and Zheng;

sentences.zh: 盛漢中陵，居、章抗節。

translations.literal: when flourishing Han suffered mid-dynasty decline, Ju and Zhang upheld their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: when flourishing Han suffered mid-dynasty decline, Ju and Zhang upheld their integrity.

sentences.zh: 支苗輕屬，猶或忘驅，況孤忝惟臣子，情地兼切，號感一隅，心與事痛。

translations.literal: Even distant branches and minor kin sometimes forgot themselves in service—how much more, as I am unworthy yet still a subject and son, with feeling and position both urgent, crying out in one corner while my heart and the matter alike are in pain.
translations.idiomatic: Even distant branches and minor kin sometimes forgot themselves in service—how much more so I, unworthy though I am, yet still subject and son, with feeling and duty both urgent, crying out in one corner while my heart and the matter alike are in pain.

sentences.zh: 是用飲血衽金，誓復宗祀。

translations.literal: Therefore I have drunk blood upon the mat and grasped the golden blade, swearing to restore the ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have drunk blood upon the mat and grasped the golden blade, swearing to restore the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 今遣輔國將軍諮議領中直兵孫沖之、龍驤將軍陳紹宗，率螭虎之士，組甲二萬，沿流電發，逕取白下。

translations.literal: I now send Advisory Staff Officer to the General Who Assists the State and Commander of the Central Guard Sun Chongzhi and General of the Flying Dragon Chen Shaozong, leading dragon-and-tiger warriors, twenty thousand in linked armor, to strike like lightning along the river and take Baixia directly.
translations.idiomatic: I now send advisory staff officer to the General Who Assists the State and commander of the central guard Sun Chongzhi and General of the Flying Dragon Chen Shaozong, leading dragon-and-tiger warriors—twenty thousand in linked armor—to strike like lightning along the river and take Baixia directly.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍領中直兵薛常寶、建威將軍領中直兵沈懷寶，長戟萬刃，羽騎千群，徑出南州，直造朱雀。

translations.literal: General of the Flying Dragon and Commander of the Central Guard Xue Changbao and General Who Establishes Might and Commander of the Central Guard Shen Huaibao, with ten thousand long halberds and a thousand companies of feathered cavalry, will march straight out of the southern provinces and advance directly upon Zhuque.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Flying Dragon and commander of the central guard Xue Changbao and General Who Establishes Might and commander of the central guard Shen Huaibao, with ten thousand long halberds and a thousand companies of feathered cavalry, will march straight out of the southern provinces and advance directly upon Zhuque Gate.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍諮議領中直兵陶亮、龍驤將軍焦度，揔中黃之旅，梟雄三萬，風掩江介，雲臨石頭。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North, Advisory Staff Officer, and Commander of the Central Guard Tao Liang and General of the Flying Dragon Jiao Du, commanding thirty thousand fierce warriors of the central yellow guard, will sweep the river lands like wind and come upon Stone City like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North, advisory staff officer, and commander of the central guard Tao Liang and General of the Flying Dragon Jiao Du, commanding thirty thousand fierce warriors of the central yellow guard, will sweep the river lands like wind and come upon Stone City like clouds.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍張冽，龍驤將軍何休明，提育、獲之徒，勁悍之卒，邪趨金陵，北指閶闔。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might Zhang Lie and General of the Flying Dragon He Xiuming, leading warriors of the Yu and Huo type and fierce, hardy troops, will strike obliquely toward Jinling and point north toward the Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Might Zhang Lie and General of the Flying Dragon He Xiuming, leading warriors of the Yu and Huo type and fierce, hardy troops, will strike obliquely toward Jinling and point north toward the Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍張係伯、龍驤將軍陳慶，勒輕銳五千，強弩一萬，飛鋒班瀆，齊會西明。

translations.literal: Generals of the Flying Dragon Zhang Xibo and Chen Qing will muster five thousand light elite troops and ten thousand strong crossbowmen, their flying vanguard spreading along the waterways, and assemble together at Ximing.
translations.idiomatic: Generals of the Flying Dragon Zhang Xibo and Chen Qing will muster five thousand light elite troops and ten thousand strong crossbowmen, their flying vanguard spreading along the waterways, and assemble together at Ximing.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、尋陽內史鄧琬，撮湘、雍之兵，勇敢四萬，授律緫威，飆集京邑。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Interior Administrator of Xunyang Deng Wan, gathering the forces of Xiang and Yong, forty thousand brave men, will receive the battle law and gather authority, sweeping like a gale upon the capital.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions and interior administrator of Xunyang Deng Wan, gathering the forces of Xiang and Yong—forty thousand brave men—will receive the battle law and gather authority, sweeping like a gale upon the capital.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍、領府司馬張悅，蒼兕千艘，水軍五萬，大董群校，絡繹繼道。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Acting Marshal of the Establishment Zhang Yue, with a thousand blue-ox ships and fifty thousand naval troops, will greatly oversee the commanders, their columns following one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the Barbarians and acting marshal of the establishment Zhang Yue, with a thousand blue-ox ships and fifty thousand naval troops, will greatly oversee the commanders, their columns following one after another along the road.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、豫章內史劉衍、寧朔將軍、武昌太守劉弼、寧朔將軍、西陽太守謝稚、建威將軍、領中直兵、晉熙太守閻湛之，皆掃境勝兵，薦誠請效。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Interior Administrator of Yuzhang Liu Yan, General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Wuchang Liu Bi, General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Xiyang Xie Zhi, and General Who Establishes Might, Commander of the Central Guard, and Administrator of Jinxi Yan Zhanzhi have all swept their territories for victorious troops and offered their loyalty, begging to serve.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions and interior administrator of Yuzhang Liu Yan, General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Wuchang Liu Bi, General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Xiyang Xie Zhi, and General Who Establishes Might, commander of the central guard, and administrator of Jinxi Yan Zhanzhi have all swept their territories for victorious troops and offered their loyalty, begging to serve.

sentences.zh: 後將軍、郢州刺史安陸王子綏懷恩纏慕，鞠旅先辰。

translations.literal: Rear General and Inspector of Ying Province Prince of Anlu Zisui, cherishing grace and bound by longing, has mustered his troops ahead of the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General and inspector of Ying Province, Prince of Anlu Zisui, cherishing grace and bound by longing, has mustered his troops ahead of the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、湘州刺史邵陵王子元席颿陵波，整眾遄至。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Inspector of Xiang Province Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan, spreading sails across the waves, has assembled his forces and hastened to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions and inspector of Xiang Province, Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan, spreading sails across the waves, has assembled his forces and hastened to arrive.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、荊州刺史臨海王子頊練甲陝西，獻徒萬數。

translations.literal: Vanguard General and Inspector of Jing Province Prince of Linhai Zishang has drilled armor west of the passes and presented troops in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard General and inspector of Jing Province, Prince of Linhai Zishang, has drilled armor west of the passes and presented troops in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍、冠軍長史、長沙內史何惠文，見拔先皇，誠深投袂。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State, Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers Champions, and Interior Administrator of Changsha He Huiwen, raised up by the late emperor, has shown deep loyalty by flinging aside his sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the State, chief clerk to the General Who Conquers Champions, and interior administrator of Changsha, He Huiwen, raised up by the late emperor, has shown deep loyalty by flinging aside his sleeves.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、雍州刺史袁顗，不謀同契，雷發漢南。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Inspector of Yong Province Yuan Yi, without prior counsel yet of one accord, has thundered forth from south of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions and inspector of Yong Province Yuan Yi, without prior counsel yet of one accord, has thundered forth from south of the Han.

sentences.zh: 建武將軍、順陽太守劉道憲，懷忠抱慨，不遠三千。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Martial Power and Administrator of Shunyang Liu Daoxian, cherishing loyalty and embracing indignation, has come from no less than three thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Martial Power and administrator of Shunyang Liu Daoxian, cherishing loyalty and embracing indignation, has come from no less than three thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 梁、益、青、徐、兗、豫、吳、會，皆密介歸誠，誓為表裏。

translations.literal: Liang, Yi, Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Wu, and Kuaiji have all secretly pledged their loyalty and sworn to be inner and outer support alike.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, Yi, Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Wu, and Kuaiji have all secretly pledged their loyalty and sworn to be inner and outer support alike.

sentences.zh: 孤親緫烝徒，十有餘萬，白羽咽川，霜鋒照野，金聲振谷，鳴鼙聒天。

translations.literal: I myself shall command the massed hosts, more than a hundred thousand strong; white feather arrows choke the rivers, frosted blades light the fields, golden clamor shakes the valleys, and beating drums deafen the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: I myself shall command the massed hosts, more than a hundred thousand strong: white feather arrows choke the rivers, frosted blades light the fields, golden clamor shakes the valleys, and beating drums deafen the heavens.

sentences.zh: 凡諸將帥，皆忠無匿情，智無遺計，果幹剛鷙，譎略多奇。

translations.literal: All the generals and commanders are loyal without hidden feelings, wise without plans left unused, resolute, capable, fierce, and cunning in strategy and rich in stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals and commanders are loyal without hidden feelings, wise without plans left unused, resolute, capable, fierce, and rich in cunning strategy and stratagems.

sentences.zh: 水陸長驅，數道並進，發舟踰險，背水爭先。

translations.literal: By land and water they will drive far, advancing on several routes at once, launching boats over perilous waters and contending for the front with rivers at their backs.
translations.idiomatic: By land and water they will drive far, advancing on several routes at once, launching boats over perilous waters and contending for the front with rivers at their backs.

sentences.zh: 以此眾戰，孰能斯禦，推此義銳，滄海可垔。

translations.literal: With such a host to fight, who could withstand it? Push this righteous sharpness forward, and even the blue sea could be dammed.
translations.idiomatic: With such a host to fight, who could withstand it? Push this righteous sharpness forward, and even the blue sea could be dammed.

sentences.zh: 諸君或荷寵前朝，感恩舊日；

translations.literal: You gentlemen have either received favor under the former dynasty and feel gratitude for old days,
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen have either received favor under the former dynasty and feel gratitude for old days,

sentences.zh: 或弈世貞淳，見危授命。

translations.literal: or for generations have practiced steadfast purity and would give your lives when danger appears.
translations.idiomatic: or for generations have practiced steadfast purity and would give your lives when danger appears.

sentences.zh: 而逼迫寇手，效節莫由。

translations.literal: Yet you are coerced by the enemy's hand and have no means to prove your loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are coerced by the enemy's hand and have no means to prove your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今大軍密邇，形援已接，見幾而作，豈俟終日！

translations.literal: Now the great army draws near in secret, and visible support is already at hand—act when you see the moment; why wait for the day to end!
translations.idiomatic: Now the great army draws near in secret, and visible support is already at hand. Act when you see the moment—why wait for the day to end!

sentences.zh: 便宜轉禍趣福，因變立功。

translations.literal: It is fitting to turn calamity toward blessing and, seizing the change, establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to turn calamity toward blessing and, seizing the change, establish merit.

sentences.zh: 夫旦、奭與三監並時，金、霍與上官共主，邪正粈雜，何世無之！

translations.literal: Dan and Shi existed at the same time as the Three Overseers; Jin Ri and Huo Guang shared rule with Shangguan—crooked and straight have always been mixed; what age has lacked this!
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Shi existed at the same time as the Three Overseers; Jin Ri and Huo Guang shared rule with Shangguan. Crooked and straight have always been mixed—what age has lacked this!

sentences.zh: 但績亮則名播，姦騁則道消耳。

translations.literal: Only when merit is bright does fame spread; when treachery runs rampant, the Way is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Only when merit is bright does fame spread; when treachery runs rampant, the Way is extinguished.

sentences.zh: 紀季入齊，陳平歸漢，身尊譽遠，明誓是裒，成範全規，殷監匪遠。

translations.literal: Ji Ji entered Qi and Chen Ping returned to Han; their persons were honored and their fame reached far. Bright oaths gather such men—complete models and full standards; the stern lesson of Yin is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ji entered Qi and Chen Ping returned to Han; their persons were honored and their fame reached far. Bright oaths gather such men—complete models and full standards. The stern lesson of Yin is not far off.

sentences.zh: 若玩咎惟休，告舍罔悟，則誅及五族，有殄無遺。

translations.literal: If you treat calamity as rest and heed no warning nor counsel, then punishment will reach the five kindreds and none will be left alive.
translations.idiomatic: If you treat calamity as rest and heed no warning nor counsel, then punishment will reach the five kindreds and none will be left alive.

sentences.zh: 軍科爵賞，信如皦日，巫山既燎，芝艾共煙，幸遵良塗，無守毀轍。

translations.literal: Military discipline, ranks, and rewards—faith bright as the noonday sun; once Mount Wu is burned, mugwort and artemisia share the same smoke; I hope you will follow the good road and not cling to a ruined track.
translations.idiomatic: Military discipline and the granting of ranks and rewards are as trustworthy as the bright noonday sun. When Mount Wu burns, mugwort and artemisia rise in the same smoke. I urge you to take the right path and not hold to a course already ruined.

sentences.zh: 檄到宣告，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: When this proclamation arrives, let all hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: When this proclamation reaches you, let everyone hear and know it.

sentences.zh: 購太宗萬戶侯，布絹二萬匹，金銀五百斤，其餘各有差。

translations.literal: A bounty for Taizong: marquisate of ten thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of cloth and silk, five hundred jin of gold and silver; the rest at graded rewards.
translations.idiomatic: A reward was posted for Taizong: the rank of marquis of ten thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred jin of gold and silver; other rewards were set at varying levels.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣荊州典籤邵宰乘驛還江陵，經過襄陽，袁顗馳書報琬，勸勿解甲，并奉表勸子勛即位。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Jingzhou Registrar Shao Zai by express relay back to Jiangling; passing through Xiangyang, Yuan Yi sent urgent letter reporting to Wan, urging not to lay down arms, and jointly submitted a memorial urging Zi Xun to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent the Jingzhou registrar Shao Zai back to Jiangling by express relay. When he passed through Xiangyang, Yuan Yi sent an urgent letter to Wan urging him not to disarm, and together they submitted a memorial recommending that Zi Xun take the throne.

sentences.zh: 郢州承子勛初檄，及聞太宗定大事，即解甲下標。

translations.literal: Yingzhou, upon receiving Zi Xun's initial proclamation, and upon hearing Taizong had settled the great affair, immediately laid down arms and lowered its banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Province had received Zi Xun's first proclamation, but when it heard that Taizong had secured the succession, it at once disarmed and lowered its standards.

sentences.zh: 繼聞尋陽不息，而顗又響應，郢府行事錄事參軍荀卞之大懼，慮為琬所咎責，即遣諮議領中兵參軍鄭景玄率軍馳下，并送軍糧。

translations.literal: Then hearing Xunyang had not ceased, and Yuan Yi had also responded, Ying prefecture acting Registrar Xun Bianzhi was greatly afraid, fearing blame from Wan, and immediately sent Consultation Leader and Central Troops Commander Zheng Jingxuan to lead troops south in haste, also sending military grain.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the rebellion at Xunyang had not ended and Yuan Yi had joined in, Xun Bianzhi, the acting registrar of Ying Prefecture, was terrified of being blamed by Wan. He immediately sent Zheng Jingxuan, consultation leader and commander of central troops, to march south at speed, along with military provisions.

sentences.zh: 琬乃稱說符瑞，造乘輿御服，云松滋縣生豹自來，柴桑縣送竹有「來奉天子」字，又云青龍見東淮，白鹿出西岡。

translations.literal: Wan then proclaimed auspicious omens, made imperial carriage and regalia, saying a leopard born in Songzi came of itself, bamboo sent from Chaishang bore the characters "come to serve the Son of Heaven," and also saying an azure dragon appeared in Eastern Huai and a white deer emerged from the western hill.
translations.idiomatic: Wan then proclaimed auspicious signs and had an imperial carriage and regalia made. He claimed that a leopard born in Songzi had come of its own accord, that bamboo sent from Chaishang bore the words "come to serve the Son of Heaven," and that an azure dragon had appeared in eastern Huai and a white deer on the western hills.

sentences.zh: 令顧昭之撰為《瑞命記》。

translations.literal: He ordered Gu Zhaozhi to compile it as Record of the Auspicious Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He had Gu Zhaozhi compile a work entitled Record of the Auspicious Mandate.

sentences.zh: 立宗廟，設壇埸，矯作崇憲太后璽，令群僚上偽號於子勛。

translations.literal: He established an ancestral temple, set up an altar, forged the seal of Empress Dowager Chongxian, and ordered the officials to submit a false title to Zi Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He established an ancestral temple and set up an altar, forged the seal of Empress Dowager Chongxian, and ordered his officials to present a false imperial title to Zi Xun.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月七日，即位於尋陽城，改景和二年為義嘉元年。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the second year of Taishi, he took the throne at Xunyang city, changing the second year of Jinghe to the first year of Yijia.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the first month of the second year of Taishi, he was enthroned at Xunyang. The second year of Jinghe was renamed the first year of Yijia.

sentences.zh: 以安陸王子綏為司徒、驃騎將軍、揚州刺史，尋陽王子房車騎將軍，臨海王子頊衛將軍，並開府儀同三司，邵陵王子元撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Anlu Prince Zi Shou as Minister of Works, Cavalry General-in-Chief, and Yangzhou inspector; Xunyang Prince Zi Fang as Chariots General; Linhai Prince Zi Xiang as Guards General—all with offices equal to the Three Excellencies; and Shaoling Prince Zi Yuan as General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Prince Zi Shou of Anlu as Minister of Works, Cavalry General-in-Chief, and inspector of Yangzhou; Prince Zi Fang of Xunyang as Chariots General; and Prince Zi Xiang of Linhai as Guards General—all with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies. Prince Zi Yuan of Shaoling was made General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 其日雲雨晦合，行禮忘稱萬歲。

translations.literal: That day clouds and rain were dark and merged; in performing the rites they forgot to shout "ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky was dark with rain, and during the ceremony they forgot to shout "Long may he live!"

sentences.zh: 取子勛所乘車，除腳以為輦，置偽殿之西。

translations.literal: They took the carriage Zi Xun had ridden, removed its footboard to make a palanquin, and placed it west of the false hall.
translations.idiomatic: They took the carriage Zi Xun had used, removed its footboard to make a palanquin, and set it up west of the mock palace hall.

sentences.zh: 其夕，有鳩棲其中，鴞鳥集其幰；

translations.literal: That evening a dove roosted in it, and owls gathered on its canopy;
translations.idiomatic: That evening a dove roosted inside it, and owls gathered on its canopy;

sentences.zh: 又有禿鶖集城上。

translations.literal: there were also bald vultures perched on the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: bald vultures also perched atop the city wall.

sentences.zh: 子綏拜司徒日，雷電晦冥，震其黃閣柱，鴟尾墮地；

translations.literal: On the day Zi Shou received the Minister of Works, thunder and lightning in gloom struck his yellow gate pillars, and the owl-tail ornament fell to the ground;
translations.idiomatic: On the day Zi Shou was appointed Minister of Works, thunder and lightning burst through the gloom, striking the pillars of his yellow gate; the owl-tail finial fell to the ground;

sentences.zh: 又有鴟棲其帳上。

translations.literal: there were also owls perched on his canopy.
translations.idiomatic: and owls perched on his canopy as well.

sentences.zh: 以鄧琬為左將軍、尚書右僕射，張悅領軍將軍、吏部尚書，征虜將軍如故；

translations.literal: Deng Wan was made General of the Left and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Zhang Yue was made General-in-Chief of the Household Army and Minister of Personnel, retaining his post as General Who Subdues the Barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was appointed General of the Left and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat. Zhang Yue was made General-in-Chief of the Household Army and Minister of Personnel, while retaining his title as General Who Subdues the Barbarians;

sentences.zh: 進袁顗號安北將軍，加尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and added as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and given the additional post of Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臨川內史張淹為侍中。

translations.literal: Linchuan Interior Minister Zhang Yan was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, interior minister of Linchuan, was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 府主簿顧昭之、武昌太守劉弼並為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Prefecture Chief Clerk Gu Zhaozhi and Wuchang Administrator Liu Bi were both made Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhaozhi, chief clerk of the prefectural staff, and Liu Bi, administrator of Wuchang, were both appointed Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守王子仲委郡奔尋陽，亦為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Lujiang Administrator Wang Zizhong abandoned his commandery and fled to Xunyang, and was also made Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zizhong, administrator of Lujiang, abandoned his commandery and fled to Xunyang, where he too was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽內史丘景先、廬陵內史殷損、西陽太守謝稚、後軍府記室參軍孫詵、長沙內史孔靈產、參軍事沈伯玉、荀道林並為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Poyang Interior Minister Qiu Jingxian, Luling Interior Minister Yin Sun, Xiyang Administrator Xie Zhi, Rear Army Registrar Sun Shen, Changsha Interior Minister Kong Lingchan, and staff officers Shen Boyu and Xun Daolin were all made Gentlemen of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jingxian of Poyang, Yin Sun of Luling, Xie Zhi of Xiyang, Sun Shen of the rear army staff, Kong Lingchan of Changsha, and the staff officers Shen Boyu and Xun Daolin were all appointed Gentlemen of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 荀卞之為尚書左丞，府主簿江乂為右丞，府主簿蕭寶欣為通直郎。

translations.literal: Xun Bianzhi was made Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Prefecture Chief Clerk Jiang Yi was made Right Assistant Director; Prefecture Chief Clerk Xiao Baoxin was made Direct Transmission Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Bianzhi was made Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Jiang Yi, chief clerk of the staff, was made Right Assistant Director; and Xiao Baoxin, another chief clerk, was made Direct Transmission Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 琬大息粹、悅息洵並正員郎，粹領衛尉，洵弟洌司徒主簿。

translations.literal: Wan's eldest son Cui and Yue's eldest son Xun were both made regular gentlemen; Cui oversaw the Minister of the Guard, and Xun's younger brother Lie was made Secretariat archivist of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's eldest son Cui and Yue's eldest son Xun were both appointed regular gentlemen. Cui took charge of the Minister of the Guard, and Xun's younger brother Lie became archivist to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 建武將軍、領軍主、晉熙太守閻湛之加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Jianwu General, Household Army Commander, and Jinxi Administrator Yan Zhanzhi was added as General Who Calms the North.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhanzhi, Jianwu General, commander of the household army, and administrator of Jinxi, was additionally appointed General Who Calms the North.

sentences.zh: 廬陵內史王僧胤為秘書丞。

translations.literal: Luling Interior Minister Wang Shangyin was made Secretariat Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shangyin, interior minister of Luling, was appointed Secretariat Archivist.

sentences.zh: 桂陽太守劉卷為尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Guiyang Administrator Liu Juan was made Palace Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Juan, administrator of Guiyang, was appointed Palace Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 褚靈嗣、潘欣之、沈光祖，中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Chu Lingci, Pan Xinzhi, and Shen Guangzu were made Secretariat Communication Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Lingci, Pan Xinzhi, and Shen Guangzu were appointed Secretariat Communication Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 餘諸州郡，並加爵號。

translations.literal: The remaining provinces and commanderies all had ranks and titles added.
translations.idiomatic: All other provinces and commanderies received additional ranks and titles as well.

sentences.zh: 琬性鄙闇，貪吝過甚，財貨酒食，皆身自量校。

translations.literal: Wan's nature was coarse and dull, and his greed and stinginess exceeded all measure; valuables, wine, and food he personally measured and inspected.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was coarse and obtuse by nature, and his greed and stinginess knew no bounds. He personally weighed and checked every item of property, wine, and food.

sentences.zh: 至是父子並賣官鬻爵，使婢僕出市道販賣，酣歌博奕，日夜不休。

translations.literal: By now father and sons alike sold offices and peddled ranks, had maidservants go to the market to trade, and caroused and gambled day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: By then he and his sons were selling offices and trading in ranks, sending maidservants into the streets to peddle goods, and drinking, singing, and gambling without pause day or night.

sentences.zh: 大自矜遇，賓客到門者，歷旬不得前。

translations.literal: He was greatly self-important; guests who came to his gate might wait ten days without being received.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself in the highest regard. Guests who came to his door might wait ten days without being admitted.

sentences.zh: 內事悉委褚靈嗣等三人，群小橫恣，競為威福，士庶忿怨，內外離心矣。

translations.literal: Internal affairs were all entrusted to Chu Lingci and two others; petty men ran rampant, each contending for authority and blessing; gentry and commoners resented it, and inside and outside lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted all internal affairs to Chu Lingci and two others. Petty men ran wild, each scrambling for power and favor. Officials and commoners seethed with resentment, and the regime lost the loyalty of those within and without.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣散騎常侍、領軍將軍王玄謨領水軍南討，吳興太守張永為其後繼；

translations.literal: Taizong sent Regular Cavalry Attendant and General-in-Chief Wang Xuanmo to lead the naval forces south in punitive campaign, with Wu Xing Administrator Zhang Yong as rear support;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Wang Xuanmo, Regular Cavalry Attendant and General-in-Chief, to lead the fleet south in attack, with Zhang Yong, administrator of Wu Xing, as his rear support;

sentences.zh: 又遣寧朔將軍尋陽內史沈攸之、寧朔將軍江方興、龍驤將軍劉靈遺率眾屯虎檻。

translations.literal: He also sent General Who Calms the North and Xunyang Interior Minister Shen Youzhi, General Who Calms the North Jiang Fangxing, and Dragon Agile General Liu Lingyi to lead troops and encamp at Tiger Barrier.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Shen Youzhi, General Who Calms the North and interior minister of Xunyang; Jiang Fangxing, General Who Calms the North; and Liu Lingyi, Dragon Agile General, to lead forces and encamp at Tiger Barrier.

sentences.zh: 時東賊甚急，張永、江方興回軍東討。

translations.literal: At the time the eastern rebels were very pressing; Zhang Yong and Jiang Fangxing turned their armies east to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern rebels were pressing hard at the time, so Zhang Yong and Jiang Fangxing turned their armies eastward to attack them.

sentences.zh: 尚書下符曰：

translations.literal: The Imperial Secretariat dispatched a document saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Secretariat issued a directive that read:

sentences.zh: 夫晦明遞運，崇替相沿，帝宋之基，懋業維永，聖祖重光，氤氳上業。

translations.literal: As dark and bright alternate in turn and elevation and replacement follow in succession, the foundation of the Song emperor's house has flourishing merit enduring forever, and the sacred ancestor's renewed radiance, mist ascending upon the high enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Dark and bright alternate in their seasons, and rise and fall follow one upon another. The house of Song rests on a foundation whose flourishing merit endures; the sacred ancestor's renewed radiance still mists over the high enterprise.

sentences.zh: 狂昏承祀，國維以紊，毒流九縣，釁穢三靈，搢紳戮辱，黔庶塗炭，人神同憤，朝野泣血。

translations.literal: The mad and benighted bore the sacrifice; the state's cords were tangled; poison spread through the nine commanderies; violation stained the three spirits; gentry were slaughtered and humiliated; the black-haired masses were charred; humans and spirits alike were furious; court and countryside wept blood.
translations.idiomatic: Madness and blindness took the throne; the cords of state were tangled. Poison spread through the nine commanderies and defilement stained heaven, earth, and the ancestral spirits. The gentry were slaughtered and shamed; the common people were scorched to charcoal. Humans and spirits raged together; court and countryside wept blood.

sentences.zh: 聖上明睿在躬，膺符握曜，眷懷家國，夙夜劬勞，懼社稷湮蕪，彝倫左衽。

translations.literal: The Sage Lord's clear sagacity was in his person; he received the tally and grasped the celestial glory; he cherished family and state and toiled night and day, fearing the altars destroyed and norms turned awry.
translations.idiomatic: The Sage Lord's clear wisdom was in his person; he received the mandate and grasped the celestial glory. He cherished family and state and labored day and night, fearing that the altars would be ruined and moral order overturned.

sentences.zh: 天威雷發，氛沴冰消，殄凶譙門，不俟鳴條之旅；

translations.literal: Heaven's might thundered forth; miasma melted like ice; the villain at the vilified gate was exterminated without waiting for the army that strikes at the budding branch;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's wrath thundered forth and the miasma melted like ice. The villain at the rebel gate was destroyed without waiting for the army that strikes while wrongdoing is still budding;

sentences.zh: 殲虐牧野，無勞孟津之鉞。

translations.literal: cruelty was annihilated at Muye without need for the axes at Mengjin.
translations.idiomatic: cruelty was crushed at Muye without needing the battle-axes at Mengjin.

sentences.zh: 華、夷即晏，晷緯還光，鏗鏘聞於管弦，趨翔被於冠冕，同軌仰化，異域懷風。

translations.literal: Flowers and barbarians were soon calm; sundial and weft restored their brightness; music clanged in pipes and strings; the quickened step was draped over caps and sashes; the same track looked up to transformation; foreign lands embraced the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Within and beyond the borders peace returned; the sundial and the loom's warp regained their light. Music rang from pipes and strings; the court's quickened step was draped in caps and sashes. All under one track looked up to transformation; distant lands embraced the imperial wind.

sentences.zh: 劉子勛昏世稱兵，義同翦惡，明朝不戟，罔識邪正。

translations.literal: Liu Zixun in a benighted age raised arms; righteousness was the same as cutting away evil—yet the brilliant court held no halberd and did not know crooked from straight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixun raised arms in a benighted age; his cause was the same as evil to be cut away—yet the brilliant court held no halberd and could not tell crooked from straight.

sentences.zh: 窺窬畿甸，逼遏兩江，陵上無君，暴於遐邇。

translations.literal: He peered at the capital region, pressed upon the two Yang Rivers, overstepped his superiors without a lord, and was violent over far and near.
translations.idiomatic: He peered into the capital region, pressed upon the two Yang Rivers, overstepped his superiors as though there were no sovereign, and spread violence far and near.

sentences.zh: 王赫斯怒，興言討違，命彼上將，治兵薄伐。

translations.literal: The king blazed with wrath; he raised his voice to punish rebellion; he appointed those great generals to array troops for the assault.
translations.idiomatic: The king blazed with wrath. He raised his voice to punish rebellion and appointed great generals to marshal troops for the assault.

sentences.zh: 今遣寧朔將軍、尋陽內史沈攸之，輕銳七千，飛舟先邁。

translations.literal: Now he sends General Who Calms the North and Xunyang Interior Minister Shen Youzhi, seven thousand light elite, flying boats advancing first.
translations.idiomatic: He now sends Shen Youzhi, General Who Calms the North and interior minister of Xunyang, with seven thousand light elite troops in swift boats to advance first.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉靈遺，羽林虎旅，連鋒繼造。

translations.literal: Dragon Agile General Liu Lingyi, feather-grove tiger host, linked spear-points continuing to deploy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi, Dragon Agile General, leads the feather-grove tiger host in linked columns pressing forward.

sentences.zh: 假節、督南討前鋒諸軍事、冠軍將軍、兗州刺史殷孝祖，驅濟、河勁卒，電擊雷動。

translations.literal: Acting credential-holder, Supervisor of Southern Campaign Vanguard Military Affairs, Champion General, and Yanzhou Inspector Yin Xiaozu drives Ji and He stalwart soldiers in lightning strike and thunder roll.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu, acting credential-holder, supervisor of the southern campaign vanguard, Champion General, and inspector of Yanzhou, drives the stalwart soldiers of Ji and He in a charge like lightning and thunder.

sentences.zh: 使持節、車騎將軍、江州刺史曲江縣開國侯王玄謨，烝徒五萬，董統前師。

translations.literal: Credential-holder, Chariots General, Jiangzhou Inspector, and Marquis of Qujiang County Wang Xuanmo, with massed followers of fifty thousand, oversees the lead division.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo, credential-holder, Chariots General, inspector of Jiangzhou, and Marquis of Qujiang County, commands fifty thousand massed troops and directs the lead division.

sentences.zh: 使持節、侍中、司徒、揚州刺史建安王休仁，擁神州之眾，揔督群帥。

translations.literal: Credential-holder, Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Yangzhou Inspector Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren marshals the masses of the Central Plains and commands all commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an, credential-holder, Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and inspector of Yangzhou, marshals the armies of the heartland and commands all the generals.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉勔、寧朔將軍劉懷珍，步騎五千，直指大雷。

translations.literal: Dragon Agile General Liu Mian and General Who Calms the North Liu Huaizhen, five thousand foot and horse, drive straight toward Great Thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian, Dragon Agile General, and Liu Huaizhen, General Who Calms the North, with five thousand foot and horse, drive straight toward Great Thunder.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍柳倫、司州刺史龐孟虯，淮、潁突騎，邪趣西陽。

translations.literal: General Who Calms the North Liu Lun and Sizhou Inspector Pang Mengjiao, Huai and Ying shock cavalry, slant toward Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lun, General Who Calms the North, and Pang Mengjiao, inspector of Sizhou, lead Huai and Ying shock cavalry on a slanting advance toward Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 使持節、驃騎大將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐，揔勒步師，連旗百萬，河舟代馬，遄鶩江濆，越棘吳鉤，交曜畿服，笳鼓動坤維，金甲震雲漢，掎角相望，水陸俱發。

translations.literal: Credential-holder, Great Cavalry General-in-Chief, and Yuzhou Inspector Prince of Shanyang Liu Xiuyou commands foot soldiers; banners in the millions; river boats and Dai horses surge at the riverside; Yue halberds and Wu hooks gleam across the capital lands; pipes and drums shake earth's corner; gold armor shakes the Milky Way; pincers and horns in sight; land and water both set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang, credential-holder, Great Cavalry General-in-Chief, and inspector of Yuzhou, commands the foot armies with a million linked banners. River boats and northern horses surge along the riverbanks; Yue halberds and Wu swords flash across the capital region. Pipes and drums shake the earth's foundations; golden armor shakes the Milky Way. Forces in pincer and horn formation advance together by land and water.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍武念，率雍、司之銳，已據樊、沔。

translations.literal: Champion General Wu Nian leads Yong and Si elite and already holds Fan and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nian, Champion General, leads the elite of Yong and Si and already holds Fan and Mian.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史申令孫，提彭、宋剽勇，陵塗焱奮。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Inspector Shen Lingsun lifts Peng and Song fierce courage and blazes along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lingsun, inspector of Xuzhou, leads the fierce warriors of Peng and Song, blazing along the highways.

sentences.zh: 皇上當親馭六師，降臨江服，旌旆掩雲，舳艫咽海。

translations.literal: The emperor will personally drive the six hosts, descend to the Yang region; banners cover the clouds; ships choke the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor will personally command the six armies and descend upon the Yang region. His banners will blanket the clouds; his ships will choke the sea.

sentences.zh: 昔吳、楚連衡，燕、淮勁悍，塵擾區內，聲沸秦中，霧散埃滅，豈非先鑒。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu and Chu linked in alliance; Yan and Huai were strong and fierce; dust stirred within the realm; sound boiled in the Qin heartland—mist scattered and dust extinguished; is this not a prior mirror?
translations.idiomatic: In the past Wu and Chu joined in alliance; Yan and Huai were strong and fierce. Dust stirred within the realm and their fame boiled through the heartland—yet mist scattered and dust was extinguished. Is this not a lesson from history?

sentences.zh: 而嬰彼孤城，以待該天之網，迫此烏合，以抗絡宇之師。

translations.literal: Yet they cling to that lone city, awaiting heaven's net drawn tight; they press this rabble host to resist armies spanning the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they cling to a lone city, awaiting heaven's net to close; they drive this rabble host to resist armies that span the realm.

sentences.zh: 雲羅四掩，霜鋒交集，猶勁飆之拂細草，烈火之掃寒原，燋卷之形，昭然已著。

translations.literal: Cloud net closes on four sides; frost blades cross; still like fierce gale brushing fine grass, fierce fire sweeping cold plain—the scorched scroll's form is already clearly shown.
translations.idiomatic: The cloud-net closes on four sides and frost-sharp blades cross. It will be like a fierce gale brushing fine grass, like fierce fire sweeping a cold plain—the shape of their scorching defeat is already plain to see.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惻愍我僚吏，哀矜我士民，並亦何辜，拘誤迷黨。

translations.literal: The court pities our officials and pities our soldiers and people—they too what guilt, detained and misled by the faction.
translations.idiomatic: The court pities its officials and pities its soldiers and people. What guilt do they bear, to be detained and misled by this faction?

sentences.zh: 故加宣示，令得自新。

translations.literal: Therefore we add this proclamation, letting them obtain renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore this proclamation is issued, that they may renew themselves.

sentences.zh: 如其淪惑不改，抵冒王威，同焚既至，雖悔奚補。

translations.literal: If they sink in delusion and do not change, resist and defy royal majesty, when shared burning arrives, though they repent what will it avail?
translations.idiomatic: If they remain sunk in delusion and do not change, if they resist and defy royal majesty, when the common fire comes upon them, repentance will avail nothing.

sentences.zh: 奉詔以四王幼弱，不幸陷難，兵交之日，不得妄加侵犯，若有逼損，誅翦無貸。

translations.literal: By imperial order: as the Four Princes are young and weak and unluckily trapped in hardship, on the day arms clash they must not be rashly harmed; whoever presses or injures them shall be cut down without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order: the Four Princes are young and weak and have unluckily been caught in this calamity. On the day arms clash they must not be harmed without cause. Whoever presses or injures them shall be cut down without mercy.

sentences.zh: 左右主帥，嚴相衛奉，詿誤之罪，一無所問。

translations.literal: Left and right chief commanders, strictly guard and attend them; the crime of being led astray—inquiry none at all.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders on left and right must strictly guard and protect them. The crime of having been led astray shall not be questioned at all.

sentences.zh: 琬遣孫沖之率陳紹宗、胡靈秀、薛常寶、張繼伯、焦度等前鋒一萬，來據赭圻。

translations.literal: Wan sent Sun Chongzhi leading Chen Shaozong, Hu Lingxiu, Xue Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Jiao Du, and others with ten thousand vanguard troops to come and seize Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent Sun Chongzhi, with Chen Shaozong, Hu Lingxiu, Xue Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Jiao Du, and others leading ten thousand vanguard troops, to occupy Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 沖之於道與子勛書曰：「舟楫已辦，器械亦整，三軍踴躍，人爭效命，便欲沿流掛颿，直取白下。

translations.literal: Chongzhi on the road wrote Zi Xun: "Boats are ready, weapons also ordered; the three armies leap, men vie to give their lives—we intend to follow the current, raise sails, and straight take Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: On the march Chongzhi wrote to Zi Xun: "The boats are ready and the weapons in order. The three armies are eager; every man strives to give his life. We mean to follow the current, raise our sails, and strike straight for Baixia.

sentences.zh: 願速遣陶亮眾軍，兼行相接，分據新亭、南州，則一麾定矣。

translations.literal: I wish you quickly to send Tao Liang's hosts to march together in support, divide and hold Xinting and Nanzhou, then one wave will settle it."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you quickly send Tao Liang's forces to march with us and join up, and that we divide and hold Xinting and Nanzhou—then one command will settle everything."

sentences.zh: 」乃加沖之左衛將軍，以陶亮為右衛將軍，統諸州兵俱下。

translations.literal: Then Chongzhi was added as Left Guards General, Tao Liang made Right Guards General, commanding all province armies down together.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi was then promoted to Left Guards General and Tao Liang made Right Guards General, with command over all provincial armies marching south together.

sentences.zh: 郢州軍主鄭景玄、荊州軍主劉亮、湘州軍主何昌、梁州軍主柳登、雍州軍主宗庶等合二萬人，一時俱下。

translations.literal: Yingzhou army commander Zheng Jingxuan, Jingzhou army commander Liu Liang, Xiangzhou army commander He Chang, Liangzhou army commander Liu Deng, Yongzhou army commander Zong Shu, and others combined twenty thousand men, all descending at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jingxuan, army commander of Yingzhou; Liu Liang of Jingzhou; He Chang of Xiangzhou; Liu Deng of Liangzhou; Zong Shu of Yongzhou; and others combined twenty thousand men and marched south all at once.

sentences.zh: 亮本無幹略，聞建安王休仁自上，殷孝祖又至，不敢進，屯軍鵲洲。

translations.literal: Liang originally had no capacity for strategy; hearing Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren came from above and Yin Xiaozu also arrived, he dared not advance and encamped his army at Magpie Islet.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had no real talent for command. When he heard that Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was coming from the north and Yin Xiaozu had also arrived, he dared not advance and encamped at Magpie Islet.

sentences.zh: 時琬遣閻湛之來寇廬江，臺軍主、龍驤將軍段佛榮受命討之。

translations.literal: At the time Wan sent Yan Zhanzhi to raid Lujiang; imperial army commander Dragon Agile General Duan Forong received orders to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had sent Yan Zhanzhi to raid Lujiang. Duan Forong, Dragon Agile General and imperial army commander, was ordered to attack him.

sentences.zh: 更使佛榮領鐵騎一千，回軍南討。

translations.literal: He again had Forong lead one thousand iron cavalry and turn his army south to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Forong was then given command of one thousand iron cavalry and ordered to turn his army south in attack.

sentences.zh: 三月三日，水陸攻赭圻，亮等率眾來救，殷孝祖為流矢所中死，軍主朱輔之、申謙之、張靈符竝失利，輔之副正員將軍皇甫仲遠、謙之副虎賁中郎將徐稚賓並沒。

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month, land and water attacked Zheqi; Liang and others led masses to rescue; Yin Xiaozu was struck by a stray arrow and died; army commanders Zhu Fuzhi, Shen Qianzhi, and Zhang Lingfu all lost advantage; Fuzhi's deputy Regular General Huangfu Zhongyuan and Qianzhi's deputy Tiger-Guard Central Commander Xu Zhibin both perished.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the third month the armies attacked Zheqi by land and water. Liang and others led troops to the relief, but Yin Xiaozu was killed by a stray arrow. The army commanders Zhu Fuzhi, Shen Qianzhi, and Zhang Lingfu all met defeat. Huangfu Zhongyuan, Fuzhi's deputy and a regular general, and Xu Zhibin, Qianzhi's deputy and Tiger-Guard central commander, both fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 孝祖支軍主范潛率五百人投亮。

translations.literal: Xiaozu's detached army commander Fan Qian led five hundred men to surrender to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qian, commander of Xiaozu's detached force, led five hundred men in surrender to Liang.

sentences.zh: 時東軍已捷，江方興復還虎檻，建安王休仁遣方興、劉靈遺各領三千人助赭圻，以方興領孝祖軍，沈攸之代孝祖為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: At the time the eastern army had already won; Jiang Fangxing returned again to Tiger Barrier; Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren sent Fangxing and Liu Lingyi each commanding three thousand to aid Zheqi; Fangxing took Xiaozu's army; Shen Youzhi replaced Xiaozu as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army had already won by then. Jiang Fangxing returned to Tiger Barrier. Prince Xiuren of Jian'an sent Fangxing and Liu Lingyi, each with three thousand men, to reinforce Zheqi. Fangxing took over Xiaozu's army, and Shen Youzhi replaced Xiaozu as commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 沖之謂陶亮曰：「孝祖梟將，一戰便死。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said to Tao Liang: "Xiaozu was a fierce general; one battle and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi said to Tao Liang: "Xiaozu was a fierce general, yet he died in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 天下事定矣，不須復戰，便當直取京都。

translations.literal: The affair under heaven is settled; no need for more fighting—we should straight take the capital."
translations.idiomatic: The empire is settled. There is no need to fight again—we should march straight on the capital."

sentences.zh: 」亮不從。

translations.literal: Liang would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Liang would not agree.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣員外散騎侍郎王道隆至赭圻督戰。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Extraordinary Regular Cavalier Gentleman Wang Daolong to Zheqi to supervise battle.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Wang Daolong, Extraordinary Regular Cavalier Gentleman, to Zheqi to supervise the fighting.

sentences.zh: 孝祖死之明日，建安王休仁又遣軍主郭季之馬步三千就攸之，攸之乃率季之及輔國將軍步兵校尉杜幼文、寧朔將軍屯騎校尉垣恭祖、龍驤將軍朱輔之、員外散騎侍郎高遵世、馬軍主龍驤將軍頓生、段佛榮等三萬人，詰旦進戰，奮擊，大破之，斬獲數千，追奔至姥山而反。

translations.literal: The day after Xiaozu died, Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren again sent army commander Guo Jizhi with three thousand horse and foot to join Youzhi; Youzhi then led Jizhi and Auxiliary State General Foot-Soldier Colonel Du Youwen, General Who Calms the North Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Yuan Gongzu, Dragon Agile General Zhu Fuzhi, Extraordinary Regular Cavalier Gentleman Gao Zunshi, horse army commander Dragon Agile General Dun Sheng, Duan Forong, and others—thirty thousand men—advancing to battle at dawn, striking fiercely, greatly defeating them, killing and capturing thousands, pursuing the fleeing to Old Woman Mountain then returning.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Xiaozu's death, Prince Xiuren of Jian'an sent the army commander Guo Jizhi with three thousand horse and foot to join Youzhi. Youzhi then led Jizhi, Du Youwen (Auxiliary State General and Foot-Soldier Colonel), Yuan Gongzu (General Who Calms the North and Colonel of Garrison Cavalry), Zhu Fuzhi (Dragon Agile General), Gao Zunshi (Extraordinary Regular Cavalier Gentleman), Dun Sheng (Dragon Agile General and cavalry commander), Duan Forong, and others—thirty thousand in all—to advance at dawn. They struck hard, won a great victory, killed and captured thousands, and pursued the fugitives to Old Woman Mountain before turning back.

sentences.zh: 沖之等於湖、白口築二城，為軍主張興世所拔。

translations.literal: Chongzhi and others built two forts at Lake and White Mouth; they were taken by army commander Zhang Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi and his men built two forts at Lake Mouth and White Mouth, but army commander Zhang Xingshi captured them.

sentences.zh: 陶亮聞湖、白二城陷沒，大懼，急呼沖之還鵲尾，留薛常寶代沖之守赭圻。
