translations.literal: Tao Liang hearing the Lake and White two forts had fallen was greatly afraid, urgently called Chongzhi back to Magpie Tail, left Xue Changbao to replace Chongzhi guarding Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Liang heard that the two forts at Lake and White Mouth had fallen, he was terrified. He urgently recalled Chongzhi to Magpie Tail and left Xue Changbao to hold Zheqi in Chongzhi's place.

sentences.zh: 先於姥山及諸岡分立營寨，亦悉敗還，共保濃湖。

translations.literal: Earlier at Old Woman Mountain and various hillocks they had separately established camps; these also all were defeated and retreated, together defending Dense Lake.
translations.idiomatic: The camps they had earlier set up separately at Old Woman Mountain and on the surrounding hills were also all lost, and the forces fell back together to defend Dense Lake.

sentences.zh: 濃湖即在鵲尾。

translations.literal: Dense Lake is right at Magpie Tail.
translations.idiomatic: Dense Lake lay directly at Magpie Tail.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅大起，國用不足，募民上米二百斛，錢五萬，雜穀五百斛，同賜荒縣除。

translations.literal: At the time armies rose greatly and national funds were insufficient; they recruited people who offered two hundred hu of rice, fifty thousand cash, and five hundred hu of mixed grain—the same reward as appointment to a remote county.
translations.idiomatic: Armies were mobilized on a vast scale and the treasury was strained. The court recruited donors who contributed two hundred hu of rice, fifty thousand cash, and five hundred hu of mixed grain, granting in return the same reward as appointment to a remote county post.

sentences.zh: 上米三百斛，錢八萬，雜穀千斛，同賜四品正令史；

translations.literal: Three hundred hu of rice offered, eighty thousand cash, one thousand hu of mixed grain—the same reward as fourth-rank regular clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred hu of rice, eighty thousand cash, and one thousand hu of mixed grain earned the reward of a fourth-rank regular clerk;

sentences.zh: 滿報，若欲署四品在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: when quota was full, if wishing appointment as fourth-rank home clerk, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: when the quota was filled, appointment as a fourth-rank home clerk was also permitted if desired.

sentences.zh: 上米四百斛，錢十二萬，雜穀一千三百斛，同賜四品正令史；

translations.literal: Four hundred hu of rice offered, one hundred twenty thousand cash, one thousand three hundred hu of mixed grain—the same reward as fourth-rank regular clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred hu of rice, one hundred twenty thousand cash, and thirteen hundred hu of mixed grain earned the reward of a fourth-rank regular clerk;

sentences.zh: 滿報，若欲署三品在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: when quota was full, if wishing appointment as third-rank home clerk, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: when the quota was filled, appointment as a third-rank home clerk was also permitted if desired.

sentences.zh: 上米五百斛，錢十五萬，雜穀一千五百斛，同賜三品令史；

translations.literal: Five hundred hu of rice offered, one hundred fifty thousand cash, one thousand five hundred hu of mixed grain—the same reward as third-rank clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred hu of rice, one hundred fifty thousand cash, and fifteen hundred hu of mixed grain earned the reward of a third-rank clerk;

sentences.zh: 滿報，若欲署內監在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: when quota was full, if wishing appointment as inner supervisor home clerk, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: when the quota was filled, appointment as a home-based inner supervisor clerk was also permitted if desired.

sentences.zh: 上米七百斛，錢二十萬，雜穀二千斛，同賜荒郡除；

translations.literal: Seven hundred hu of rice offered, two hundred thousand cash, two thousand hu of mixed grain—the same reward as remote-commandery appointment;
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred hu of rice, two hundred thousand cash, and two thousand hu of mixed grain earned the reward of appointment to a remote commandery;

sentences.zh: 若欲署諸王國三令在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: if wishing appointment as princely state third-order home clerk, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: appointment as a third-order home clerk in a princely state was also permitted if desired.

sentences.zh: 琬又遣輔國將軍、豫州刺史劉胡率眾三萬，鐵騎二千，來屯鵲尾。

translations.literal: Wan again sent Auxiliary State General and Yuzhou Inspector Liu Hu leading masses of thirty thousand and iron cavalry of two thousand to come and encamp at Magpie Tail.
translations.idiomatic: Wan again sent Liu Hu, Auxiliary State General and inspector of Yuzhou, with thirty thousand troops and two thousand iron cavalry to encamp at Magpie Tail.

sentences.zh: 胡宿將，屢有戰功，素多狡詐，為眾推伏，攸之等甚憚之。

translations.literal: Hu was a veteran general, repeatedly had battle merit, by nature much crafty and deceitful, regarded by the masses as submitted to; Youzhi and others greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was a veteran general with repeated battle honors. He was by nature crafty and deceitful, yet the troops submitted to him. Youzhi and the others feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時胡鄉人蔡那、佼長生、張敬兒各領軍隸攸之在赭圻，胡以書招之，那等並拒絕。

translations.literal: At the time Hu's townsmen Cai Na, Jiao Changsheng, and Zhang Jing'er each led armies subordinate to Youzhi at Zheqi; Hu by letter invited them; they all refused.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's fellow townsmen Cai Na, Jiao Changsheng, and Zhang Jing'er were then each leading troops under Youzhi at Zheqi. Hu wrote to recruit them, but they all refused.

sentences.zh: 胡因要那等共語，陳說平生，那等詰誚，說令歸順。

translations.literal: Hu then requested Na and others speak together, narrating their former years; they interrogated and mocked him, urging him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Hu then asked to meet Na and the others and spoke of their shared past. They questioned and mocked him in turn, urging him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 胡回軍入鵲尾，無他權略。

translations.literal: Hu returned his army into Magpie Tail, having no other stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Hu withdrew his army into Magpie Tail, with no further plan to offer.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍吳喜平定三吳，率所領五千人，并運資實，至於赭圻，於戰鳥山築壘，分遣千人，乘輕舸二百，與佼長生為游軍。

translations.literal: Auxiliary State General Wu Xi pacified the Three Wu, led his following of five thousand men, together transporting supplies and provisions, reaching Zheqi; at Battlebird Mountain he built a stockade, divided off and sent one thousand men riding two hundred light boats, with Jiao Changsheng as a screening force.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi, Auxiliary State General, having pacified the Three Wu, led his five thousand men and their supplies to Zheqi. At Battlebird Mountain he built a stockade, detached one thousand men in two hundred light boats, and joined Jiao Changsheng as a mobile screening force.

sentences.zh: 薛常寶糧盡，告胡求援。

translations.literal: Xue Changbao's grain was exhausted; he informed Hu requesting relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Changbao ran out of grain and sent word to Hu asking for relief.

sentences.zh: 三月二十九日，胡率步卒一萬，夜斫山開道，以布囊運米，來餉赭圻。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the third month, Hu led ten thousand foot soldiers, at night chopped the mountain to open a road, using cloth sacks to transport rice, coming to provision Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day of the third month, Hu led ten thousand foot soldiers. They cut a path through the mountains by night and carried rice in cloth sacks to supply Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 平旦至城下，猶隔小塹，未能得入。

translations.literal: At daybreak they reached below the city, still separated by a small moat, and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they reached the walls, but a small moat still lay between them and they could not get in.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之率眾軍攻之，軍主郭季之、荀僧韶、幢主韓欣宗等，率眾三千，為攸之勢援。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi led the mass armies to attack them; army commanders Guo Jizhi, Xun Sengshao, banner commander Han Xinzong, and others led masses of three thousand as momentum support for Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi led the main force to attack them. Army commanders Guo Jizhi, Xun Sengshao, and banner commander Han Xinzong brought three thousand men to reinforce Youzhi's assault.

sentences.zh: 胡發所由橋道，僧韶等接楯行戰，復橋得渡。

translations.literal: Hu set out along the bridge road he had come by; Sengshao and others received shields and advanced fighting, recovered the bridge, and were able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Hu advanced along the bridge by which he had come. Sengshao and the others fought forward under shield cover, retook the bridge, and crossed.

sentences.zh: 軍主劉沙彌輕騎深入，至胡麾下，遂見殺。

translations.literal: Army commander Liu Shami with light cavalry penetrated deep, reaching beneath Hu's standard, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Liu Shami rode in light cavalry deep into the enemy line until he reached Hu's own command post, where he was killed.

sentences.zh: 攸之策馬陷陳，回還，為追騎所刺；

translations.literal: Youzhi spurred his horse into the formation, turned back, and was stabbed by pursuing horsemen;
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi spurred his horse into the enemy ranks, then turned back and was stabbed by pursuing horsemen;

sentences.zh: 馬軍主段佛榮、武保救之得免。

translations.literal: cavalry army commander Duan Forong and martial guards rescued him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commander Duan Forong and his martial guards rescued him, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 並殊死戰，多所傷殺。

translations.literal: All fought to the death, with many wounded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides fought to the death, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 胡眾大敗，捨糧棄甲，緣山遁走，乘勝追之，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Hu's masses were greatly defeated, abandoned grain and cast off armor, fled along the mountains; the victors pursued and beheaded and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's army was routed. The men abandoned their grain and armor and fled along the mountain paths. The pursuers cut down and captured a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 胡被創，僅得還營。

translations.literal: Hu received wounds and barely was able to return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was wounded and barely made it back to camp.

sentences.zh: 常寶惶懼無計，遣信告胡，欲突圍奔出。

translations.literal: Changbao was fearful and without plan, sent a message informing Hu that he wished to break out of encirclement and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Changbao, desperate and at a loss, sent word to Hu that he wanted to break out and escape.

sentences.zh: 四月四日，胡自率數千人迎之，常寶等開城突圍走。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fourth month, Hu himself led several thousand men to meet them; Changbao and others opened the city and broke out in flight.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the fourth month, Hu personally led several thousand men to meet them. Changbao and his men opened the gates and broke out of the siege.

sentences.zh: 攸之率輔國將軍沈懷明、軍主周普孫、江方興、申謙之等諸軍悉力擊之。

translations.literal: Youzhi led Auxiliary State General Shen Huaiming, army commanders Zhou Pusun, Jiang Fangxing, Shen Qianzhi, and the rest of the armies to strike them with full force.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi led Shen Huaiming, Auxiliary State General, and army commanders Zhou Pusun, Jiang Fangxing, Shen Qianzhi, and the rest in an all-out assault.

sentences.zh: 吳喜率眾來赴，為胡別軍所圍，甚急。

translations.literal: Wu Xi led masses to come to the rescue and was encircled by Hu's detached army, in extreme peril.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi marched to their aid with his troops but was surrounded by a detached force of Hu's army and driven into grave danger.

sentences.zh: 有人來捉喜馬，將蔡保以刀斫之，斷手，然後得免。

translations.literal: Someone came to seize Xi's horse; General Cai Bao hacked him with a blade, severing his hand, and only then did Xi escape.
translations.idiomatic: An enemy soldier seized Xi's bridle. General Cai Bao hacked at the man with his blade and cut off his hand, and only then did Xi escape.

sentences.zh: 正員將軍幢主卜伯宗、江夏國侍郎幢主張渙力戰沒陳。

translations.literal: Regular General banner commander Bu Bozong and Jiangxia Principality Attendant Gentleman banner commander Zhang Huan fought fiercely and fell in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Regular General and banner commander Bu Bozong and Jiangxia Principality Attendant Gentleman and banner commander Zhang Huan fought to the death and fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 伯宗，益州刺史天與子也。

translations.literal: Bozong was the son of Yizhou Inspector Tianyu.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong was the son of Tianyu, inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 攸之、喜等苦戰移日，常寶、張繼伯、胡靈秀、焦度等皆被重創，走還胡軍。

translations.literal: Youzhi, Xi, and others bitterly fought for a full day; Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Hu Lingxiu, Jiao Du, and others all received grave wounds and fled back to Hu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, Xi, and the others fought bitterly all day. Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Hu Lingxiu, Jiao Du, and the rest were all badly wounded and fled back to Hu's lines.

sentences.zh: 赭圻城陷，斬偽寧朔將軍南陽太守沈懷寶、偽奉朝請領中舍人督戰謝道遇，納降數千。

translations.literal: Zheqi city fell; the rebel Pacification General and Nanyang Administrator Shen Huaibao and rebel Court Attendant-in-Ordinary supervising battle as Central Household Steward Xie Daoyu were beheaded, and several thousand submitted in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zheqi fell. The rebel generals Shen Huaibao, Pacification General and administrator of Nanyang, and Xie Daoyu, Court Attendant-in-Ordinary who had directed the fighting as Central Household Steward, were beheaded, and several thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 陳紹宗單舸奔西岸，與其部曲俱還鵲尾。

translations.literal: Chen Shaozong in a single boat fled to the western shore, and with his retainers all returned to Magpie Tail.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaozong fled alone in a single boat to the western shore and rejoined his troops at Magpie Tail.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁自虎檻進據赭圻。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an Xiuren advanced from Tiger Fence and seized Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an Xiuren advanced from Tiger Fence and took up position at Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 劉胡遣陳紹宗、陳慶率輕艓二百，大艦五十，出鵲外挑戰；

translations.literal: Liu Hu sent Chen Shaozong and Chen Qing leading two hundred light boats and fifty great ships to go out beyond Magpie and offer battle;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu sent Chen Shaozong and Chen Qing with two hundred light boats and fifty large warships to sail out beyond Magpie Tail and offer battle;

sentences.zh: 吳喜、張興世、佼長生等擊之。

translations.literal: Wu Xi, Zhang Xingshi, Jiao Changsheng, and others struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi, Zhang Xingshi, Jiao Changsheng, and the others attacked them.

sentences.zh: 喜支軍主吳獻之飛舸衝突，所向摧陷，斬獲及投水死甚多，追至鵲裏而還。

translations.literal: Xi's detached army commander Wu Xianzhi in flying boats charged and broke through; wherever he went he crushed and overthrew; beheaded, captured, and drowned dead were very many; they pursued to Magpie Interior and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's detached commander Wu Xianzhi led swift boats in a headlong charge and smashed everything in his path. A great many were killed, captured, or drowned. The pursuers chased the enemy to Magpie Interior and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太宗慮胡等或於步路向京邑，使寧朔將軍、廣德令王蘊千人防魯顯。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong feared that Hu and others might by land route march on the capital region and sent Pacification General and Guangde Magistrate Wang Yun with one thousand men to defend Luyan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong feared that Hu and his allies might march overland toward the capital and sent Wang Yun, Pacification General and magistrate of Guangde, with one thousand men to hold Luyan.

sentences.zh: 時胡等兵眾強盛，遠近疑惑。

translations.literal: At the time Hu and others' troops and masses were powerful and flourishing; near and far were doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's army was then at the height of its strength, and men near and far were uncertain which side would prevail.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲綏慰人情，遣吏部尚書褚淵至虎檻選用將帥以下，申謙之、杜幼文因此求黃門郎，沈懷明、劉亮求中書郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong wished to soothe and comfort popular sentiment and sent Minister of the Civil Service Chu Yuan to Tiger Fence to select and appoint generals and commanders downward; Shen Qianzhi and Du Youwen on this account requested Yellow Gate Gentleman; Shen Huaiming and Liu Liang requested Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong wished to reassure the troops and sent Chu Yuan, Minister of the Civil Service, to Tiger Fence to make appointments among the generals and their subordinates. Shen Qianzhi and Du Youwen used the occasion to ask for posts as Yellow Gate Gentlemen; Shen Huaiming and Liu Liang asked for Secretariat Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁即使褚淵擬選，上不許，曰：「忠臣殉國，不謀其報，臨難以干朝典，豈臣下之節邪？」

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an Xiuren thereupon had Chu Yuan draft selections; the Emperor did not permit it, saying: "Loyal ministers die for the state and do not calculate their reward; to importune court statutes amid hardship—how is that the demeanor of subjects?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an Xiuren had Chu Yuan draw up a list of appointments, but the Emperor refused, saying, "Loyal ministers die for the state without calculating their reward. To press for court appointments in the midst of battle—what sort of conduct is that for a subject?"

sentences.zh: 始安內史王職之、建安內史趙道生、安成太守劉襲，並舉郡奉順。

translations.literal: Shi'an Interior Governor Wang Zhizhi, Jian'an Interior Governor Zhao Daosheng, and Ancheng Administrator Liu Xi all raised their commanderies in submission and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an interior governor Wang Zhizhi, Jian'an interior governor Zhao Daosheng, and Ancheng administrator Liu Xi each rallied their commanderies to the imperial cause.

sentences.zh: 琬遣龍驤將軍廖琰率數千人，并發廬陵白丁攻襲。

translations.literal: Wan sent Dragon-Prancing General Liao Yan leading several thousand men, together mobilizing Luling common levies to attack Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent Liao Yan, Dragon-Prancing General, with several thousand men and also raised common levies from Luling to attack Xi.

sentences.zh: 襲與郡丞檀玢拒戰，大敗，玢臨陳見殺，襲棄郡走，據險自守。

translations.literal: Xi with Commandery Assistant Tan Bin resisted in battle and was greatly defeated; Bin at the front of the formation was killed; Xi abandoned the commandery and fled, seized defiles, and defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and his commandery aide Tan Bin fought back but were routed. Bin was killed in the front line. Xi abandoned the commandery, fled, and held a defensible position.

sentences.zh: 琰虜掠而退，襲復出據郡。

translations.literal: Yan plundered as a captive-taker and withdrew; Xi again came out and seized the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan looted the region and withdrew, and Xi returned to reoccupy the commandery.

sentences.zh: 時齊王率眾東北征討，而齊王世子為南康贛令，琬遣使收世子；

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Qi led masses northeast in punitive campaign, while the Prince of Qi's heir was Nankang Gan Magistrate; Wan sent envoys to seize the heir;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi was then leading his army northeast on campaign, while his heir served as magistrate of Gan in Nankang. Wan sent men to seize the heir;

sentences.zh: 世子腹心蕭欣祖、桓康等數十人，奉世子長子奔竄草澤，召募得百餘人，攻郡出世子。

translations.literal: The heir's intimate retainers Xiao Xinzu, Huan Kang, and several tens of others escorted the heir's eldest son fleeing into marshes and meadows, recruited and obtained a hundred-odd men, attacked the commandery, and brought out the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of the heir's closest followers, including Xiao Xinzu and Huan Kang, fled with the heir's eldest son into the marshes, recruited more than a hundred men, stormed the commandery seat, and freed the heir.

sentences.zh: 世子自號寧朔將軍，與南康相沈用之、前南海太守何曇直、晉康太守劉紹祖、北地傅浩、東莞童禽等，據郡起義。

translations.literal: The heir styled himself Pacification General, and with Nankang Chancellor Shen Yongzhi, former Nanhai Administrator He Tanzhi, Jinkang Administrator Liu Shaozu, Beidi's Fu Hao, Dongguan's Tong Qin, and others seized the commandery and raised righteous arms.
translations.idiomatic: The heir styled himself Pacification General. With Nankang chancellor Shen Yongzhi, former Nanhai administrator He Tanzhi, Jinkang administrator Liu Shaozu, Fu Hao of Beidi, Tong Qin of Dongguan, and others, he seized the commandery and rose in revolt for the court.

sentences.zh: 琬徴始興相殷孚為御史中丞，并令率郡人俱下。

translations.literal: Wan summoned Shixing Chancellor Yin Fu as Censor-in-Chief and also ordered him to lead commandery men down together.
translations.idiomatic: Wan summoned Yin Fu, chancellor of Shixing, to serve as Censor-in-Chief and ordered him to march south with the men of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 孚眾盛，世子避之於揭陽山。

translations.literal: Fu's masses were abundant; the heir avoided him at Jieyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's force was large, and the heir withdrew to Jieyang Mountain to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 琬遣武昌戴凱之為南康相，世子率眾攻之，凱之戰敗遁走。

translations.literal: Wan sent Wuchang's Dai Kaizhi as Nankang Chancellor; the heir led masses to attack him; Kaizhi was defeated in battle and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent Dai Kaizhi of Wuchang to serve as Nankang chancellor. The heir attacked him with his troops, and Kaizhi was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 世子遣幢主檀文起千人戍西昌，與襲相應。

translations.literal: The heir sent banner commander Tan Wenqi with one thousand men to garrison Xichang, coordinating with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The heir sent banner commander Tan Wenqi with one thousand men to hold Xichang in coordination with Liu Xi.

sentences.zh: 琬又遣廖琰與其中兵參軍胡昭等築壘於西昌，堅壁相守。

translations.literal: Wan again sent Liao Yan with his Central Army Major Hu Zhao and others to build stockades at Xichang and hold fast behind walls in mutual defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wan again sent Liao Yan and his Central Army Major Hu Zhao to build fortifications at Xichang and hold them in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 琬召豫章太守劉衍以為右將軍、中護軍，殷孚代為豫章太守，督上流五郡，以防襲等。

translations.literal: Wan summoned Yuzhang Administrator Liu Yan to serve as Right General and Central Army Protector; Yin Fu replaced him as Yuzhang Administrator, supervising the five upper-stream commanderies to guard against Xi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wan summoned Liu Yan, administrator of Yuzhang, to serve as Right General and Central Army Protector. Yin Fu replaced him as administrator of Yuzhang and took charge of the five upper Yangzi commanderies to block Xi and his allies.

sentences.zh: 衡陽內史王應之率郡文武五百許人，起義兵襲何慧文於長沙，徑至城下。

translations.literal: Hengyang Interior Governor Wang Yingzhi led commandery civil and military officials, about five hundred men, raised righteous troops to strike He Huiwen at Changsha, and went straight to below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingzhi, interior governor of Hengyang, led some five hundred officials and soldiers of the commandery in a loyalist attack on He Huiwen at Changsha and marched straight to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 慧文率左右出城與戰，應之勇氣奮發，擊殺數人，遂與慧文交手戰，斫慧文八創，慧文斫應之斷足，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Huiwen led his attendants out of the city to fight; Yingzhi's martial spirit flared, he struck and killed several men, then crossed hands with Huiwen in combat, hacked Huiwen eight wounds; Huiwen hacked Yingzhi severing his foot, and then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwen led his personal guard out to fight. Yingzhi fought with fierce courage, killed several men, and closed with Huiwen in hand-to-hand combat, cutting him eight times. Huiwen struck back, severed Yingzhi's foot, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時湘東國侍郎虞洽為太宗督國秩，在湘東，勸太守顏躍發兵應朝廷，躍不從。

translations.literal: At the time Xiangdong Principality Attendant Gentleman Yu Qia was supervising the principality stipend for Emperor Taizong and was in Xiangdong; he urged Administrator Yan Yue to raise troops in response to the court; Yue did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qia, Attendant Gentleman of Xiangdong Principality, was then supervising the principality stipend on Emperor Taizong's behalf in Xiangdong. He urged administrator Yan Yue to raise troops for the court, but Yue refused.

sentences.zh: 洽乃投桂陽，收募得數百人，還欲攻躍，躍懼求和，許之；

translations.literal: Qia then went to Guiyang, gathered and recruited several hundred men, returned intending to attack Yue; Yue in fear sought peace, and Qia permitted it;
translations.idiomatic: Qia then went to Guiyang, recruited several hundred men, and returned intending to attack Yue. Yue, afraid, sued for peace, and Qia agreed;

sentences.zh: 有眾二千。

translations.literal: He had masses of two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He now had two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時琬徵慧文率眾下尋陽，發長沙，已行數百里，聞洽起兵，乃回還攻洽，洽尋戰敗奔走。

translations.literal: At the time Wan had summoned Huiwen to lead masses down to Xunyang; he set out from Changsha and had already marched several hundred li when he heard Qia had raised troops, then turned back to attack Qia; Qia soon was defeated in battle and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had summoned Huiwen to march south to Xunyang. He had left Changsha and was already several hundred li on the road when he heard that Qia had risen. He turned back to attack Qia, who was soon defeated and put to flight.

sentences.zh: 殷孚既去始興，以郡五官掾譚伯初留知郡事。

translations.literal: Yin Fu having already left Shixing, he left Commandery Five-Officials Clerk Tan Bochu behind to manage commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin Fu left Shixing, he left Tan Bochu, the commandery's Five-Officials Clerk, in charge of local affairs.

sentences.zh: 士人劉嗣祖等斬伯初，據郡起義。

translations.literal: Gentlemen Liu Sizu and others beheaded Bochu, seized the commandery, and raised righteous arms.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentlemen led by Liu Sizu killed Bochu, seized the commandery, and rose for the court.

sentences.zh: 琬遣始興太守韋希真、鷹揚將軍楊弘之領眾一千討嗣祖。

translations.literal: Wan sent Shixing Administrator Wei Xizhen and Hawk-Raising General Yang Hongzhi leading masses of one thousand to punish Sizu.
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent Wei Xizhen, administrator of Shixing, and Yang Hongzhi, Hawk-Raising General, with one thousand men to suppress Sizu.

sentences.zh: 嗣祖亦遣眾出南康，與齊王世子合。

translations.literal: Sizu also sent masses out through Nankang to join the Prince of Qi's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Sizu also sent troops out through Nankang to join the Prince of Qi's heir.

sentences.zh: 希真等以義徒強盛，住廬陵不敢進。

translations.literal: Xizhen and others, because the righteous volunteers were powerful and flourishing, halted at Luling and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhen and his men, finding the loyalist forces too strong, halted at Luling and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史袁曇遠聞始興起義，遣將李萬周、陳伯紹率眾討嗣祖。

translations.literal: Guangzhou Inspector Yuan Tanyuan heard Shixing had raised righteous arms and sent generals Li Wanzhou and Chen Boshao leading masses to punish Sizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tanyuan, inspector of Guangzhou, heard that Shixing had risen for the court and sent Li Wanzhou and Chen Boshao with troops to suppress Sizu.

sentences.zh: 嗣祖遣兵戍湞陽，萬周亦築壘相守。

translations.literal: Sizu sent troops to garrison Zhenyang; Wanzhou also built stockades and held fast in mutual defense.
translations.idiomatic: Sizu sent troops to hold Zhenyang, and Wanzhou built fortifications and faced him in a stalemate.

sentences.zh: 嗣祖遣人誑萬周曰：「尋陽已平，臺遣劉勔為廣州，垂至。

translations.literal: Sizu sent someone to deceive Wanzhou, saying: "Xunyang has already been pacified; the Court has sent Liu Kan as Guangzhou inspector, about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Sizu sent a man to deceive Wanzhou, saying, "Xunyang has already fallen. The court has sent Liu Kan as inspector of Guangzhou, and he is about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 」萬周信之，便回還襲番禺，夜以長梯入城；

translations.literal: Wanzhou believed it, then turned back to strike Panyu, at night using long ladders to enter the city;
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhou believed him, turned back to strike Panyu, and entered the city at night on long ladders;

sentences.zh: 曇遠怯弱無防，聞萬周反，便徒跣出奔，萬周追斬之於城內。

translations.literal: Tanyuan was timid and weak and without defense; hearing Wanzhou had rebelled, he went out fleeing barefoot; Wanzhou pursued and beheaded him within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tanyuan was timid and unprepared. When he heard that Wanzhou had turned against him, he fled barefoot from the city. Wanzhou pursued him and cut him down inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史檀翼被代還至廣州，資貨鉅萬，萬周誣以為逆，襲而殺之。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou Inspector Tan Yi, having been replaced and returning to Guangzhou, had goods and valuables in the tens of thousands; Wanzhou slandered him as rebellious, struck him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yi, inspector of Jiaozhou, had been relieved of office and was returning through Guangzhou with immense wealth. Wanzhou falsely accused him of rebellion, attacked him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遂劫掠公私銀帛，藉略袁、檀珍寶，悉以自入。

translations.literal: He then plundered public and private silver and silk, seized and took Yuan and Tan's precious treasures, and all entered his own possession.
translations.idiomatic: He then looted public and private stores of silver and silk, seized the treasures of Yuan and Tan, and kept everything for himself.

sentences.zh: 袁顗悉雍州之眾，來赴尋陽。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi mustered all Yongzhou's masses and came to join at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi gathered the full strength of Yongzhou and marched to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 時孔道存為衛軍長史，行荊州事。

translations.literal: At the time Kong Daocun was Guards Army Chief Clerk, acting Jingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daocun was then chief clerk of the Guards Army and was acting for Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 琬以黃門侍郎劉道憲代之，以道存為侍中，行雍州事。

translations.literal: Wan used Yellow Gate Attendant Gentleman Liu Daoxian to replace him, and made Daocun Attendant-in-Chief, acting Yongzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wan replaced him with Liu Daoxian, Yellow Gate Attendant Gentleman, and made Daocun Attendant-in-Chief with authority over Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 柳元景之誅也，元景弟子世隆為上庸太守，民吏共藏匿之。

translations.literal: At the execution of Liu Yuanjing, Yuanjing's younger clansman disciple Shilong was Shangyong Administrator; the people and officials together concealed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuanjing was executed, his clansman Liu Shilong, who was administrator of Shangyong, was hidden by the local officials and people.

sentences.zh: 顗起兵，召世隆，不至。

translations.literal: When Yi raised troops, he summoned Shilong, but Shilong did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi raised his army, he summoned Shilong, but Shilong did not come.

sentences.zh: 顗既下，世隆乃合率蠻、宋二千餘人，起義於上庸，來襲襄陽。

translations.literal: After Yi had marched down, Shilong then combined and led Man and Song tribesmen, more than two thousand, raised righteous arms at Shangyong, and came to strike Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi marched south, Shilong gathered more than two thousand tribal warriors from the Man and Song peoples, rose at Shangyong, and marched to attack Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 道存遣將王式民、康元隆等迎擊於萬山，世隆大敗，還郡自守。

translations.literal: Daocun sent generals Wang Shimin, Kang Yuanlong, and others to meet and strike them at Wanshan; Shilong was greatly defeated and returned to his commandery to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daocun sent Wang Shimin, Kang Yuanlong, and others to meet them at Wanshan. Shilong was routed and withdrew to his commandery to defend himself.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之等與劉胡相持久不決，上又遣強弩將軍任農夫、振武將軍武會倉、冗從僕射全景文、軍主劉伯符等領兵繼至。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi and others with Liu Hu faced each other in prolonged stalemate without resolution; the Emperor again sent Strong Crossbow General Ren Nongfu, Quelling Martial General Wu Huicang, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary Quan Jingwen, army commander Liu Bofu, and others leading troops to follow and arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi and Liu Hu remained locked in stalemate. The Emperor then sent Ren Nongfu, Strong Crossbow General, Wu Huicang, Quelling Martial General, Quan Jingwen, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary, army commander Liu Bofu, and others with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 攸之繕治船舸，材板不周，計無所出。

translations.literal: Youzhi repaired and prepared boats and ships, but timber and planks were insufficient, and he had no plan to produce any.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi set about repairing his fleet, but timber and planking were short and he could find no remedy.

sentences.zh: 會琬送五千片榜供胡軍用，俄而風潮奔迅，榜捍突柵出江，胡等力不能制，自撞船艦，殺沒數十人，赴流而下，來泊攸之等營，於是材板大足。

translations.literal: It happened that Wan sent five thousand planks to supply Hu's army; presently wind and tide surged swiftly, the planks burst through the palisade out into the river; Hu and others could not control them by force, themselves collided with ships, killed and drowned several tens; they went with the current downstream, came to moor at Youzhi and others' camp, and thus timber and planks were greatly sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wan sent five thousand planks for Hu's army. Suddenly a fierce wind and tide drove the planks through the stockade and out into the river. Hu's men could not control them; the planks smashed into their own ships and killed or drowned several dozen men before drifting downstream to Youzhi's camp. Youzhi thus had all the timber he needed.

sentences.zh: 琬進袁顗都督征討諸軍事，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Wan advanced Yuan Yi to Supervisor of Military Affairs for the Punitive Campaign over all armies and granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Wan promoted Yuan Yi to supervisor of military affairs for the punitive campaign and granted him a full military band.

sentences.zh: 六月十八日，顗率樓船千艘，來入鵲尾，張興世建議越鵲尾上據錢溪，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the sixth month, Yi led tower ships by the thousand, came and entered Magpie Tail; Zhang Xingshi proposed crossing above Magpie Tail to seize Qian Creek and cut their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the sixth month, Yi entered Magpie Tail with a thousand tower ships. Zhang Xingshi proposed moving upstream beyond Magpie Tail to hold Qian Creek and cut the enemy's supply line.

sentences.zh: 胡累攻之，不能克，事在興世傳。

translations.literal: Hu repeatedly attacked him but could not overcome him; the affair is in Xingshi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Hu attacked him again and again but could not dislodge him; the full account is given in Zhang Xingshi's biography.

sentences.zh: 劉亮率所領至胡寨下，胡遣其副孫犀及張靈、焦度鐵騎五匹，越磵取亮，不能得，犀回馬去，亮使左右善射者夾射之，墜馬，斬犀首。

translations.literal: Liu Liang led his following to below Hu's stockade; Hu sent his deputy Sun Xi and Zhang Ling, Jiao Du with five iron cavalry mounts, crossing the ravine to seize Liang, but could not obtain him; Xi turned his horse to leave; Liang had attendants skilled at shooting shoot from both sides, Xi fell from his horse, and Liang beheaded Xi's head.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang led his men to Hu's camp. Hu sent his deputy Sun Xi with Zhang Ling and Jiao Du and five armored horsemen across a ravine to capture Liang, but they failed. As Xi turned to flee, Liang had skilled archers shoot at him from both sides. Xi fell from his horse, and Liang cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 張繼伯副馬可率所領來降。

translations.literal: Zhang Jibo's deputy Ma Ke led his following to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jibo's deputy Ma Ke led his troops over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 劉亮營寨，深入賊地，袁顗畏憚之，曰：「賊入我肝臟裏，何由得活！

translations.literal: Liu Liang encamped in stockades deep within rebel territory; Yuan Yi feared and respected him, saying: "The rebels have entered my liver and entrails—how can I live!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang built his camp deep in enemy territory. Yuan Yi was alarmed and said, "The enemy is inside my very vitals—how can we survive?"

sentences.zh: 」劉胡率輕舸四百，由鵲頭內路，欲攻錢溪。

translations.literal: Liu Hu led four hundred light boats by the inner route from Magpie Head, intending to attack Qian Creek.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu led four hundred light boats along the inner route from Magpie Head to attack Qian Creek.

sentences.zh: 既而謂其長史王念叔曰：「吾少習步戰，未閑水鬥。

translations.literal: Presently he said to his Chief Clerk Wang Nianshu: "From youth I practiced foot combat and am not skilled in water fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Then he said to his chief clerk Wang Nianshu, "I have practiced infantry fighting since youth and am not skilled in naval combat.

sentences.zh: 若步戰，恆在數萬人中，水戰在一舸之上，舸舸各進，不復相關，正在三十人中取，此非萬全之計，吾不為也。

translations.literal: In foot combat one is always among tens of thousands of men; in water combat one is atop a single boat, boat after boat advances separately and no longer relates to one another—the outcome rests on thirty men. This is not a plan of complete security; I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: In infantry battle I am always among tens of thousands of men. In a naval battle I stand on a single boat while each vessel advances on its own and the fleet no longer moves as one. Victory then depends on thirty men. That is no sure plan, and I will not undertake it."

sentences.zh: 」乃託瘧疾，住鵲頭不進。

translations.literal: He then pleaded malaria and halted at Magpie Head without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded malaria and remained at Magpie Head without advancing.

sentences.zh: 遣龍驤將軍陳慶領三百舸向錢溪，戒慶不須戰：「張興世、武會倉，吾之所悉，自當走耳。

translations.literal: He sent Dragon-Prancing General Chen Qing leading three hundred boats toward Qian Creek, admonishing Qing not to fight: "Zhang Xingshi and Wu Huicang are men I know well—they will flee on their own."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chen Qing, Dragon-Prancing General, with three hundred boats toward Qian Creek and told him not to fight. "Zhang Xingshi and Wu Huicang are men I know well—they will flee on their own."

sentences.zh: 」陳慶至錢溪，不敢攻。

translations.literal: When Chen Qing reached Qian Creek, he did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Qing reached Qian Creek, he did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 越錢溪，於梅根立寨。

translations.literal: He crossed beyond Qian Creek and built a stockade at Meigen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed beyond Qian Creek and built a stockade at Meigen.

sentences.zh: 胡別遣將王起領百舸攻興世，興世擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Hu separately sent General Wang Qi leading a hundred boats to attack Xingshi; Xingshi struck them and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu separately sent Wang Qi with a hundred boats to attack Xingshi, but Xingshi routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 胡率其餘舸馳還，謂顗曰：「興世營寨已立，不可卒攻，昨日小戰，未足為損。

translations.literal: Hu led his remaining boats galloping back and said to Yi: "Xingshi's stockade is already established and cannot be suddenly attacked; yesterday's small battle was insufficient to count as damage.
translations.idiomatic: Hu raced back with his remaining boats and told Yi, "Xingshi's camp is already established and cannot be taken in a sudden assault. Yesterday's skirmish was no real loss.

sentences.zh: 陳慶已與南陵、大雷諸軍共遏其上，大軍在此，鵲頭諸將又斷其下流，已墮圍中，不足復慮。

translations.literal: Chen Qing has already with Nanling, Dalei, and the rest of the armies jointly blocked them above; the great army is here; Magpie Head's generals again cut their lower stream—they have already fallen into encirclement and are not worth further concern."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qing, together with the armies at Nanling and Dalei, is already blocking them upstream. Our main force is here, and the generals at Magpie Head have cut them off downstream. They are already trapped, and there is nothing more to worry about."

sentences.zh: 」顗怒胡不戰，謂曰：「糧運梗塞，當如此何？

translations.literal: Yi was angry that Hu would not fight and said to him: "Grain transport is blocked and obstructed—what is to be done about this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi was furious that Hu would not fight and said, "Our grain route is cut. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 」胡曰：「彼尚得泝流越我而上，此運何以不得沿流越彼而下邪！

translations.literal: Hu said: "They can still go upstream against the current and pass above us—why cannot this transport go downstream along the current and pass below them!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "If they can still fight upstream past us, why cannot our supplies go downstream past them?"

sentences.zh: 」顗更使胡率步卒二萬，鐵馬一千，往攻興世。

translations.literal: Yi again had Hu lead twenty thousand foot soldiers and one thousand iron horses to go attack Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then ordered Hu to lead twenty thousand foot soldiers and one thousand armored horsemen to attack Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 休仁因此命沈攸之、吳喜、佼長生、劉靈遺、劉伯符等進攻濃湖，造皮艦十乘，拔其營柵，苦戰移日，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiuren on this account ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, Jiao Changsheng, Liu Lingyi, Liu Bofu, and others to advance and attack Nonghu, built ten leather-covered assault boats, pulled up their camp palisades, bitterly fought for a full day, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren therefore ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, Jiao Changsheng, Liu Lingyi, Liu Bofu, and the others to attack Lake Nong. They built ten leather-covered assault boats, tore up the enemy palisades, fought bitterly all day, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 顗被攻既急，馳信召胡令還。

translations.literal: Yi, being attacked with urgency, sent urgent message summoning Hu to return.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed by the attack, Yi sent an urgent summons for Hu to return.

sentences.zh: 張興世既據錢溪，江路岨斷，胡軍乏食，琬大送資糧，畏興世不敢下。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi having already seized Qian Creek, the river route was ruggedly cut off; Hu's army lacked food; Wan greatly sent supplies and grain, but feared Xingshi and did not dare descend.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Xingshi held Qian Creek, the river route was cut and Hu's army went hungry. Wan sent large supplies, but his men feared Xingshi and did not dare move downstream.

sentences.zh: 胡遣將迎之，為錢溪所破，資實覆沒都盡，燒米三十萬斛，胡眾駭懼。

translations.literal: Hu sent generals to meet them and was defeated by Qian Creek; supplies and provisions were overturned and drowned entirely; three hundred thousand hu of rice were burned; Hu's masses were terrified and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent men to escort the convoy, but they were defeated at Qian Creek. The supplies were lost entirely, three hundred thousand hu of rice were burned, and Hu's army was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 胡副張喜來降，說胡欲叛。

translations.literal: Hu's deputy Zhang Xi came to surrender and reported that Hu intended to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's deputy Zhang Xi surrendered and reported that Hu intended to defect.

sentences.zh: 八月二十四日，胡誑顗云：「更率步騎二萬，上取興世，兼下大雷餘餫。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month, Hu deceived Yi, saying: "I will again lead twenty thousand foot and cavalry, go up to take Xingshi, and also descend to Dalei's remaining grain stores."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month, Hu deceived Yi, saying, "I will lead twenty thousand foot and horse again to take Xingshi upstream and also seize the remaining grain at Dalei downstream."

sentences.zh: 」令顗悉度馬配之，其夜，委顗奔走，徑趣梅根。

translations.literal: He ordered Yi to transfer all horses to equip him; that night he abandoned Yi and fled, going straight to Meigen.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yi to give him every available horse. That night he abandoned Yi and fled straight for Meigen.

sentences.zh: 先令薛常寶辦船舸，悉撥南陵諸軍，燒大雷諸城而走。

translations.literal: He had first ordered Xue Changbao to prepare boats and ships, fully redeployed the Nanling armies, burned the Dalei cities, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He had already ordered Xue Changbao to prepare boats, pulled out all the Nanling garrisons, burned the towns at Dalei, and fled.

sentences.zh: 顗聞胡走，亦棄眾西奔，至青林見殺。

translations.literal: Yi heard Hu had fled, also abandoned his masses and fled west; reaching Qinglin he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi heard that Hu had fled, he too abandoned his army and fled west. He was killed at Qinglin.

sentences.zh: 胡率數百舸二萬人向尋陽，報子勛詐云：「袁顗已降，軍皆散，唯己率所領獨反。

translations.literal: Hu led several hundred boats and twenty thousand men toward Xunyang, reporting to Zixun falsely, saying: "Yuan Yi has already surrendered, the armies have all dispersed, only I leading my following alone have turned in revolt."
translations.idiomatic: Hu led several hundred boats and twenty thousand men toward Xunyang and falsely reported to Zixun, "Yuan Yi has surrendered, the armies have scattered, and I alone have turned against them with the men still under my command."

sentences.zh: 宜速處分，為一戰之資，當停據盆城，誓死不貳。

translations.literal: You ought quickly to settle affairs, make provision for one battle, ought halt and hold Pencheng, vowing death and no second loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Dispose of matters at once, gather what is needed for a single decisive battle, hold Pencheng as our base, and swear never to waver.

sentences.zh: 」乃於江外夜取沔口。

translations.literal: " Then at night beyond the river he seized Mian Ford.
translations.idiomatic: " That night he took Mian Ford from beyond the river.

sentences.zh: 琬聞胡去，惶擾無復計，呼褚靈嗣等謀之，並不知所出，唯云更集兵力，加賞五階，或云三階者。

translations.literal: Wan heard Hu had gone, in alarm and confusion with no plan left, summoned Chu Lingsi and others to deliberate; all did not know what to propose, only saying to gather military strength again, adding rewards by five ranks, or some saying three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan heard that Hu had departed, he panicked and could think of nothing. He called Chu Lingsi and others into council, but none could suggest a way forward—only proposals to regather troops and raise rewards by five ranks, or by three, depending on who spoke.

sentences.zh: 張悅始發兄子浩喪，乃稱疾呼琬計事，令左右伏甲帳後，戒之：「若聞索酒，便出。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue had just sent off mourning for his elder brother's son Hao; then feigning illness summoned Wan to discuss affairs, ordered attendants to lie in ambush with armor behind the tent, admonishing them: "If you hear wine requested, come out."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue had only just begun mourning for his nephew Hao when he feigned illness and summoned Wan to consult on affairs. He hid armed men behind the tent and instructed them, "When you hear me call for wine, come out."

sentences.zh: 」琬既至，悅曰：「卿首唱此謀，今事已急，計將安出？

translations.literal: " Wan having arrived, Yue said: "You first raised this plot—now affairs are urgent; what plan will you put forth?"
translations.idiomatic: " When Wan arrived, Yue said, "You were the first to urge this conspiracy. The crisis is upon us. What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 」琬曰：「正當斬晉安王，封府庫，以謝罪耳。

translations.literal: " Wan said: "Just ought to execute the Prince of Jin'an, seal the treasury storehouses, to beg pardon—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: " Wan said, "We should execute the Prince of Jin'an, seal the treasury, and offer that as our act of repentance."

sentences.zh: 」悅曰：「今日寧可賣殿下求活邪？

translations.literal: " Yue said: "Today could one sell the Prince to seek life?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yue said, "Would you sell His Highness today merely to save your own skin?"

sentences.zh: 」因呼求酒，再呼，左右震懾不能應。

translations.literal: " Then he called seeking wine; called again; attendants left and right, trembling in fear, could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: " He then called for wine, and called again, but his attendants were so terrified they could not answer.

sentences.zh: 第二子洵提刀走出，餘人續至，即斬琬。

translations.literal: The second son Xun, grasping a blade, walked out; the rest followed in succession, and immediately beheaded Wan.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Xun came out with a drawn blade, the others rushed in after him, and Wan was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 琬死時，年六十。

translations.literal: When Wan died, his years were sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was sixty when he died.

sentences.zh: 時中護軍劉順在座，驚起抱悅，左右人欲殺之，悅顧曰：「無關護軍。

translations.literal: At that time Central Protector of the Army Liu Shun was seated there; startled, he rose and embraced Yue; attendants wished to kill him; Yue looked back and said: "It has nothing to do with the Protector of the Army."
translations.idiomatic: Central Protector of the Army Liu Shun was present. Startled, he sprang up and shielded Yue. Yue's men moved to kill him, but Yue turned and said, "The Protector of the Army has no part in this."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Then they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " They held their hands.

sentences.zh: 潘欣之聞琬死，勒兵而至，悅使人語之曰：「鄧琬謀反，即已梟戮。

translations.literal: Pan Xin, hearing Wan had died, led troops and arrived; Yue sent a man to address him, saying: "Deng Wan plotted rebellion and has already been executed and his head displayed."
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Xinshi heard that Wan was dead, he marched his troops to the scene. Yue sent someone to tell him, "Deng Wan plotted rebellion and has already been put to death."

sentences.zh: 」欣之乃回還，取琬兒並殺之。

translations.literal: " Xin then turned back, took Wan's son and killed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: " Xinshi then withdrew, seized Wan's son, and killed him too.

sentences.zh: 悅因單舸齎琬首馳下，詣建安王休仁降。

translations.literal: Yue thereupon with a lone boat, carrying Wan's head, galloped downstream, went to Prince Jian'an Xiuren and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took a single boat, bearing Wan's head, raced downstream, and surrendered to Prince Jian'an Liu Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 蔡那子道淵，以父為太宗效力，被繫作部，因亂脫鏁入城，執子勛囚之。

translations.literal: Cai Na's son Daoyuan, because his father had served Taizong, was imprisoned as an artisan; taking advantage of the turmoil he broke his shackles and entered the city, seized Zi Xun and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Na's son Daoyuan had been imprisoned as a laborer because his father had served the founding emperor's house. Amid the chaos he broke his chains, entered the city, seized Zi Xun, and held him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之諸軍至江州，斬子勛於桑尾牙下，傳首京都。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi's various armies reached Jiang Province, beheaded Zi Xun beneath the gate at Sangwei, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's forces reached Jiang Province, they beheaded Zi Xun at the Sangwei gate and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉順及餘同逆，並伏誅。

translations.literal: Liu Shun and the rest who shared the rebellion, all suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shun and the other rebels were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 吳喜、張興世進向荊州，沈懷明向郢州，劉亮、張敬兒向雍州，孫超之向湘州，沈思仁、任農夫向豫章，所至皆平定。

translations.literal: Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi advanced toward Jing Province, Shen Huaiming toward Ying Province, Liu Liang and Zhang Jinger toward Yong Province, Sun Chao toward Xiang Province, Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu toward Yuzhang—all places they reached were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi marched on Jingzhou, Shen Huaiming on Yingzhou, Liu Liang and Zhang Jinger on Yongzhou, Sun Chaozhi on Xiangzhou, and Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu on Yuzhang. Everywhere they went, order was restored.

sentences.zh: 劉胡走入沔，眾稍散，比至石城，裁餘數騎。

translations.literal: Liu Hu fled into Mian; his masses gradually scattered; by the time he reached Shicheng, barely several riders remained.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu fled toward the Han River, his followers scattering until by the time he reached Shicheng only a handful of horsemen were left.

sentences.zh: 竟陵郡丞陳懷真，憲子也，聞胡經過，率數十人斷道邀之。

translations.literal: Jingling Commandery Assistant Chen Huaizhen, a son of Xian, hearing Hu would pass by, led several tens of men to cut the road and intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huaizhen, assistant magistrate of Jingling and son of Chen Xian, heard that Hu was passing through and led several dozen men to block the road and ambush him.

sentences.zh: 胡人馬既疲，自度不免，因隨懷真入城，告渴，與之酒，胡飲酒畢，引佩刀自刺，不死，斬首送京邑。

translations.literal: Hu's men and horses being already weary, he judged himself unable to escape, therefore followed Huaizhen into the city, declared thirst; wine was given him; when Hu had finished drinking he drew his girdle-knife and stabbed himself—did not die—so his head was cut off and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's men and horses were exhausted. Seeing no escape, he followed Huaizhen into the city and asked for water. They gave him wine. When he had drunk his fill, he drew his sword and stabbed himself but failed to die, so they beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 張興世弟僧產追胡，未至石城數十里，逢送胡首信，將還竟陵，殺懷真，竊有其功。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi's younger brother Sengchan pursued Hu; not yet reaching Shicheng by several tens of li, he met the messenger bearing Hu's head; intending to return to Jingling, he killed Huaizhen and stole the merit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi's younger brother Sengchan was pursuing Hu when, still several dozen li short of Shicheng, he met the messenger carrying Hu's head. He turned back toward Jingling, murdered Huaizhen, and claimed the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 郢州行事張沈、偽竟陵太守丘景先聞敗，變形為沙門逃走，追擒伏誅。

translations.literal: Ying Province acting administrator Zhang Shen and the false Jingling Administrator Qiu Jingxian, hearing of defeat, changed their appearance to become monks and fled; pursued, captured, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shen, acting administrator of Yingzhou, and Qiu Jingxian, the rebel-appointed magistrate of Jingling, heard of the defeat, disguised themselves as monks, and fled. They were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 荊州聞濃湖平，議欲更遣軍與郢州合勢，又欲斷據巴陵，經日不決。

translations.literal: Jing Province, hearing Nonghu was pacified, debated wishing again to send armies to join strength with Ying Province, and also wished to cut off and hold Baling—days passed without a decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou learned that Nonghu had fallen, its leaders debated whether to send more troops to join forces with Yingzhou or to seize and hold Baling. Days passed without a decision.

sentences.zh: 乃遣將趙道始於江津築壘，任演戍沙橋，諸門津要，皆有屯兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sent the general Zhao Daoshi to build ramparts at Jiang Ford, Ren Yan to garrison Shaqiao, and at every gate and strategic crossing there were garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: They sent General Zhao Daoshi to build fortifications at Jiang Ford, posted Ren Yan at Shaqiao Bridge, and stationed troops at every gate and strategic crossing.

sentences.zh: 人情轉離，將士漸逃散。

translations.literal: Human sentiment turned away; officers and soldiers gradually fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty crumbled and soldiers deserted in growing numbers.

sentences.zh: 更議奉子頊奔益州，就蕭惠開，典籤阮道預、邵宰不同，曰：「近奉別詔，諸藩若改迷歸順者，悉復本爵。

translations.literal: They debated again supporting Zi Xu in flight to Yi Province to join Xiao Huikai; Registrar Ruan Daoyu and Shao Zai disagreed, saying: "We have lately received a separate edict: all feudatories who correct their error and return to allegiance shall fully recover their former titles."
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed escorting Zi Xu to Yi Province to seek refuge with Xiao Huikai, but Registrar Ruan Daoyu and Administrator Shao Zai objected, saying, "We have just received a special edict promising that any prince who abandons rebellion and submits will have his original rank restored."

sentences.zh: 且任叔兒已斷白帝，楊僧嗣據梁州，雖復欲西，豈可得至。

translations.literal: " Moreover Ren Shuer has already cut off White Emperor City, Yang Sengsi holds Liang Province—even if we wish again to go west, how could we arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: " Besides, Ren Shuer already blocks White Emperor City and Yang Sengsi holds Liangzhou. Even if we wished to flee west, how could we get there?"

sentences.zh: 」道預、邵宰即與劉道憲解遣白丁，遣使歸罪。

translations.literal: " Daoyu and Shao Zai at once with Liu Daoxian released the common levies and sent envoys to declare guilt and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruan Daoyu and Shao Zai promptly joined Liu Daoxian in dismissing the conscripted militia and sent envoys to confess their crimes and submit.

sentences.zh: 荊州治中宗景、土人姚儉等勒兵入城，殺道憲、預、記室參軍鮑照，劫掠府庫，無復孑遺，執子頊以降。

translations.literal: Jing Province aide Zong Jing, local leader Yao Jian and others led troops into the city, killed Daoxian, Yu, and Secretariat Officer Bao Zhao, plundered the treasury until nothing single remained, seized Zi Xu and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Jing, the provincial aide, and local leaders such as Yao Jian led troops into the city, killed Liu Daoxian, Ruan Daoyu, and secretariat officer Bao Zhao, looted the treasury to the last item, seized Zi Xu, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧琬徵兵巴東，巴東太守羅寶稱辭以郡接凶蠻，兵力不足分。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Deng Wan was recruiting troops in Badong, Badong Administrator Luo Baocheng declined on the grounds that the commandery bordered fierce barbarians and military strength was insufficient to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Deng Wan was conscripting troops in Badong, Administrator Luo Baocheng refused, citing the commandery's frontier with hostile tribes and his lack of forces to spare.

sentences.zh: 巴東人任叔兒聚徒起義，遣信要寶稱，寶稱持疑未決，暴疾死。

translations.literal: A man of Badong, Ren Shuer, gathered followers and raised righteous arms, sent a message summoning Baocheng; Baocheng hesitated undecided, and died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shuer of Badong gathered a band and rose in revolt, sending word to summon Baocheng. Baocheng wavered, then died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 叔兒乃自號輔國將軍，引兵據白帝，殺寶稱二子，阻守三陝。

translations.literal: Shuer thereupon styled himself General Who Assists the State, led troops to hold White Emperor, killed Baocheng's two sons, and blocked and guarded the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: Shuer then declared himself General Who Assists the State, seized White Emperor City, killed both of Baocheng's sons, and blocked the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 蕭惠開遣費欣壽等五千人攻叔兒，叔兒與戰，大破之，斬欣壽。

translations.literal: Xiao Huikai sent Fei Xinshou and others, five thousand men, to attack Shuer; Shuer joined battle and greatly defeated them, beheading Xinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huikai sent Fei Xinshou with five thousand men against Shuer. Shuer met them in battle, routed the force, and beheaded Xinshou.

sentences.zh: 子頊又遣中兵參軍何康之領宜都太守，討叔兒。

translations.literal: Zi Xu again sent Central Army Staff Officer He Kangzhi to lead as Administrator of Yidu and attack Shuer.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xu then dispatched Central Army Staff Officer He Kangzhi as acting Administrator of Yidu to campaign against Shuer.

sentences.zh: 軍至陝口，為夷帥向子通所破，挺身走還。

translations.literal: The army reached the gorge mouth, was broken by the barbarian chieftain Xiang Zitong, and he alone escaped and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached the gorge entrance but was smashed by the tribal chieftain Xiang Zitong. Kangzhi alone fought his way out and fled back.

sentences.zh: 叔兒遂固白帝。

translations.literal: Shuer thereupon firmly held White Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuer then tightened his hold on White Emperor City.

sentences.zh: 孔道存知尋陽已平，遣使歸順。

translations.literal: Kong Daocun, learning Xunyang was already pacified, sent envoys to return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Daocun learned that Xunyang had fallen, he sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 尋聞柳世隆、劉亮當至，眾悉奔逃，道存及三子同時自殺。

translations.literal: Soon hearing Liu Shilong and Liu Liang were about to arrive, the masses all fled; Daocun and his three sons at the same time killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he heard that Liu Shilong and Liu Liang were approaching. His followers scattered. Daocun and his three sons killed themselves on the same day.

sentences.zh: 何慧文始謀同逆，其母禁之不從，母乃攜女歸江陵，遽嫁之。

translations.literal: He Huiwen at first plotted to join the rebellion; his mother forbade him and he would not obey; the mother thereupon took her daughter back to Jiangling and hastily married her off.
translations.idiomatic: He Huiwen had at first planned to join the rebellion, but his mother forbade it and he would not listen. She took his sister back to Jiangling and married her off at once.

sentences.zh: 慧文才兼將吏，幹略有施，雖害王應之，上特加原宥，吳喜宣旨赦之。

translations.literal: Huiwen's talent combined general and clerk; his administrative capacity had effect. Though he had harmed Wang Yingzhi, the emperor specially added pardon; Wu Xi proclaimed the edict and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwen was talented as both soldier and administrator and had shown real ability. Although he had killed Wang Yingzhi, the emperor specially ordered him spared, and Wu Xi came to announce the pardon.

sentences.zh: 慧文曰：「既陷逆節，手害忠義，天網雖復恢恢，何面目以見天下之士。

translations.literal: Huiwen said: "Having fallen into rebellious conduct, with my own hand harmed the loyal and righteous—the heavenly net though wide again, with what face could I meet the gentlemen of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Huiwen said, "I have committed treason and killed a loyal man with my own hand. However wide heaven's net may be, how could I face the gentlemen of the empire?"

sentences.zh: 」和藥將飲，門生覆之，乃不食而死。

translations.literal: " He mixed drugs and was about to drink; his students covered him; he then did not eat and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He mixed poison and was about to drink it, but his students restrained him, so he fasted until he died.

sentences.zh: 顏躍慮虞洽還都，說其始時同逆，密使人殺之。

translations.literal: Yan Yue, fearing Yu Qia would return to the capital and speak of his early complicity in rebellion, secretly sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yue feared that if Yu Qia returned to the capital he would reveal Yue's early role in the rebellion, and secretly had him killed.

sentences.zh: 初，淮南定陵人賈襲宗本縣已為劉胡所得，率二十人投沈攸之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jia Xizong of Dingling in Huainan—his home county had already been taken by Liu Hu—led twenty men to join Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jia Xizong of Dingling in Huainan, whose home district had fallen to Liu Hu, rallied twenty men and joined Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 攸之言之建安王休仁，休仁版為司徒參軍督護，使還鄉里招集，為胡所禽，以火炙之，問臺軍消息，一無所言，瞋目謂胡曰：「君稱兵內侮，窺覦神器，未聞奇謀遠略，而為炮烙之刑。

translations.literal: Youzhi spoke of him to Prince Jian'an Xiuren; Xiuren appointed him as Staff Officer to the Minister of State supervising defense, sent him back to his native place to recruit, was captured by Hu, was roasted by fire, was questioned about the court army's news, and said not a single thing, glaring and saying to Hu: "You have raised troops and insulted within, coveting the imperial regalia—you have not heard of wondrous stratagems or distant designs, yet you apply roasting punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi recommended him to Prince Jian'an Liu Xiuren, who appointed him staff officer to the Minister of State with supervisory duties and sent him home to raise troops. Hu captured him and tortured him with fire, demanding news of the imperial armies. Xizong said nothing. Glaring at Hu, he said, "You have taken up arms against the throne and covet the Mandate, yet I hear no grand strategy from you—only the torments of a petty tyrant."

sentences.zh: 僕本以身奉義，死亦何有。

translations.literal: I, your servant, from the start offered my body to righteousness; in death what is there?
translations.idiomatic: " I offered my life to the cause of righteousness from the first. What is death to me?"

sentences.zh: 」胡乃斬之。

translations.literal: " Hu thereupon beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu then had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 前軍典籤範道興志不同逆，為琬所誅，其餘奉順見害者，並為上所愍。

translations.literal: Former Forward Army Registrar Fan Daoxing's intent did not agree with rebellion; he was executed by Wan; the rest who submitted to allegiance yet were harmed—all were pitied by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Daoxing, former registrar of the Forward Army, had refused to join the rebellion and was executed by Wan. The emperor also mourned the others who had remained loyal yet were killed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「前鎮軍參軍督護范道興，朕之舊隸，經從北藩，徒役南畿，遭離命會，抱恩固節，受害群凶，言念純誠，良有憫愴。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Former Staff Officer to the General Who Guards the Army supervising defense Fan Daoxing was my old retainer, having followed the northern princely establishment, then served in the southern capital region, encountered the separation of fate's turning, embraced grace and held fast to integrity, suffered harm from the wicked host—speaking of his pure loyalty, there is truly deep pity."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Fan Daoxing, former supervisory staff officer to the General Who Guards the Army, was an old servant of Ours. He had followed the northern princely household and later served in the southern capital. Caught in this calamity, he repaid kindness with steadfast loyalty and was slain by the rebels. Remembering his pure devotion, We are deeply moved to pity."

sentences.zh: 可贈員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously appointed Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment.

sentences.zh: 南城令鮑法度、後軍典籤馮次民、永新令應生、新建令庫延寶、上饒令黃難等，違逆識順，同被誅滅，言念既往，宜在追榮。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Nancheng Bao Fadu, Rear Army Registrar Feng Cimin, Magistrate of Yongxin Ying Sheng, Magistrate of Xinjian Ku Yanbao, Magistrate of Shangrao Huang Nan and others, though the rebellion opposed them they recognized allegiance, together were executed and extinguished—speaking of what is past, they ought to receive posthumous honor.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Fadu, magistrate of Nancheng; Feng Cimin, registrar of the Rear Army; Ying Sheng, magistrate of Yongxin; Ku Yanbao, magistrate of Xinjian; Huang Nan, magistrate of Shangrao; and others recognized the right side amid rebellion and were all put to death. Remembering their past conduct, they too deserve posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 可贈生奉朝請，法度南臺御史，次民、延寶、難並員外將軍。」

translations.literal: They may be granted Gentleman Attending Court at Morning Audience in life; Fadu, Censor of the Southern Bureau; Cimin, Yanbao, and Nan all Outside-the-Regular-Appointment General."
translations.idiomatic: Let them receive the rank of Gentleman Attending Court at Morning Audience; Fadu shall be made Censor of the Southern Bureau; and Cimin, Yanbao, and Nan shall each be made Outside-the-Regular-Appointment General."

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「寧朔將軍、督豫州之梁郡諸軍事、豫州刺史、領南梁郡太守竟陵張興世，都統水軍，屢戰克捷，仍進斷賊上流錢溪，貴口苦戰，平定凶逆，今封南平郡作唐縣開國侯，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Xingshi of Jingling, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Liang Commandery in Yu Province, Inspector of Yu Province, and concurrent Administrator of Southern Liang Commandery, overall commanded the water armies, repeatedly in battle achieved victory, then advanced to cut the rebels' upper stream at Qianxi, at Guikou fought bitterly, pacified the wicked rebels—now enfeoff as Marquis Who Establishes a State of Zuotang County, Nanping Commandery, with a fief of one thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized, "Zhang Xingshi of Jingling, General Who Pacifies the North, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Liang commandery in Yu Province, Inspector of Yu Province, and concurrent Administrator of Southern Liang, commanded the fleet, won repeated victories, advanced to block the rebel upstream at Qianxi, fought bitterly at Guikou, and helped quell the rebellion. He is now to be enfeoffed as Marquis of Zuotang in Nanping commandery, with a fief of one thousand households."

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍、參司徒中直兵軍事廣平佼長生，同統水軍屢戰，及興世上據錢溪，長生獨距賊衝要，功次興世，今封武陵郡遷陵縣開國侯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Jiao Changsheng of Guangping, Staff Officer for the Minister of State's Central Direct Troops, together commanded the water armies in repeated battles; when Xingshi advanced to hold Qianxi, Changsheng alone blocked the rebels' vital crossing—merit second to Xingshi—now enfeoff as Marquis Who Establishes a State of Qianling County, Wuling Commandery, with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Changsheng of Guangping, General Who Pacifies the North and staff officer for the Minister of State's central direct troops, fought repeatedly with the fleet. When Xingshi seized Qianxi, Changsheng alone held the rebels' critical crossing. His merit ranked second only to Xingshi's. He is now to be enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianling in Wuling commandery, with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍、試守西陽太守吳興全景文、尚書比部郎吳縣孫超之、假輔國將軍、右衛將軍南彭城劉亮等三人，並經晉陵苦戰，景文、超之仍又北討破釜，水軍斷賊糧運，及經葛塚、石梁二處破賊，亮南伐經大戰，又最處險劇。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Quan Jingwen of Wuxing, Acting Administrator of Xiyang, Lang of the Comparison Section in the Imperial Secretariat Sun Chaozhi of Wu County, and Acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Right Guard Liu Liang of Nan Pengcheng—the three of them all passed through bitter fighting at Jinling; Jingwen and Chaozhi again northward attacked and broke Pofu, the water army cut the rebels' grain transport, and at Gezhong and Shiliang two places broke the rebels; Liang in the southern campaign passed through great battles and was moreover in the most dangerous and arduous positions.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingwen of Wuxing, General Who Pacifies the North and acting Administrator of Xiyang; Sun Chaozhi of Wu, lang of the Comparison Section in the Imperial Secretariat; and Liu Liang of Nan Pengcheng, Acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Right Guard—all three fought bitterly at Jinling. Jingwen and Chaozhi later attacked north and broke Pofu, the fleet cut rebel grain shipments, and they defeated the enemy at Gezhong and Shiliang. Liang fought through major battles in the southern campaign and bore the heaviest dangers.

sentences.zh: 景文今封西陽郡孝寧縣，超之封長沙郡羅縣，亮封順陽縣，並開國侯，食邑各六百戶。

translations.literal: Jingwen is now enfeoffed at Xiaoning County, Xiyang Commandery; Chaozhi at Luo County, Changsha Commandery; Liang at Shunyang County—all as Marquises Who Establish a State, each with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen is to be made Marquis of Xiaoning in Xiyang commandery, Chaozhi Marquis of Luo in Changsha commandery, and Liang Marquis of Shunyang, each with a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 假輔國將軍、驃騎司馬劉靈遺、寧朔將軍、右軍蔡那、寧朔將軍、屯騎校尉段佛榮等三人，統治攻道，並經苦戰，靈遺今封新野郡新野縣，那封始平郡平陽縣，佛榮封湘東郡臨蒸縣，並開國伯，食邑各五百戶。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Assists the State and Rapid Cavalry Major Liu Lingyi, General Who Pacifies the North and General of the Right Army Cai Na, and General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Duan Furong—the three of them governed the assault routes and all passed through bitter fighting; Lingyi is now enfeoffed at Xinye County, Xinye Commandery; Na at Pingyang County, Shiping Commandery; Furong at Linzheng County, Xiangdong Commandery—all as Earls Who Establish a State, each with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi, Acting General Who Assists the State and rapid-cavalry major; Cai Na, General Who Pacifies the North and general of the Right Army; and Duan Furong, General Who Pacifies the North and colonel of the Garrison Cavalry—all three directed assault routes through bitter fighting. Lingyi is to be made Earl of Xinye in Xinye commandery, Na Earl of Pingyang in Shiping commandery, and Furong Earl of Linzheng in Xiangdong commandery, each with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 假輔國將軍、左軍吳興沈懷明、龍驤將軍、積射將軍東平周盤龍、司徒參軍南彭城李安民等三人，懷明經晉陵破賊，又水軍南伐，統治攻道，盤龍雖不統軍，並經大戰，先登陷陳，安民又隨張興世遏斷錢溪，別統軍貴口破賊，今封懷明建安郡吳興縣，盤龍封晉安郡晉安縣，安民封建安郡邵武縣，並開國子，食邑各四百戶。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Left Army Shen Huaiming of Wuxing, Dragon-Prancing General and Target-shooting General Zhou Panlong of Dongping, and Staff Officer to the Minister of State Li Anmin of Nan Pengcheng—the three of them: Huaiming passed through Jinling and broke the rebels, again with the water army campaigned south, governed the assault routes; though Panlong did not overall command armies, he passed through great battles, first to ascend and break the formation; Anmin again followed Zhang Xingshi in blocking and cutting Qianxi, separately commanded armies at Guikou and broke the rebels—now enfeoff Huaiming at Wuxing County, Jian'an Commandery; Panlong at Jin'an County, Jin'an Commandery; Anmin at Shaowu County, Jian'an Commandery—all as Viscounts Who Establish a State, each with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming of Wuxing, Acting General Who Assists the State and general of the Left Army; Zhou Panlong of Dongping, Dragon-Prancing General and target-shooting general; and Li Anmin of Nan Pengcheng, staff officer to the Minister of State—Huaiming broke the rebels at Jinling and later led the fleet south along the assault routes. Though Panlong did not command an army himself, he fought through major battles and was first over the ramparts. Anmin followed Zhang Xingshi in blocking Qianxi and separately defeated the enemy at Guikou. Huaiming is to be made Viscount of Wuxing in Jian'an commandery, Panlong Viscount of Jin'an in Jin'an commandery, and Anmin Viscount of Shaowu in Jian'an commandery, each with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 假輔國將軍、游擊將軍彭城杜幼文、龍驤將軍、羽林監太原王穆之、龍驤將軍、羽林監濟北頓生、龍驤將軍、羽林監沛郡周普孫、員外散騎侍郎朱重恩等五人，幼文經晉陵破賊，在軍統攻道，南伐濃湖，普孫副沈攸之都統眾軍，穆之、生、重恩並南伐有功。

translations.literal: Acting General Who Assists the State and Mobile Campaign General Du Youwen of Pengcheng, Dragon-Prancing General and Forest of Feathers Supervisor Wang Muzhi of Taiyuan, Dragon-Prancing General and Forest of Feathers Supervisor Dun Sheng of Jibei, Dragon-Prancing General and Forest of Feathers Supervisor Zhou Pusun of Pei Commandery, and Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment Zhu Chong'en—the five of them: Youwen passed through Jinling and broke the rebels, in the army governed the assault routes, campaigned south to Nonghu; Pusun assisted Shen Youzhi in overall command of the mass of armies; Muzhi, Sheng, and Chong'en all had merit in the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Du Youwen of Pengcheng, Acting General Who Assists the State and mobile campaign general; Wang Muzhi of Taiyuan, Dragon-Prancing General and supervisor of the Forest of Feathers; Dun Sheng of Jibei, Dragon-Prancing General and supervisor of the Forest of Feathers; Zhou Pusun of Pei, Dragon-Prancing General and supervisor of the Forest of Feathers; and Zhu Chong'en, Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment—Youwen broke the rebels at Jinling, directed assault routes in the field, and campaigned south to Nonghu. Pusun served as Shen Youzhi's deputy in overall command. Muzhi, Sheng, and Chong'en all distinguished themselves in the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 今封幼文邵陵郡邵陽縣，穆之封衡陽郡衡山縣，生封始平郡武功縣，普孫封順陽郡清水縣，重恩封南海郡龍川縣，並開國男，食邑各三百戶。」

translations.literal: Now enfeoff Youwen at Shaoyang County, Shaoling Commandery; Muzhi at Hengshan County, Hengyang Commandery; Sheng at Wugong County, Shiping Commandery; Pusun at Qingshui County, Shunyang Commandery; Chong'en at Longchuan County, Nanhai Commandery—all as Barons Who Establish a State, each with a fief of three hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Youwen is to be made Baron of Shaoyang in Shaoling commandery, Muzhi Baron of Hengshan in Hengyang commandery, Sheng Baron of Wugong in Shiping commandery, Pusun Baron of Qingshui in Shunyang commandery, and Chong'en Baron of Longchuan in Nanhai commandery, each with a fief of three hundred households."

sentences.zh: 江方興以戰功為太子左衛率，賊未平，病卒，追封武當縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Jiang Fangxing, for military merit, was made Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard; the rebels were not yet pacified when he died of illness; posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Wudang County, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fangxing was made Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard for his battlefield merit, but died of illness before the rebels were fully subdued. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Wudang, with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 方興，濟陽考城人，衣冠之舊也。

translations.literal: Fangxing was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang, of an old gentry house.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing came from Kaocheng in Jiyang and was of an old eminent family.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍、虎賁中郎將董凱之，隨張興世破胡、白城，先登，封河隆縣子，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Dragon-Prancing General and Tiger-Gallant Central Commander Dong Kaizhi, following Zhang Xingshi in breaking Hu and Baicheng, was first to ascend, enfeoffed as Viscount of Helong County, with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Kaizhi, Dragon-Prancing General and tiger-gallant central commander, followed Zhang Xingshi in defeating Liu Hu at Baicheng and was first over the wall. He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Helong, with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 軍主張靈符，東南征討有功，封上饒縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Army Commander Zhang Lingfu, in the southeastern campaigns and punitive expeditions had merit, enfeoffed as Baron of Shangrao County, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingfu, an army commander, distinguished himself in the southeastern campaigns and was enfeoffed as Baron of Shangrao, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 前征北長兼行參軍楊覆，以貴口有功，封綏城縣男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Former Chief of the Northern Campaign Section and Acting Staff Officer Yang Fu, for merit at Guikou, enfeoffed as Baron of Suicheng County, with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, former chief of the northern campaign section and acting staff officer, was rewarded for his service at Guikou with enfeoffment as Baron of Suicheng, with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 追贈虞洽、檀玢給事中。

translations.literal: Yu Qia and Tan Bin were posthumously granted Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qia and Tan Bin were posthumously appointed Attendants Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 以李萬周為步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Li Wanzhou was made Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanzhou was appointed Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 陳懷真以斬劉胡功，追封永豐縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Chen Huaizhen, for the merit of beheading Liu Hu, was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Yongfeng County, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huaizhen was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Yongfeng, with a fief of three hundred households, for his part in killing Liu Hu.

sentences.zh: 段佛榮

translations.literal: Duan Furong
translations.idiomatic: Duan Furong

sentences.zh: 段佛榮，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Duan Furong was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Furong was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，自游擊將軍為輔師將軍、豫州刺史，蒞任清謹，為西土所安。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi, from Mobile Campaign General he became General Who Assists the Army and Inspector of Yu Province; on assuming office he was pure and cautious, and the western regions were reassured by him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi he rose from Mobile Campaign General to General Who Assists the Army and Inspector of Yu Province. His administration was scrupulous and restrained, and the western territories took comfort in his rule.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年，徵為散騎常侍，領長水校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, he was summoned as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Colonel of the Ever-Flowing Waters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, he was recalled to court as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Colonel of the Ever-Flowing Waters.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷衛尉，領右軍將軍，未拜，復出為冠軍將軍、南豫州刺史、歷陽太守。
