translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Commandant of the Guards and concurrent General of the Right Army; before receiving appointment he was again sent out as General Who Conquers Champions, Inspector of Southern Yu Province, and Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Commandant of the Guards with concurrent appointment as General of the Right Army, but before he could take up that post he was sent out again as General Who Conquers Champions, Inspector of Southern Yu Province, and Administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，追贈前將軍，改封雲杜縣，諡曰烈侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died; posthumously granted Forward General, his fief changed to Yundu County, posthumous title Marquis Lie.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died. He was posthumously made Forward General, his fief was changed to Yundu county, and he was given the posthumous title Marquis Lie.

sentences.zh: 劉靈遺

translations.literal: Liu Lingyi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi

sentences.zh: 劉靈遺，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Lingyi was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi was a native of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，自輔師將軍、淮南太守，為南豫州刺史、歷陽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui, from General Who Assists the Army and Administrator of Huainan he became Inspector of Southern Yu Province and Administrator of Liyang, his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhui he was promoted from General Who Assists the Army and Administrator of Huainan to Inspector of Southern Yu Province and Administrator of Liyang, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，徵為散騎常侍，領步兵校尉、南蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrent Colonel of the Footsoldiers and Administrator of Southern Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, with concurrent appointment as Colonel of the Footsoldiers and Administrator of Southern Lanling.

sentences.zh: 病卒，諡曰壯侯。

translations.literal: He died of illness; posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 袁顗，字景章，陳郡陽夏人，太尉淑兄子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Yan, styled Jingzhang, was a man of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, a nephew of the Grand Minister Shu on his elder brother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan, whose courtesy name was Jingzhang, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery. He was a nephew of Grand Minister Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 父洵，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Xun was Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had served as Administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 顗初為豫州主簿，舉秀才，不行。

translations.literal: Yan at first was Chief Clerk of Yu Province, was recommended as a Cultivated Talent, and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yan began as chief clerk of Yu Province, was recommended as a Cultivated Talent, and declined the summons.

sentences.zh: 後補始興王濬後軍行參軍，著作佐郎，廬陵王紹南中郎主簿，世祖征虜、撫軍主簿，廬江太守，尚書都官郎，江夏王義恭驃騎記室參軍，汝陰王文學，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Acting Staff Officer of the Rear Army under Prince of Shixing Jun, Assistant in the Composition Section, Chief Clerk to the Southern Central Commander under Prince of Luling Shao, Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians and to the General Who Pacifies the Army under Shizu, Administrator of Lujiang, Lang of the Ministry Section in the Imperial Secretariat, Secretariat Officer to the Rapid Cavalry General under Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Literary Scholar under Prince of Ruyin, and Groom-in-Waiting to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Prince of Shixing Liu Jun as acting staff officer of the rear army, as assistant in the Composition Section, as chief clerk to the southern central commander under Prince of Luling Liu Shao, as chief clerk to the campaigns of Emperor Xiaowu, as Administrator of Lujiang, as lang of the Ministry Section in the Imperial Secretariat, as secretariat officer to Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong, as literary scholar under Prince of Ruyin, and as groom-in-waiting to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時顗父為吳郡，顗隨父在官。

translations.literal: At that time Yan's father was in Wu Commandery, and Yan followed his father in office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his father was serving in Wu commandery, and Yan accompanied him there.

sentences.zh: 值元兇弑立，安東將軍隨王誕舉兵入討，板顗為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: It happened that the prime culprit murdered and enthroned himself; General Who Pacifies the East Prince of Sui Dan raised troops to enter and punish; Yan was appointed on commission as Advisory Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper murdered the emperor and seized the throne, Prince of Sui Liu Dan, General Who Pacifies the East, raised an army to punish him, and Yan was commissioned as advisory staff officer.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除正員郎，晉陵太守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was appointed Regular Lang and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Regular Lang and Administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，服闋，為中書侍郎，又除晉陵太守，襲南昌縣五等子。

translations.literal: He encountered his father's mourning; when mourning ended he became Secretariat Gentleman of the Central Secretariat, again was appointed Administrator of Jinling, and inherited the fifth-rank Viscount of Nanchang County.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death and the mourning period, he became Gentleman of the Central Secretariat, was again made Administrator of Jinling, and inherited the fifth-rank viscounty of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，除東海王禕平南司馬、尋陽太守，行江州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he was appointed Pacification-of-the-South Major under Prince of Donghai Yi, Administrator of Xunyang, and acting administrator of Jiang Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he was made Pacification-of-the-South major under Prince of Donghai Liu Yi, Administrator of Xunyang, with acting charge of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 復為義陽王昶前軍司馬，太守如故。

translations.literal: Again he became Forward Army Major under Prince of Yiyang Chang, his administrator post as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made forward-army major under Prince of Yiyang Liu Chang, retaining his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 昶尋罷府，司馬職解，加寧朔將軍，改太守為內史。

translations.literal: Chang soon closed his princely establishment, the major's office was dissolved, Yan was added as General Who Pacifies the North, and Administrator was changed to Interior Governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang's princely establishment was dissolved, Yan's major's post ended. He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, and his title of administrator was changed to interior governor.

sentences.zh: 復為尋陽王子房冠軍司馬，將軍如故，行淮南、宣城二郡事。

translations.literal: Again he became Conquest-of-Champions Major under Prince of Xunyang Zifang, his generalship as before, acting in the affairs of Huainan and Xuancheng two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made conquest-of-champions major under Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang, retaining his general's rank, with acting charge of Huainan and Xuancheng commanderies.

sentences.zh: 五年，召為太子中庶子，御史中丞，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned as Central Aide to the Crown Prince, Imperial Censor, and concurrent Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to serve as central aide to the crown prince and imperial censor, with concurrent appointment as chief rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 明年，除晉安王子勛鎮軍長史、襄陽太守，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Army Aide to the General Who Pacifies the Army under Prince of Jin'an Zixun, Administrator of Xiangyang, and added as General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed army aide to the pacification general under Prince of Jin'an Liu Zixun and Administrator of Xiangyang, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 未行，復為永嘉王子仁左軍長史、廣陵太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Before departing he was again made Army Aide to the Left Army under Prince of Yongjia Ziren, Administrator of Guangling, his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he was reassigned as army aide to the left army under Prince of Yongjia Liu Ziren and Administrator of Guangling, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 未拜，復為侍中，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before receiving appointment he was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent General of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume that office, he was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary with concurrent appointment as General of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 大明末，新安王子鸞以母嬖有盛寵，太子在東宮多過失，上微有廢太子立子鸞之意，從容頗言之。

translations.literal: At the end of Daming, Prince of Xin'an Ziluan, because his mother as a favorite had abundant favor, and the crown prince in the Eastern Palace had many faults, the emperor slightly had the intent to depose the crown prince and establish Ziluan, and in easy conversation spoke of it considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daming era, Prince of Xin'an Liu Ziluan's mother enjoyed extraordinary favor at court. The crown prince had committed many faults in the Eastern Palace, and the emperor began to consider deposing him in favor of Ziluan, speaking of the idea openly in conversation.

sentences.zh: 顗盛稱太子好學，有日新之美。

translations.literal: Yan greatly praised the crown prince's love of learning, having the beauty of daily renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan spoke at length in praise of the crown prince's love of learning and his daily improvement.

sentences.zh: 世祖又以沈慶之才用不多，言論頗相蚩毀，顗又陳慶之忠勤有幹略，堪當重任。

translations.literal: The emperor also held that Shen Qingzhi's talent and usefulness were limited, and their remarks mutually disparaged each other; Yan again stated that Qingzhi was loyal, diligent, and resourceful, fit to bear heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also considered Shen Qingzhi of limited ability, and their talk ran to mutual disparagement; yet Yan again urged that Qingzhi was loyal, diligent, and capable of strategy, fit for a weighty post.

sentences.zh: 由是前廢帝深感顗，慶之亦懷其德。

translations.literal: Hence the Former Deposed Emperor came to feel deeply toward Yan, and Qingzhi likewise cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Former Deposed Emperor formed a strong regard for Yan, and Qingzhi in turn was grateful for his favor.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，誅群公，欲引進顗，任以朝政，遷為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe, when the mass of nobles were executed, he wished to advance Yan and entrust him with court administration, promoting him to Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe, after the slaughter of the great ministers, he meant to bring Yan forward and charge him with state affairs, promoting him to Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 又下詔曰：「宗社多故，釁因冢司，景命未淪，神祚再乂，自非忠謀密契，豈伊克殄。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued, saying: "The altars of state have many troubles; the cause of strife lies in the chief minister. The mandate of Heaven is not yet fallen; the divine throne is restored once more. Unless there are loyal plans in secret accord, how could this be extinguished?"
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "The realm has suffered many calamities; the breach arose from the chief minister. Heaven's mandate is not yet spent; the sacred succession is renewed. Without loyal counsel in secret union, how could the evil be ended?"

sentences.zh: 侍中祭酒、領前軍將軍、新除吏部尚書顗，游擊將軍、領著作郎、兼尚書左丞徐爰，誠心內款，參聞嘉策，匡贊之效，寔監朕懷。

translations.literal: Yan, Attendant-in-Ordinary Libationer, concurrent General of the Forward Army, and newly appointed Minister of the Civil Service, together with Xu Ai, Mobile Campaign General, concurrent Gentleman of the Composition Bureau and Acting Left Assistant in the Imperial Secretariat—all were sincere within, participated in hearing excellent plans; the effect of their support and praise truly oversaw Our heart's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, libationer among the attendants-in-ordinary, concurrent General of the Forward Army, and newly appointed Minister of the Civil Service, and Xu Ai, Mobile Campaign General, concurrent Gentleman of the Composition Bureau and acting Left Assistant in the Imperial Secretariat, were inwardly sincere, joined in excellent counsel, and their aid in governance was truly before Our mind.

sentences.zh: 宜甄茅社，以獎義槩。

translations.literal: They ought to be granted fief and state altars to reward righteous resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Let them be granted fiefs and state altars to reward their righteous resolve.

sentences.zh: 顗可封新隆縣子，爰可封吳平縣子，食邑各五百戶。

translations.literal: Yan may be enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinlong County; Xu Ai may be enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuping County, each with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yan shall be enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinlong, Xu Ai as Viscount of Wuping, each with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 」俄而意趣乖異，寵待頓衰。

translations.literal: " Before long their aims diverged, and favor and treatment abruptly declined.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon their inclinations fell out of step, and imperial favor sharply waned.

sentences.zh: 始令顗與沈慶之、徐爰參知選事，尋復反以為罪，使有司糾奏，坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: At first Yan was ordered with Shen Qingzhi and Xu Ai to participate in managing selections; soon afterward this was turned into a crime, the relevant offices were made to impeach him, and he was punished by serving in office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yan, Shen Qingzhi, and Xu Ai were ordered to share in managing appointments; soon this was turned against him as a crime, the relevant offices impeached him, and he was reduced to serving in plain clothes while retaining his post.

sentences.zh: 從幸湖熟，往反數日，不被喚召。

translations.literal: On an imperial progress to Hushu, going back and forth for several days, he was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Hushu, Yan went back and forth for several days without being called to audience.

sentences.zh: 顗慮及禍，詭辭求出，沈慶之為顗固陳，乃見許。

translations.literal: Yan, fearing disaster, used specious words to request departure; Shen Qingzhi strongly pleaded on Yan's behalf, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing ruin, Yan made a pretext to ask to leave office; Shen Qingzhi argued firmly on his behalf, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 除建安王休仁安西長史、襄陽太守，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Army Aide to the Pacification-of-the-West under Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, Administrator of Xiangyang, with the additional rank of General Who Conquers Champions.
translations.idiomatic: He was made army aide to the pacification-of-the-west under Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren and Administrator of Xiangyang, with the additional rank of General Who Conquers Champions.

sentences.zh: 休仁不行，即以顗為使持節、督雍、梁、南北秦四州、郢州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Xiuren did not take up the post; Yan was thereupon made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Yong, Liang, Northern and Southern Qin four provinces and for Jingling and Sui two commanderies in E Province, concurrent Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yong, his general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuren declined to go, Yan was at once made bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs for Yong, Liang, Northern and Southern Qin, and for Jingling and Sui in E Province, concurrent colonel pacifying the barbarians, and Inspector of Yong, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 顗舅蔡興宗謂之曰：「襄陽星惡，豈可冒邪？

translations.literal: Yan's maternal uncle Cai Xingzong said to him, "The stars are ill-omened at Xiangyang—how can you brave them?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan's uncle Cai Xingzong said to him, "The stars are inauspicious over Xiangyang. How can you risk it?"

sentences.zh: 」顗曰：「白刃交前，不救流矢，事有緩急故也。

translations.literal: " Yan said, "With naked blades before one, one does not ward off stray arrows—affairs have their urgent and their slow."
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "When blades are crossed before you, you do not trouble yourself with stray arrows. There is a time for urgency and a time for delay."

sentences.zh: 今者之行，本願生出虎口。

translations.literal: The purpose of this journey now is simply to escape the tiger's jaws alive.
translations.idiomatic: This journey is meant only to let me walk out of the tiger's jaws alive.

sentences.zh: 且天道遼遠，何必皆驗，如其有徵，當脩德以禳之耳。

translations.literal: Moreover the Way of Heaven is remote—why must every sign be fulfilled? If there should be omens, one ought to cultivate virtue to avert them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is far off; why must every omen come true? If signs appear, one should cultivate virtue to avert them.

sentences.zh: 」於是狼狽上路，恆慮見追，行至尋陽，喜曰：「今始免矣！

translations.literal: " Thereupon he set out in disarray on the road, constantly fearing pursuit; when he reached Xunyang he rejoiced and said, "Now at last I am safe!"
translations.idiomatic: " He then took the road in disarray, ever fearing pursuit. Reaching Xunyang, he said in delight, "Now at last I am free!"

sentences.zh: 」與鄧琬款狎相過，常請間，必盡日窮夜。

translations.literal: " With Deng Wan he became intimate in frequent visits, often requesting private audience, and always stayed from dawn till night.
translations.idiomatic: " He grew intimate with Deng Wan, visited him constantly, often asked for private meetings, and would stay from dawn through the night.

sentences.zh: 顗與琬人地本殊，眾知其有異志矣。

translations.literal: Yan and Wan were utterly unlike in birth and station; the multitude knew he harbored a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Wan differed utterly in origin and standing, and everyone knew he had turned his mind elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 太宗使朝士與顗書曰：

translations.literal: The emperor had court gentlemen write to Yan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had court gentlemen write to Yan, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫夷陂相因，興革遞數，或多難而固其國，或殷憂而啟聖明，此既著於前史，亦彰於聞見。

translations.literal: "Level ground and steep banks succeed one another; rise and fall follow in turn. Some states are strengthened through many hardships; some sage rulers are awakened through deep sorrow. This is already set forth in former histories and also clear in what we have heard and seen."
translations.idiomatic: "Low ground and steep banks follow one another; rise and fall come in succession. Some states are made firm through many hardships; some sage rulers are awakened through deep sorrow. This is written in the histories of old and plain to those who hear and see."

sentences.zh: 王室不造，昏凶肆虐，神鼎將淪，宗稷幾泯，幸天未亡宋，乾曆有歸。

translations.literal: "The royal house was ill-fated; the wicked and violent ran rampant; the sacred vessel was about to sink; the altars of state nearly perished—fortunately Heaven had not yet destroyed Song, and the heavenly succession had a place to return."
translations.idiomatic: "The royal house was ill-starred; the wicked and violent held sway; the sacred vessel was near foundering; the altars of state were nearly extinguished—yet Heaven had not yet destroyed Song, and the heavenly succession found its way home."

sentences.zh: 主上體自聖文，繼明作睿，而辱均牖里，屯逾夏臺。

translations.literal: "Our lord in person embodies sacred culture and succeeds the bright in becoming wise, yet suffered disgrace equal to Youli and hardship surpassing the Xia Tower."
translations.idiomatic: "Our lord embodies sacred learning and succeeds to enlightened rule, yet suffered shame like that of the Zhou king in Youli and hardship greater than imprisonment in the Xia Tower."

sentences.zh: 既天地俱憤，義勇同奮，克殄鯨鯢，三靈更造，應天順民，爰集寶命，四海屬息肩之歡，華戎見來蘇之泰。

translations.literal: "When Heaven and Earth alike were enraged and the righteous rose together, the whale and kraken were destroyed, the three spirits were remade, Heaven was answered and the people followed, and the precious mandate was gathered; within the four seas all wished to rest their shoulders; among Chinese and barbarians all saw the peace of renewal."
translations.idiomatic: "When Heaven and Earth shared in wrath and the righteous rose as one, the great evils were cut down, the three spirits were remade, the mandate answered Heaven and followed the people, and the precious throne was secured. The four seas longed to lay down their burdens; Chinese and barbarians alike saw renewal."

sentences.zh: 吾等獲免刀鋸，僅全首領，復身奉惟新，命承亨運，緩帶談笑，擊壤聖世。

translations.literal: "We have escaped the blade and barely kept our heads, again in person serving the renewal, our lives receiving a flourishing fortune, loosening our belts in laughter, beating the clods in a sage age."
translations.idiomatic: "We were spared the blade and kept our heads, again serving the new order in person, our lives granted a flourishing age—we loosen our belts in talk and beat the clods in a sage reign."

sentences.zh: 汝雖劬勞於外，跡阻京師，然心期所寄，江、漢何遠。

translations.literal: "Though you toil abroad and your tracks are blocked from the capital, yet what the heart looks to is near—how far are the Yangtze and the Han?"
translations.idiomatic: "Though you labor abroad and your steps cannot reach the capital, what the heart rests on is near—what distance are the Yangtze and the Han?"

sentences.zh: 自九江告變，皆謂鄧氏狂惑，比日國言藉藉，頗塵吾子。

translations.literal: "Since the alarm at Jiujiang, all have said the Deng clan was mad and deluded; of late the talk of the realm is clamorous and has somewhat stained you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: "Since the rising at Jiujiang, all have called the Dengs mad; lately the talk of the realm has been loud, and it has somewhat touched you, sir."

sentences.zh: 道路之議，豈其或然，聞此之日，能無駭惋。

translations.literal: "Can the talk of the road be so? On the day this was heard, how could one not be struck with shock and regret?"
translations.idiomatic: "Can gossip on the road be true? When this was heard, who could not be shaken with shock and regret?"

sentences.zh: 凶人反道敗德，日夜滋深，昵近狡慝，取謀豺虎，非惟毒流外物，惡積中朝，乃欲毀陵邑，虐崇憲，燒宗廟，鹵御物，然後蕩覆京都，必使蘭蕕俱盡。

translations.literal: "The wicked man turns from the Way and ruins virtue, daily growing deeper, drawing near crafty villains and taking counsel from tiger and wolf. Not only does poison flow to things outside; evil accumulates within the court. He would destroy the imperial tombs, abuse the honored statutes, burn the ancestral temples, seize the imperial goods, and then overturn the capital—he would make orchid and artemisia perish together."
translations.idiomatic: "The wicked man turns from the Way and ruins virtue, growing worse day by day, drawing near the crafty and taking counsel from wolves. His poison is not only abroad; his evil piles up within the court. He would destroy the imperial tombs, abuse the honored laws, burn the ancestral temples, seize the imperial treasures, then overturn the capital and make the noble and the base perish together."

sentences.zh: 自非聖上廟筭靈圖，俛眉遜避，維持內外，擁衛臣下，則赤縣為戎，百姓其魚矣。

translations.literal: "Unless the sage lord's temple calculations and numinous designs, bowing his brows and yielding in avoidance, upheld inner and outer and shielded his ministers below, the red land would have become a battlefield and the hundred surnames would have been fish on the chopping block."
translations.idiomatic: "Had not the sage lord's temple calculations and numinous designs, yielding and holding back, sustained court and camp and shielded his ministers below, the realm would have become a battlefield and the people fish on the block."

sentences.zh: 此事此理，寧可孰念！

translations.literal: "On this matter and this principle, how can one dwell in thought alone!"
translations.idiomatic: "On this matter and this principle—how can one weigh it only in private thought?"

sentences.zh: 既天道輔順，謳歌有奉，高祖之孫，文皇之子，德洞九幽，功貫三曜，匡拯家國，提毓黔首，若不子民南面，將使神器何歸。

translations.literal: "Since Heaven's Way assists the compliant and songs of praise have a lord, a grandson of the founding emperor and a son of the civilizing emperor—his virtue penetrates the nine shades, his merit runs through the three luminaries, saving and raising the house and state and nurturing the black-headed people—if he does not face south as parent to the people, to whom would the sacred vessel go?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now that Heaven's Way aids the righteous and songs of praise have their lord—a grandson of the founder and son of the civilizing emperor, whose virtue reaches the nine shades and whose merit spans the three lights, who rescued the house and state and nurtured the people—if he does not face south as ruler, to whom should the sacred vessel go?"

sentences.zh: 而群小構慝，妄生窺覬，成軫惑燕，貫高亂趙，讒人罔極，自古有之。

translations.literal: "Yet petty men weave malice and rashly harbor designs of spying; like Cheng Zhuan who misled Yan and Guan Gao who disturbed Zhao, slanderers know no limit—this has existed from antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet petty men weave malice and rashly harbor designs; as Cheng Zhuan misled Yan and Guan Gao disturbed Zhao, slander knows no limit—this has been so since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 汝中京冠冕，儒雅世襲，多見前載，縣鑒忠邪，何遠遺郎中之清軌，近忘太尉之純槩。

translations.literal: "You are the crown of the central capital, steeped in Confucian learning through generations, having seen much in former records and able to mirror loyalty and treachery—why abandon at a distance the clear track of the Master of Writing and forget at hand the pure resolve of the Grand Marshal?"
translations.idiomatic: "You are the ornament of the central capital, heir to learning through generations, well read in former records and able to mirror loyalty and treachery—why cast away afar the clear path of the Master of Writing and forget close at hand the pure resolve of the Grand Marshal?"

sentences.zh: 相與，或群從舅甥，或姻婭周款，一旦胡、越，能無悵恨。

translations.literal: "Among us, some are cousins and uncles and nephews, some are kin by marriage and close in affection—once suddenly separated like Hu and Yue, how could there be no regret?"
translations.idiomatic: "Among us are cousins and uncles and nephews, and kin by marriage close in affection—if suddenly sundered like foreign lands, how could there be no sorrow?"

sentences.zh: 若疑誑所至，邪詖無窮，汝當誓眾奮戈，翦此朝食。

translations.literal: "If suspicion and deceit have reached you and evil slander is endless, you ought to swear the host and raise weapons and cut off this morning's meal."
translations.idiomatic: "If suspicion and deceit have reached you and slander is endless, you should swear the host, take up arms, and destroy this morning's foe."

sentences.zh: 若自延過聽，迷塗未遠，聖上臨物以仁，接下以愛，豈直雍齒先封，乃當射鉤見相矣！

translations.literal: "If you yourself prolong a generous hearing and have not strayed far from the path, the sage lord in facing things uses benevolence and in receiving those below uses love—is it only Yong Chi who was enfeoffed first? You too would be received like the one who shot the hook!"
translations.idiomatic: "If you yourself still keep to a generous hearing and have not strayed far, the sage lord faces things with benevolence and receives those below with love—is Yong Chi's early enfeoffment alone the model? Even he who shot the hook was received!"

sentences.zh: 當由力窘跡屈，丹誠未亮邪。

translations.literal: "Perhaps it is because strength is strained and tracks are bent that your red loyalty has not yet shone forth."
translations.idiomatic: "Perhaps because your strength is strained and your path bent, your loyal heart has not yet been made clear."

sentences.zh: 跂予南服，寤寐延首，若反棹沿流，歸誠鳳闕，錫珪開宇，非爾而誰。

translations.literal: "We look south in longing, waking and sleeping with uplifted head. If you turn your oars and follow the current, return in loyalty to the phoenix gate, grant of jade and opening of territory—who but you?"
translations.idiomatic: "We gaze south in longing, waking and sleeping with raised heads. If you turn your oars with the current and return in loyalty to the imperial gate, jade grants and broad domains—who but you shall receive them?"

sentences.zh: 吾等並過荷曲慈，俱叨非服，紆金拖玉，改觀蓬門，入奉舜、禹之渥，出見羲、唐之化，雍容揄揚，信白駒空谷之時也。

translations.literal: "We have all overborne received gracious favor, all undeservedly worn rank, trailing gold and dragging jade, changing the view of our humble gates, entering to receive the bounty of Shun and Yu, going out to see the transformation of Xi and Tang, easy in bearing and praised in song—truly the time of the white colt in the empty valley."
translations.idiomatic: "We have all over-received gracious favor and worn rank beyond our desert, trailing gold and dragging jade, so that our humble gates look changed; entering we receive the bounty of Shun and Yu, going out we see the transformation of Xi and Tang—at ease and praised in song, truly like the white colt in the empty valley."

sentences.zh: 奈何毀擲先基，自蹈凶戾，山門蕭瑟，松庭誰掃，言念楚路，豈不思父母之邦。

translations.literal: "Why then cast away the former foundation and tread yourself into wicked violence—the mountain gate desolate, who sweeps the pine courtyard? Speaking of the road to Chu, do you not think of the land of your parents?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why then throw away the former foundation and tread yourself into wickedness—the mountain gate desolate, who sweeps the pine courtyard? Thinking of the road to Chu, do you not long for your parents' land?"

sentences.zh: 幸納惡石，以蠲美疹。

translations.literal: "We hope you will accept harsh counsel to remove fair blemishes."
translations.idiomatic: "Accept harsh counsel to remove what is flawed."

sentences.zh: 裁書表意，爾其圖之。

translations.literal: "This letter states our intent—consider it well."
translations.idiomatic: "This letter states our intent. Consider it well."

sentences.zh: 時尚書右僕射蔡興宗是顗舅，領軍將軍袁粲是顗從父弟，故書云群從舅甥也。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Xingzong, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was Yan's uncle, and Yuan Can, General of the Palace Gate, was Yan's cousin on the father's side—hence the letter speaks of cousins and uncles and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cai Xingzong, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was Yan's uncle, and Yuan Can, General of the Palace Gate, was Yan's paternal cousin—hence the letter's mention of cousins and uncles and nephews.

sentences.zh: 子勛徵顗下尋陽，遣侍中孔道存行雍州事。

translations.literal: Zixun summoned Yan down to Xunyang and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Kong Daocun to act in Yong Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixun summoned Yan down to Xunyang and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Kong Daocun to handle Yong Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 顗乃率眾馳下，使子戩領家累俱還。

translations.literal: Yan then led his host racing downstream and sent his son Zhan to bring the household dependents back as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then led his troops racing downstream and sent his son Zhan to bring the whole household back with him.

sentences.zh: 時劉胡屯鵲尾，久不決。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Hu was encamped at Quewei, and for a long time the issue was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Hu was encamped at Quewei, and the outcome remained long undecided.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年夏，加顗都督征討諸軍事，給鼓吹一部，率樓船千艘，戰士二萬，來入鵲尾。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Taishi, Yan was added as Supervisor of Military Affairs for the punitive campaign, granted one set of martial music, and led a thousand tower ships and twenty thousand fighting men to enter Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Taishi, Yan was made supervisor of military affairs for the punitive campaign, granted one set of martial music, and led a thousand tower ships and twenty thousand soldiers into Quewei.

sentences.zh: 顗本無將略，性又怯橈，在軍中未嘗戎服，語不及戰陳，唯賦詩談義而已。

translations.literal: Yan originally had no military strategy; by nature he was also timid and yielding. In the army he never wore martial dress, his talk never touched battle arrays—only composing poetry and discussing principles.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had no gift for command and was by nature timid and pliant. In camp he never wore armor, never spoke of battle—only of poetry and doctrine.

sentences.zh: 不能撫接諸將，劉胡每論事，酬對甚簡，由此大失人情，胡常切齒恚恨。

translations.literal: He could not comfort and win over the generals. Whenever Liu Hu discussed affairs, his replies were very brief; thereby he greatly lost men's hearts, and Hu often gnashed his teeth in hatred.
translations.idiomatic: He could not win the generals over. Whenever Liu Hu discussed affairs, Yan's answers were terse, and he thereby lost men's hearts; Hu often gnashed his teeth in hatred.

sentences.zh: 胡以南運未至，軍士匱乏，就顗換襄陽之資。

translations.literal: Because supplies from the south had not arrived and the soldiers were exhausted, Hu asked Yan to exchange resources from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: As southern supplies had not arrived and the troops were depleted, Hu asked Yan to exchange resources from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 顗答曰：「都下兩宅未成，亦應經理，不可損徹。

translations.literal: Yan replied, "The two mansions in the capital are not yet finished and also need managing—they cannot be reduced to the last degree."
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "The two mansions at court are not yet finished and still need tending—they cannot be stripped bare."

sentences.zh: 」又信往來之言，京師米貴，斗至數百，以為不勞攻伐，行自離散，於是擁甲以待之。

translations.literal: " He also believed reports from travelers that grain in the capital was dear, a dou reaching several hundred, and thought that without laboring to attack, they would scatter of themselves—thereupon he hugged his armor and waited.
translations.idiomatic: " He also believed travelers' reports that grain in the capital was dear, a dou costing hundreds, and thought that without fighting the enemy would scatter on their own—so he hugged his armor and waited.

sentences.zh: 太宗使顗舊門生徐碩奉手詔譬顗曰：「卿歷觀古今，嶮之與強，何嘗可恃。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yan's former student Xu Shuo to deliver an imperial letter in hand and admonish Yan, saying: "You have surveyed antiquity and the present—how often can one rely on peril or strength?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Yan's former student Xu Shuo with an imperial letter in hand to admonish him: "You have read antiquity and the present—when has one ever relied on peril or strength?"

sentences.zh: 自朕踐阼，塗路梗塞，卿無由奉表，未經為臣。

translations.literal: "Since We ascended the throne, the roads have been blocked; you had no means to present memorials and have not yet been Our minister."
translations.idiomatic: "Since We took the throne, the roads have been blocked; you had no way to present memorials and have not yet been Our minister."

sentences.zh: 今追蹤竇融，猶未為晚也。」

translations.literal: "To follow in the tracks of Dou Rong is still not too late."
translations.idiomatic: "To follow Dou Rong's example is still not too late."

sentences.zh: 顗子戩，為偽黃門侍郎，加輔國將軍，戍盆城。

translations.literal: Yan's son Zhan served as bogus Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State, garrisoning Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Zhan served as counterfeit Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State, defending Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 尋陽敗，戩棄城走，討禽伏誅。

translations.literal: When Xunyang fell, Zhan abandoned the city and fled; pursued and captured, he was executed where he lay.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunyang fell, Zhan abandoned the city and fled; he was pursued, captured, and executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 孔覬，字思遠，會稽山陰人，太常琳之孫也。

translations.literal: Kong Ji, styled Siyuan, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji, grandson of the Minister of Ceremonies Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji, whose courtesy name was Siyuan, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji and was grandson of Minister of Ceremonies Kong Lin.

sentences.zh: 父邈，揚州治中。

translations.literal: His father Miao was an aide in Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Miao served as an aide in Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 覬少骨梗有風力，以是非為己任。

translations.literal: Ji from youth was stern in bone and forceful in bearing, taking right and wrong as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji was stern and forceful, making right and wrong his personal concern.

sentences.zh: 口吃，好讀書，早知名。

translations.literal: He stammered, loved reading, and was early known by reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He stammered, loved books, and was known early by name.

sentences.zh: 初舉揚州秀才，補主簿，長沙王義欣鎮軍功曹，衡陽王義季安西主簿，戶曹參軍，領南義陽太守，轉署記室，奉箋固辭，曰：「記室之局，實惟華要，自非文行秀敏，莫或居之。

translations.literal: At first he was nominated as a provincial candidate of Yangzhou, appointed as registrar, served as merit officer to Prince of Changsha Yixin's army that guards the realm, as registrar to Prince of Hengyang Yiji's pacification-of-the-west staff, as staff officer of the Household Section, and concurrent Administrator of Southern Yiyang; then he was transferred to acting recorder and submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "The post of recorder is truly a splendid and important office; unless one's culture and conduct are outstanding and keen, none may occupy it."
translations.idiomatic: At first he was nominated as Yangzhou's provincial candidate, made registrar, served as merit officer on Prince of Changsha Liu Yixin's staff as general who guards the realm, as registrar on Prince of Hengyang Liu Yiji's pacification-of-the-west staff, as staff officer of the Household Section, and concurrent Administrator of Southern Yiyang; then he was transferred to acting recorder and firmly declined by memorial, saying, "The recorder's office is truly splendid and important; unless culture and conduct are outstanding and keen, none should hold it."

sentences.zh: 覬遜業之舉，無聞於鄉部；

translations.literal: "Ji's nomination for yielding achievement was unheard of in his district;"
translations.idiomatic: "Ji's nomination for yielding achievement was unknown in his district;"

sentences.zh: 惰遊之貶，有編於疲農。

translations.literal: "the censure for idle roaming was recorded among the weary farmers."
translations.idiomatic: "the censure for idle roaming was entered among the weary farmers."

sentences.zh: 直山淵藏引，用不遐棄，故得抃風舞潤，憑附彌年。

translations.literal: "Mount Zhi's deep store drew him forth and used him without casting him far away; therefore he could clap in wind and dance in rain, relying on attachment for many years."
translations.idiomatic: "Mount Zhi drew him from deep store and did not cast him away; thus he could rejoice in wind and rain, clinging to patronage for many years."

sentences.zh: 今日之命，非所敢冒。

translations.literal: "Today's appointment is not what I dare presume upon."
translations.idiomatic: "Today's appointment is not what I dare accept."

sentences.zh: 昔之學優藝富，猶尚斯難，況覬能薄質魯，亦何容易。

translations.literal: "Men of old, though excellent in learning and rich in talent, still found this difficult—how much the more for Ji, whose ability is thin and nature dull?"
translations.idiomatic: "Men of old, though excellent in learning and rich in arts, still found this hard—how much more for Ji, whose ability is thin and nature dull?"

sentences.zh: 覬聞居方辨物，君人所以官才；

translations.literal: "Ji has heard that occupying one's place and distinguishing things is how the ruler assigns offices;"
translations.idiomatic: "Ji has heard that occupying one's place and distinguishing things is how the ruler assigns offices;"

sentences.zh: 陳力就列，自下所以奉上。

translations.literal: "displaying one's strength and taking one's rank is how those below serve those above."
translations.idiomatic: "displaying one's strength and taking one's rank is how those below serve those above."

sentences.zh: 覬雖不敏，常服斯言。

translations.literal: "Though Ji is not keen, he constantly takes this saying to heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Though Ji is not keen, he constantly holds to this saying."

sentences.zh: 今寵藉惟舊，舉非尚德，恐無以提衡一隅，僉允視聽者也。

translations.literal: "Now favor and old ties alone are the reason for the nomination, not exaltation of virtue—I fear there is no means to weigh one corner and satisfy all who look and listen."
translations.idiomatic: "Now favor and old ties alone prompted the nomination, not exaltation of virtue—I fear there is no way to weigh one corner and satisfy all who look and listen."

sentences.zh: 伏願天明照其心請，乞改今局，授以閑曹，則鳧鶴從方，所憂去矣。

translations.literal: "I bow and hope Heaven's brightness will illumine my heartfelt request: beg to change this office and grant an idle post—then duck and crane will each take their place, and what I fear will be gone."
translations.idiomatic: "I bow and hope Heaven's brightness will see my heartfelt request: grant a change of office to an idle post—then duck and crane will each keep their place, and my worry will pass."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「夫以記室之要，宜須通才敏忠，加性情勤密者。

translations.literal: " He also said: "For the importance of the recorder's post, one needs comprehensive talent, keen loyalty, and moreover a diligent and close nature."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The recorder's post requires comprehensive talent and keen loyalty, with a diligent and close nature besides."

sentences.zh: 覬學不綜貫，性又疏惰，何可以屬知秘記，秉筆文閨。

translations.literal: "Ji's learning is not comprehensive; his nature is also loose and lazy—how can he be entrusted with secret records and hold the brush in the literary inner court?"
translations.idiomatic: "Ji's learning is not comprehensive; his nature is loose and lazy—how can he be entrusted with secret records and hold the brush in the literary inner court?"

sentences.zh: 假吹之尤，方斯非濫。

translations.literal: "The fault of the man who borrows another's breath—compared with this, is not excessive appointment."
translations.idiomatic: "The fault of borrowing another's breath—compared with this, the appointment is not excessive."

sentences.zh: 覬少淪常檢，本無遠植，榮進之願，何能忘懷。

translations.literal: "Ji in youth fell below ordinary restraint and originally had no far-reaching growth; the wish for honor and advancement—how could he forget it in his breast?"
translations.idiomatic: "Ji in youth fell below ordinary restraint and had no far-reaching growth; the wish for honor and advancement—how could he forget it?"

sentences.zh: 若實有螢爝，增暉光景，固其騰聲之日，飛藻之辰也，豈敢自求從容，保其淡逸。

translations.literal: "If he truly has firefly or torch, adding brightness to the scene, that is indeed the day his fame rises and his brush flies—how would he dare seek ease for himself and keep bland detachment?"
translations.idiomatic: "If he truly had firefly or torch to add light to the scene, that would be the day his fame rose and his brush flew—how would he dare seek ease and keep bland detachment?"

sentences.zh: 伏願矜其魯拙，業之有地，則曲成之施，終始優渥。

translations.literal: "I bow and hope you will pity his dullness and give his craft a place—then the favor of bringing him to completion will be generous from first to last."
translations.idiomatic: "I bow and hope you will pity his dullness and give his craft a place—then the favor of bringing him to completion will be generous throughout."

sentences.zh: 」義季不能奪，遂得免。

translations.literal: " Yiji could not overcome his objections, and he was thereby excused.
translations.idiomatic: " Yiji could not overcome his objections, and Ji was excused.

sentences.zh: 召為通直郎，太子中舍人，建平王友，秘書丞，中書侍郎，隨王誕安東諮議參軍，領記室，黃門侍郎，建平王宏中軍長史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Direct Communication Attendant, Central Aide to the Crown Prince, Friend to the Prince of Jianping, Secretary Gentleman, Gentleman of the Central Secretariat, advisory staff officer to Prince of Sui Dan's eastern pacification, concurrent recorder, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and army aide to the central army under Prince of Jianping Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Direct Communication Attendant, central aide to the crown prince, friend to the Prince of Jianping, secretary gentleman, gentleman of the Central Secretariat, advisory staff officer to Prince of Sui Liu Dan's eastern pacification, concurrent recorder, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and army aide to the central army under Prince of Jianping Liu Hong.

sentences.zh: 復為黃門，臨海太守。

translations.literal: Again he was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 初，晉世散騎常侍選望甚重，與侍中不異，其後職任閒散，用人漸輕。

translations.literal: At first, in the Jin era the selection and prestige of Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment were very weighty, no different from Attendant-in-Ordinary; afterward the duties grew idle and scattered, and appointments gradually grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: At first in the Jin era the selection and prestige of Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment were very weighty, no different from Attendant-in-Ordinary; later the duties grew idle and appointments gradually grew lighter.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，世祖欲重其選，詔曰：「散騎職為近侍，事居規納，置任之本，實惟親要，而頃選常侍，陵遲未允，宜簡授時良，永置清轍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian, the emperor wished to restore weight to the selection and issued an edict, saying: "The office of Attendant Cavalier is a close attendant; its affairs lie in remonstrance and intake. The root of appointment is truly intimate and important, yet of late the selection of regular attendants has declined and not been fitting—worthy men of the time should be chosen and a clear track set forever."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian the emperor wished to restore weight to the selection and issued an edict: "The attendant cavalier serves close at hand; his affairs are remonstrance and intake. The root of the appointment is truly intimate and important, yet lately the choice of regular attendants has declined and not been fitting—men of the time should be chosen and a clear standard set forever."

sentences.zh: 」於是吏部尚書顏竣奏曰：「常侍華選，職任俟才，新除臨海太守孔覬意業閑素，司徒左長史王彧懷尚清理，並任為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yan Jun, Minister of the Civil Service, memorialized, saying: "The attendant cavalier is a splendid selection; the office awaits talent. The newly appointed Administrator of Linhai Kong Ji is calm in intent and plain in conduct; Wang Yu, Left Army Aide to the Minister of State, cherishes clarity and order—both are fit to serve as Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment."
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Yan Jun, Minister of the Civil Service, memorialized: "The attendant cavalier is a splendid selection awaiting talent. The newly appointed Administrator of Linhai Kong Ji is calm in intent and plain in conduct; Wang Yu, left army aide to the Minister of State, cherishes clarity and order—let both serve as Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment."

sentences.zh: 」世祖不欲威權在下，其後分吏部尚書置二人，以輕其任。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not wish authority to rest below; afterward he divided the Minister of the Civil Service into two posts to lighten the office.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not wish authority to rest below; afterward he divided the Minister of the Civil Service into two posts to lighten the charge.

sentences.zh: 侍中蔡興宗謂人曰：「選曹要重，常侍閑淡，改之以名而不以實，雖主意欲為輕重，人心豈可變邪！

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Xingzong said to others, "The Selection Bureau is important and weighty; the attendant cavalier is idle and light—changing the name without changing the reality: though the intent is to make light and heavy, can men's hearts be altered?"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Xingzong said to others, "The Selection Bureau is important; the attendant cavalier is idle and light—changing the name without changing the reality: though the intent is to shift weight, can men's hearts be changed?"

sentences.zh: 」既而常侍之選復卑，選部之貴不異。

translations.literal: " Before long the selection for attendant cavalier again grew base, and the prestige of the Selection Bureau was no different.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the selection for attendant cavalier again grew base, and the Selection Bureau's prestige was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 覬領本州大中正。

translations.literal: Ji concurrently served as Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Ji concurrently served as chief rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，改太子中庶子，領翊軍校尉，轉秘書監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he was changed to Central Aide to the Crown Prince, concurrent Colonel of the Assisting Army, and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming he was made central aide to the crown prince, concurrent colonel of the Assisting Army, and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 欲以為吏部郎，不果。

translations.literal: He was intended for appointment as Lang of the Ministry of the Civil Service, but it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was meant to be made lang of the Ministry of the Civil Service, but it did not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉卿，御史中丞，坐鞭令史，為有司所糾，原不問。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of Justice and Imperial Censor; for having flogged a clerical officer he was impeached by the relevant offices, but was pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Court of Justice and imperial censor; for flogging a clerical officer he was impeached by the relevant offices but pardoned without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 六年，除義興太守，未之任，為尋陽王子房冠軍長史，加寧朔將軍，行淮南、宣城二郡事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Administrator of Yixing; before taking up the post he was made conquest-of-champions army aide under Prince of Xunyang Zifang, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North, acting in the affairs of Huainan and Xuancheng two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Administrator of Yixing; before assuming it he was made conquest-of-champions army aide under Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North and acting charge of Huainan and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 其年，復除安陸王子綏冠軍長史、江夏內史，復隨府轉後軍長史如故。

translations.literal: That same year he was again appointed conquest-of-champions army aide under Prince of Anlu Zisui and Interior Governor of Jiangxia; again following the princely establishment he was transferred to army aide to the rear army as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was again made conquest-of-champions army aide under Prince of Anlu Liu Zisui and interior governor of Jiangxia, then with the princely household transferred again to army aide to the rear army as before.

sentences.zh: 為人使酒仗氣，每醉輒彌日不醒，僚類之間，多所凌忽，尤不能曲意權幸，莫不畏而疾之。

translations.literal: As a man he was given to wine and swaggering spirit; whenever drunk he would not sober for a whole day. Among colleagues he often treated many with contempt, and above all could not bend to please the powerful and favored—none did not fear and resent him.
translations.idiomatic: He was given to wine and a swaggering temper; when drunk he would not sober for a whole day. Among colleagues he often showed contempt, and above all could not bend to please the powerful—everyone feared and resented him.

sentences.zh: 不治產業，居常貧罄，有無豐約，未嘗關懷。

translations.literal: He did not manage property; he was constantly poor and empty at home; whether he had much or little, he never gave it a thought.
translations.idiomatic: He did not manage estates; he lived in constant poverty; whether times were rich or lean, he never cared.

sentences.zh: 為二府長史，典籤諮事，不呼不敢前，不令去不敢去。

translations.literal: As army aide to two princely establishments, registrars and advisory staff—if he did not call, they did not dare advance; if he did not dismiss, they did not dare leave.
translations.idiomatic: As army aide in two princely establishments, registrars and advisory staff did not dare step forward unless called, nor leave unless dismissed.

sentences.zh: 雖醉日居多，而明曉政事，醒時判決，未嘗有壅。

translations.literal: Though drunk days were many, he was clear in government affairs; when sober his judgments never piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Though drunk most days, he was clear in government; when sober his judgments never piled up.

sentences.zh: 眾咸云：「孔公一月二十九日醉，勝他人二十九日醒也。

translations.literal: All said together, "Master Kong is drunk twenty-nine days of the month—better than others' twenty-nine days awake."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said, "Master Kong is drunk twenty-nine days in the month—better than others' twenty-nine days awake."

sentences.zh: 」世祖每欲引見，先遣人覘其醉醒。

translations.literal: " Whenever Emperor Xiaowu wished to summon him for audience, he first sent men to spy on whether he was drunk or sober.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever Emperor Xiaowu wished to receive him in audience, he first sent someone to see whether he was drunk or sober."

sentences.zh: 性真素，不尚矯飾，遇得寶玩，服用不疑，而他物粗敗，終不改易。

translations.literal: His nature was genuinely plain; he did not esteem affectation. When he obtained treasures or curios, he used them without hesitation; other things might be coarse and worn, yet he never changed them.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was genuinely plain and scorned pretense. Fine treasures he used without a second thought; coarse, worn things he kept and never traded in.

sentences.zh: 時吳郡顧覬之亦尚儉素，衣裘器服，皆擇其陋者。

translations.literal: At the time Gu Yanzhi of Wu commandery also valued thrift and simplicity; for fur coats, utensils, and dress he always chose the shabbiest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gu Yanzhi of Wu commandery likewise prized thrift: for coats, utensils, and dress he always picked the shabbiest he could find.

sentences.zh: 宋世言清約，稱此二人。

translations.literal: In the Song age, when men spoke of purity and restraint, they named these two.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Song, when men praised purity and restraint, they named these two.

sentences.zh: 覬弟道存，從弟徽，頗營產業。

translations.literal: Gu Yanzhi's younger brother Daocun and his cousin Hui were quite active in building up estates.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanzhi's younger brother Daocun and his cousin Hui were rather busy amassing property.

sentences.zh: 二弟請假東還，覬出渚迎之，輜重十餘船，皆是綿絹紙席之屬。

translations.literal: When both younger brothers took leave to return east, Gu Yanzhi went out to the islet to meet them—more than ten boats of baggage, all cotton silk, paper, matting, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When both younger brothers took leave to return east, Gu Yanzhi went out to the river islet to meet them: more than ten boats of baggage, all silk, paper, mats, and such goods.

sentences.zh: 覬見之，偽喜，謂曰：「我比困乏，得此甚要。

translations.literal: Seeing them, he feigned delight and said, "I have lately been in want; getting this is most needed.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw them he feigned delight and said, "I have been hard pressed lately—this is just what I need.

sentences.zh: 」因命上置岸側，既而正色謂道存等曰：「汝輩忝預士流，何至還東作賈客邪！

translations.literal: " He had it all unloaded on the bank, then with stern face told Daocun and the rest, "You disgrace the scholar-official class—how could you return east and become mere merchants!"
translations.idiomatic: " He had everything carried ashore, then with a stern face told Daocun and the others, "You rank among the scholar-official class—how could you go back east and play merchant!"

sentences.zh: 」命左右取火燒之，燒盡乃去。

translations.literal: " He ordered attendants to fetch fire and burn it all; only when it was consumed did he leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered his attendants to set it ablaze and did not leave until the last bundle was ash.

sentences.zh: 先是，庾徽之為御史中丞，性豪麗，服玩甚華，覬代之，衣冠器用，莫不粗率。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu Huizhi had been Censor-in-Chief—by nature extravagant, his dress and ornaments very splendid. When Gu Yanzhi replaced him, hat, robe, utensils, nothing was not rough and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu Huizhi had served as Censor-in-Chief, a man of lavish tastes whose dress and ornaments were splendid. When Gu Yanzhi took his place, hat, robe, and every utensil were deliberately rough and plain.

sentences.zh: 蘭臺令史並三吳富人，咸有輕之之意，覬蓬首緩帶，風貌清嚴，皆重跡屏氣，莫敢欺犯。

translations.literal: Archive clerks and wealthy men of the Three Wu all had thoughts of looking down on him; but Gu Yanzhi, with unkempt hair and loose sash, bearing clear and stern—all stepped softly and held their breath, none daring to slight or affront him.
translations.idiomatic: Archive clerks and wealthy men of the Three Wu all meant to look down on him; yet Gu Yanzhi, hair unkempt and sash loose, with a bearing clear and stern, made every man tread softly and hold his breath—none dared slight or cross him.

sentences.zh: 庾徽之，字景猷，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Huizhi, styled Jingyou, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huizhi, whose courtesy name was Jingyou, came from Yanling in Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 自中丞出為新安王子鸞北中郎長史、南東海太守，卒官。

translations.literal: From censor he went out as army aide to the North Army of the Central Army for Prince Xin'an Ziluan, and as Administrator of Southern Donghai; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the censorate, he became army aide to the North Army of the Central Army for Prince Xin'an Ziluan and Administrator of Southern Donghai, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，召覬為太子詹事，遣故佐平西司馬庾業為右軍司馬，代覬行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he summoned Ji as Household Steward of the Heir Apparent and sent his former aide Yu Ye, former aide to the Pacification-West army, as army aide to the Right Army to act in Ji's stead in Kuaiji commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he summoned Kong Ji as Household Steward of the Heir Apparent and sent his former aide Yu Ye, once staff officer to the Pacification-West army, as army aide to the Right Army to govern Kuaiji in Ji's place.

sentences.zh: 時上流反叛，上遣都水使者孔璪入東慰勞。

translations.literal: At the time the upper Yangzi regions were in rebellion; the emperor sent the Commissioner of Waterworks Kong Xuan into the east to offer comfort and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The upper Yangzi was in revolt; the emperor sent the Commissioner of Waterworks Kong Xuan east to offer comfort and rewards.

sentences.zh: 璪至，說覬以廢帝侈費，倉儲耗盡，都下罄匱，資用已竭。

translations.literal: When Xuan arrived, he persuaded Ji that the Deposed Emperor's extravagance had emptied the granaries, the capital was stripped bare, and resources were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan arrived, he told Ji that the Deposed Emperor's extravagance had drained the granaries, stripped the capital bare, and exhausted every resource.

sentences.zh: 今南北並起，遠近離叛，若擁五郡之銳，招動三吳，事無不克。

translations.literal: Now north and south rise together, near and far split away—if you rally the keen edge of five commanderies and stir the Three Wu, nothing could fail.
translations.idiomatic: North and south are rising together; near and far are breaking away. Rally the sharp edge of five commanderies and stir the Three Wu, and nothing can fail.

sentences.zh: 覬然其言，遂發兵馳檄。

translations.literal: Ji thought the words sound and thereupon raised troops and sped proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji found the argument convincing, raised troops, and sent proclamations flying.

sentences.zh: 覬子長公、璪二子淹、玄竝在都，馳信密報。

translations.literal: Ji's son Changgong and Xuan's two sons Yan and Xuan were together in the capital and sent urgent secret reports.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Changgong and Xuan's sons Yan and Xuan were all in the capital and sent urgent secret word back.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月，竝叛逃東歸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taishi, all fled the rebellion and escaped eastward home.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Taishi, they all broke away and fled east.

sentences.zh: 遣書要吳郡太守顧琛，琛以母年篤老，又密邇京邑，與長子寶素謀議，未叛。

translations.literal: He sent letters inviting Wu commandery Administrator Gu Chen; Chen, because his mother was advanced in years and the capital lay close at hand, consulted with his eldest son Bao at length and did not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He sent letters summoning Wu commandery Administrator Gu Chen. Chen, whose mother was very old and the capital uncomfortably near, debated at length with his eldest son Bao and held back.

sentences.zh: 少子寶先時為山陰令，馳書報琛，以南師已近，朝廷孤弱，不時順從，必有覆滅之禍。

translations.literal: His younger son Bao had been Magistrate of Shanyin and sent urgent word to Chen that the southern armies were near, the court isolated and weak—if they did not submit in time, ruin was certain.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Bao, then magistrate of Shanyin, sent urgent word that the southern armies were close, the court isolated and weak, and delay would mean certain ruin.

sentences.zh: 覬前鋒軍已渡浙江，琛遂據郡同反。

translations.literal: Ji's vanguard had already crossed the Zhe River; Chen thereupon held the commandery and joined the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Ji's vanguard had crossed the Zhe River, Chen seized the commandery and joined the revolt.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守王曇生、義興太守劉延熙、晉陵太守袁標，一時回應。

translations.literal: Administrators Wang Tansheng of Wuxing, Liu Yanxi of Yixing, and Yuan Biao of Jinling all responded at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tansheng of Wuxing, Liu Yanxi of Yixing, and Yuan Biao of Jinling all answered at once.

sentences.zh: 庾業既東，太宗即以代延熙為義興，加建威將軍，以延熙為巴陵王休若鎮東長史。

translations.literal: Once Ye had gone east, Emperor Ming appointed him in Yanxi's place in Yixing and added him General Who Establishes Might, making Yanxi army aide to the East-Pacifying army for Prince Baling Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu Ye had gone east, Emperor Ming put him in Yanxi's place as administrator of Yixing with the rank General Who Establishes Might, and made Yanxi army aide on Prince Baling Xiuruo's eastern staff.

sentences.zh: 業至長塘湖，即與延熙合。

translations.literal: When Ye reached Longtang Lake, he immediately joined Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ye reached Longtang Lake and at once joined forces with Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣建威將軍沈懷明東討，尚書張永係進，鎮東將軍巴陵王休若董統東討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaiming east to attack, Minister of Works Zhang Yong to follow in support, and East-Pacifying General Prince Baling Xiuruo to supervise overall eastern campaign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaiming east to attack, Minister of Works Zhang Yong to follow, and East-Pacifying General Prince Baling Xiuruo to command the entire eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 移檄東土曰：

translations.literal: He issued a proclamation to the eastern regions, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He issued a proclamation to the eastern provinces:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞釁集有兆，禍至無門，倚伏之來，實惟人致。

translations.literal: I have heard that when calamity gathers, omens appear; disaster arrives though no gate opens—for fortune and misfortune alike, men alone bring them on.
translations.idiomatic: It is said that when rebellion gathers, signs appear first; calamity finds its way in though no door stands open. Fortune and ruin alike are wrought by men.

sentences.zh: 故囂、述貪亂，終殄宗祀；

translations.literal: Hence Proud and Comfortable, greedy for chaos, in the end extinguished their ancestral sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Proud and Comfortable, greedy for chaos, in the end wiped out their own ancestral rites;

sentences.zh: 昌、憲構氛，旋潤斧鉞。

translations.literal: Chang and Xian raised miasma and soon moistened the axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and Xian raised a foul air and soon felt the imperial blade.

sentences.zh: 斯則昭章記牒，炯戒今古者也。

translations.literal: This is what shines from annals and registers—a bright warning for past and present.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the annals record in plain light—a warning that burns for every age.

sentences.zh: 自國步時艱，三綱道盡，神歇靈繹，璿業綴旒。

translations.literal: Since the throne's path grew harsh, the three bonds' way was spent, spirits ceased and numen trailed, the jade scepter's line hung by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: Since the realm's path grew harsh, the three bonds were spent, spirits fell silent and numen trailed away, and the jade scepter's line hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 皇上仁雄集瑞，英睿應歷，鳳儀熛升，龍輝電舉。

translations.literal: The emperor, benevolent and heroic, gathers auspices; brilliant and sage, he answers to the reign cycle—phoenix bearing blazes aloft, dragon glory springs like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor, benevolent and heroic, gathers auspices; brilliant and sage, he answers the age—phoenix bearing blazes aloft, dragon glory leaping like lightning.

sentences.zh: 蕩穢紫樞，不俟鳴條之誓，凝政中宇，不肆漂杵之威。

translations.literal: He sweeps filth from the purple hinge without awaiting the oath beneath the sounding branch; he consolidates rule within the central realm without unleashing the pestle-washing wrath.
translations.idiomatic: He sweeps filth from the imperial hinge without waiting for the oath beneath the sounding branch; he consolidates rule within the central realm without unleashing the pestle-washing wrath of total war.

sentences.zh: 是以墜維再造，虧天重構，幽明裁紀，標配斯光。

translations.literal: Thus the fallen net is woven anew, the broken heaven rebuilt; shade and light receive their measure, and models are aligned in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the fallen net is woven anew and the broken heaven rebuilt; shade and light receive their measure, and the empire's pattern is set in glory.

sentences.zh: 而群凶恣虐，協扇童孺，蕞爾東垂，復淪醜跡，邪回從慝，蜂動蟻附。

translations.literal: Yet the vicious band wantonly brutalize, rousing even children—in that tiny eastern verge they sink again into vile paths, the crooked follow evil, swarming like bees, clinging like ants.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the vicious band brutalize at will, rousing even children; that tiny eastern verge sinks again into vile paths, the crooked follow evil, swarming like bees and clinging like ants.

sentences.zh: 聖圖霆發，神威四臨，羽馹所屆，義旅雲屬，欃鉞所麾，逆徒冰泮，勝負之效，皎然已顯。

translations.literal: The sacred design thunders forth, divine might presses on four sides; where courier feathers arrive, righteous hosts mass like clouds; where the comet-axe points, rebels melt like ice—the outcome, clear and bright, is already plain.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred design thunders forth and divine might presses on every side; where courier feathers arrive, righteous hosts mass like clouds; where the comet-axe points, rebels melt like ice—the outcome is already plain as daylight.

sentences.zh: 司徒建安王英猷冠世，董率元戎。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an, Minister of State, leads the age in strategy and commands the main host.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an, Minister of State, leads the age in strategy and commands the main host.

sentences.zh: 驃騎山陽王風略夙昭，撫厲中陳。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Prince Shanyang, long famed for bearing and design, heartens the central array.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince Shanyang, long famed for bearing and design, heartens the central battle line.

sentences.zh: 或振霜江、蠡，或騰焱荊、河，金甲燭天庭，囂聲震海浦。

translations.literal: Some shake frost over the Yangzi and Lake regions, some soar with flame over Jing and Yellow River lands—golden armor lights the heavenly court, clamor rolls along the sea shores.
translations.idiomatic: Some shake frost over the Yangzi and Taihu, some soar with flame over Jing and the Yellow River—golden armor lights the court of heaven, and clamor rolls along the sea shores.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、吳興太守張永，東南標秀，協贊戎機。

translations.literal: Forward General and Wuxing Administrator Zhang Yong, the southeast's brilliant standard, assists the war council.
translations.idiomatic: Forward General and Wuxing Administrator Zhang Yong, the southeast's brilliant standard, assists the war council.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍沈懷明、鎮東中兵參軍劉亮、武衛將軍壽寂之，霜銳五千，熊騰虎步。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaiming, Central Army Staff Officer to the East-Pacifying Army Liu Liang, and Martial Guard General Shou Jizhi—five thousand frost-keen men, surging like bears, treading like tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming, Liu Liang, and Shou Jizhi lead five thousand frost-keen troops that surge like bears and tread like tigers.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍王穆之、龍驤將軍頓生，鐵騎連群，風驅電邁。

translations.literal: Grand Marshals Wang Muzhi and Dun Sheng—iron cavalry in chains, wind-driven, lightning-hurried.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshals Wang Muzhi and Dun Sheng bring iron cavalry in endless ranks, wind-driven and lightning-swift.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍齊王、射聲校尉姚道和，樓艦千艘，覆川蓋汜。

translations.literal: Right Army General the Prince of Qi and Master of Archery Yao Daohe—a thousand tower ships veiling the rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, Right Army General, and Yao Daohe, Master of Archery, with a thousand tower ships that veil the rivers.

sentences.zh: 左軍垣恭祖、步兵校尉杜幼文、冗從僕射全景文、員外散騎侍郎孫超之，並率虎旅，駱驛雲赴。

translations.literal: Left Army Yuan Gongzu, Footsoldier Commandant Du Youwen, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary Quan Jingwen, and Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment Sun Chaozhi—all leading tiger brigades, relay upon relay clouding in.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gongzu of the Left Army, Du Youwen, Quan Jingwen, and Sun Chaozhi all lead tiger brigades that come relay upon relay like gathering clouds.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍杜敬真、殿中將軍陸攸之、建武將軍吳喜，甲楯一萬，分趣義興。

translations.literal: Palace Generals Du Jingzhen and Lu Youzhi and General Who Establishes Martial Might Wu Xi—ten thousand in armor and shield, diverging on Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingzhen, Lu Youzhi, and Wu Xi bring ten thousand men in armor and shield, marching on Yixing by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 予猥承人乏，緫司戎統，聳劍東馳，申憤海曲。

translations.literal: I humbly inherit men's lack, oversee the martial command, raise my sword eastward, vent wrath along the coastal bend.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly fill a post no better man wanted, oversee the martial command, raise my sword and ride east, and vent my wrath along the coastal bend.

sentences.zh: 噴氣則白日盡晦，刷馬則清江倒流。

translations.literal: A shout of breath and the white sun turns dark; a sweep of horses and the clear river flows backward.
translations.idiomatic: Our breath alone could darken the white sun; our horses' sweep could turn the clear river backward.

sentences.zh: 以此伐叛，何勍不剿，以此柔服，何順不懷。

translations.literal: With this to crush rebels—what stronghold will not be cut down? With this to gentle submission—what allegiance will not come home?
translations.idiomatic: With such force to crush rebels, what stronghold will not fall? With such mercy to win submission, who will not return to allegiance?

sentences.zh: 愍彼群迷，弗辨堯、桀，螳黽微命，擬雷霆之衝；

translations.literal: Pity those deluded throngs who cannot tell Yao from Jie—mantis and locust, slight lives daring the thunderbolt's charge;
translations.idiomatic: Pity those deluded masses who cannot tell Yao from Jie—mantis and locust, slight lives daring the thunderbolt's charge;

sentences.zh: 已枯之葉，當霜飆之隊。

translations.literal: withered leaves meeting the frost-gale's ranks.
translations.idiomatic: withered leaves meeting the ranks of the frost gale.

sentences.zh: 尺豎所為寒心，匹婦所為歎息。

translations.literal: A cubit-high child's heart turns cold; every woman sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Every common man shudders; every woman sighs.

sentences.zh: 夫因禍致慶，資敗為成，前監不忘，後事明筮。

translations.literal: Through calamity comes blessing, from defeat comes achievement—past mirrors are not forgotten, later deeds are clear in the divining stalks.
translations.idiomatic: From calamity comes blessing; from defeat, triumph. Past mirrors are not forgotten, and the stalks of divination make the future plain.

sentences.zh: 若能相率歸順，投兵效款，則福鍾當年，祉覃來裔，孰如身轘宗屠，鬼餧魂泣者哉！

translations.literal: If you can lead one another back in allegiance and lay down arms in good faith, fortune will toll this very year, blessing reach generations yet unborn—who would choose body broken on the wheel, clan slaughtered, ghosts starved, souls weeping?
translations.idiomatic: If you can lead one another back in allegiance and lay down arms in good faith, fortune will ring out this very year and blessing reach generations yet unborn—who would choose the wheel, clan slaughter, starving ghosts, and weeping souls?

sentences.zh: 詳鏡安危，自求多福。

translations.literal: Study the mirror of peril and safety; seek your own measure of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh peril and safety in the mirror of this hour, and seek your own fortune.

sentences.zh: 購生禽覬千五百戶開國縣侯；

translations.literal: A reward: capture Ji alive—Marquis of a state-opening county with one thousand five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Capture Kong Ji alive: Marquis of a state-opening county with one thousand five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 生擒琛千戶開國縣侯。

translations.literal: capture Chen alive—marquis with one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: capture Gu Chen alive: marquis with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 斬送者半賞。

translations.literal: Half the reward for delivery dead.
translations.idiomatic: Half the reward if delivered dead.

sentences.zh: 時將士多是東人，父兄子弟皆已附逆，上因送軍普加宣示曰：「朕方務德簡刑，使四罪不相及，助順同逆者，一以所從為斷。

translations.literal: At the time most officers were easterners whose fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews had already joined the rebels; the emperor therefore proclaimed to the whole army: "I now pursue virtue and lighten punishments, so that the four crimes do not reach one another; help or hinder alike—each shall be judged only by whom he follows."
translations.idiomatic: Most of the officers were easterners whose fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews had already joined the rebels. The emperor therefore proclaimed to the whole army: "I now pursue virtue and lighten punishments, so that guilt does not spread through a clan. Whether you aid or oppose us, each man shall be judged only by whom he follows."

sentences.zh: 卿等當深達此懷，勿以親戚為慮也。

translations.literal: "You must grasp this intent deeply; do not let kinsmen be your worry."
translations.idiomatic: "Take this intent to heart and do not let kinsmen be your worry."

sentences.zh: 」眾於是大悅。

translations.literal: " The troops thereupon rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops thereupon rejoiced greatly.

sentences.zh: 覬所遣孫曇瓘等軍，頓晉陵九里，部陳甚盛。

translations.literal: Armies Ji sent under Sun Tanhuan and others halted at Jinling's Jiuli; formation very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: The armies Kong Ji sent under Sun Tanhuan and others halted at Jiuli in Jinling in a very imposing formation.

sentences.zh: 懷明至奔牛，所領寡弱，乃築壘自固。

translations.literal: Huaiming reached Benniu with a feeble following and built ramparts to hold himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiming reached Benniu with a feeble force and built ramparts to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 張永至曲阿，未知懷明安否，百姓驚擾，將士咸欲離散。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong reached Qu'e, not knowing whether Huaiming was safe; the people were alarmed, officers and men all wanted to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong reached Qu'e without knowing whether Huaiming was safe. The people panicked and officers and men alike wanted to scatter.

sentences.zh: 永退還延陵，就休若；

translations.literal: Yong retreated to Yanling and joined Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: Yong fell back to Yanling and joined Xiuruo.

sentences.zh: 諸將帥咸勸退保破岡。

translations.literal: Commanders all urged falling back to defend Pogang.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders all urged retreat to hold Pogang.

sentences.zh: 其日大寒，風雪甚猛，塘埭決壞，眾無固心。

translations.literal: That day was bitter cold, wind and snow fierce; dikes and dams burst, the host had no firm heart.
translations.idiomatic: That day was bitterly cold, with fierce wind and snow; dikes burst and the army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 休若宣令：「敢有言退者，斬！

translations.literal: Xiuruo proclaimed: "Whoever speaks of retreat—beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo proclaimed: "Whoever speaks of retreat shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」眾小定，乃築壘息甲。

translations.literal: " The masses settled somewhat; they built ramparts and rested the armor.
translations.idiomatic: " The army steadied somewhat; they built ramparts and rested.

sentences.zh: 尋得懷明書，賊定未進。

translations.literal: Soon they received Huaiming's letter: the rebels were fixed and not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they received word from Huaiming: the rebels were holding position and not advancing.

sentences.zh: 軍主劉亮又繼至，兵力轉加，人情乃安。

translations.literal: Army chief Liu Liang came up next; strength kept growing; hearts steadied.
translations.idiomatic: Army chief Liu Liang came up next; as strength grew, hearts steadied.

sentences.zh: 時永世令孔景宣復反，柵縣西江峴山，斷遏津徑，劉延熙加其寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: At the time Yongshi Magistrate Kong Jingxuan rebelled again, palisading Xijiang Qianshan in the county, cutting ferry paths; Yanxi added him General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yongshi magistrate Kong Jingxuan rebelled again, fortifying Xijiang Qianshan in the county and cutting the ferry paths; Yanxi made him General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 杜敬真、陸攸之、溧陽令劉休文攻景宣別寨，斬其中兵參軍史覽之等十五人。

translations.literal: Du Jingzhen, Lu Youzhi, and Liyang Magistrate Liu Xiuwen attacked Jingxuan's detached stockade and beheaded his Central Army staff officer Shi Lanzhi and fifteen others.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingzhen, Lu Youzhi, and Liyang magistrate Liu Xiuwen attacked Jingxuan's outpost and beheaded his central staff officer Shi Lanzhi and fifteen others.

sentences.zh: 永世人徐崇之率鄉里起義，攻縣斬景宣。

translations.literal: Xu Chongzhi of Yongshi led his township in uprising, stormed the county seat, and killed Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chongzhi of Yongshi rallied his township, stormed the county seat, and killed Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 吳喜至，板崇之領縣事。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi arrived, he appointed Chongzhi to administer the county.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi arrived, he appointed Chongzhi to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉休文等誠效，除休文寧朔將軍，縣如故；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming commended Xiuwen and the rest for loyal effort, appointed Xiuwen General Who Pacifies the North with his magistracy unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming commended Xiuwen and the others for loyal service, made Xiuwen General Who Pacifies the North while keeping his magistracy;

sentences.zh: 崇之殿中將軍，行永世縣事，並賜侯爵。

translations.literal: Chongzhi Palace General acting in Yongshi county affairs—both were granted marquis titles.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi Palace General acting in Yongshi county affairs—both were granted marquis titles.

sentences.zh: 喜、敬真及員外散騎侍郎竺超之等至國山縣界，遇東軍於虎檻村，擊大破之。

translations.literal: Xi, Jingzhen, and Attendant Cavalier Without Regular Appointment Zhu Chaozhi reached Guoshan county border, met eastern forces at Hujian village, struck and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Jingzhen, and Attendant Cavalier Zhu Chaozhi reached the border of Guoshan county, met eastern forces at Hujian village, and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 自國山進吳城，去義興十五里。

translations.literal: From Guoshan they advanced on Wucheng, fifteen li from Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: From Guoshan they advanced on Wucheng, fifteen li from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 劉延熙遣楊玄、孫矯之、沈靈秀、黃泰四軍拒喜。

translations.literal: Yanxi sent four armies under Yang Xuan, Sun Jiaozhi, Shen Lingxiu, and Huang Tai to resist Xi.
