translations.idiomatic: Yanxi sent four armies under Yang Xuan, Sun Jiaozhi, Shen Lingxiu, and Huang Tai to resist Xi.

sentences.zh: 喜等兵力甚弱，眾寡勢懸，交戰盡日，臨陳斬楊玄、孫矯之、黃泰，餘眾一時奔走，因進義興南郭外。

translations.literal: Xi's force was very weak, numbers grievously uneven; they fought all day, cut down Yang, Sun, and Huang on the field; the rest fled at once, and they advanced to outside Yixing's south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's force was very weak and the odds grievously uneven. They fought all day, cut down Yang, Sun, and Huang on the field, and the rest fled at once; they then advanced to outside the south gate of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 延熙屯軍南射堂，喜遣步騎擊之，即退還水北，乃柵斷長橋，保郡自守。

translations.literal: Yanxi encamped at the South Archery Hall; Xi sent infantry and cavalry to strike; he at once fell back north of the water, then palisaded and cut the long bridge, holding the commandery to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi encamped at the South Archery Hall. Xi sent infantry and cavalry to strike; Yanxi at once fell back north of the water, palisaded the long bridge, and held the commandery to defend.

sentences.zh: 喜築壘與之相持。

translations.literal: Xi built ramparts and faced him in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Xi built ramparts and faced him in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 庾業於長塘湖口夾岸築城，有眾七千餘人，器甲甚盛，與延熙遙相掎角。

translations.literal: Yu Ye built cities on both banks at Longtang Lake mouth—more than seven thousand men, armor and weapons splendid—pinching from afar with Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ye built fortresses on both banks at Longtang Lake mouth with more than seven thousand men and splendid armor, coordinating from afar with Yanxi in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 沈懷明、張永與晉陵軍相持，久不決。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiming and Zhang Yong locked with Jinling forces long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming and Zhang Yong remained locked with the Jinling army, long unresolved.

sentences.zh: 太宗每遣軍，輒多所求須，不時上道。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor sent troops, they always demanded much and did not march on time.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor sent reinforcements, they always demanded much and failed to march on time.

sentences.zh: 外監朱幼舉司徒參軍督護任農夫，驍果有膽力，性又簡率，資給甚易，乃以千人配之，使助東討。

translations.literal: Outer Supervisor Zhu You recommended Staff Officer to the Minister Ren Nongfu—bold and brave, nature simple and direct, supplies very easy—and gave him a thousand men to aid the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Outer Supervisor Zhu You recommended Ren Nongfu, staff officer to the Minister of State—bold, brave, plain in manner, and easy to supply—and gave him a thousand men to aid the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 時庾業兵盛，農夫於延陵出長塘，雖云千兵，至者裁四百。

translations.literal: Ye's troops were strong; Nongfu left Yanling for Longtang—though said to be a thousand, barely four hundred arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ye's troops were strong. Nongfu left Yanling for Longtang; though said to command a thousand, barely four hundred had arrived.

sentences.zh: 未至數十里，遣人參候，云：「賊築城猶未合。

translations.literal: Within several tens of li he sent scouts who reported: "The rebels' walls are not yet joined.
translations.idiomatic: Still several tens of li away, he sent scouts who reported, "The rebels' walls are not yet joined.

sentences.zh: 」農夫率廣武將軍高志之、永興令徐崇之馳往攻之。

translations.literal: " Nongfu led Forward Martial General Gao Zhizhi and Yongxing Magistrate Xu Chongzhi in a rush to attack.
translations.idiomatic: " Nongfu led Forward Martial General Gao Zhizhi and Yongxing magistrate Xu Chongzhi in a rush to attack.

sentences.zh: 因其城壘未立，農夫親持刀楯，赴城入陳，大破之，庾業棄城走義興。

translations.literal: While their ramparts stood unfinished, Nongfu himself took shield and blade, charged into the array at the walls, smashed them utterly; Ye abandoned the city and fled toward Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: While the ramparts were still unfinished, Nongfu himself took up shield and blade, charged into the wall's defenders, and routed them utterly. Yu Ye abandoned the city and fled toward Yixing.

sentences.zh: 先是，龍驤將軍阮佃夫募得蜀人數百，多壯勇便戰，皆著犀皮鎧，執短兵。

translations.literal: Earlier Grand Marshal Ruan Dianfu had recruited several hundred Shu men—mostly stout, brave, skilled in battle—all in rhinoceros-hide armor with short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Grand Marshal Ruan Dianfu had recruited several hundred Shu men, mostly stout, brave, and skilled in battle, all in rhinoceros-hide armor with short weapons.

sentences.zh: 本應就佃夫向晉陵，未發，會農夫須人，分以配之。

translations.literal: They were to join Dianfu against Jinling but had not set out; when Nongfu needed men, they were divided to him.
translations.idiomatic: They were to join Dianfu against Jinling but had not yet set out; when Nongfu needed men, they were assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 及戰，每先登，東人並畏憚，又怪其形飾殊異，舊傳狐獠食人，每見之，輒奔走。

translations.literal: In battle they always climbed first; easterners feared them, and finding their look so strange, remembering old tales that fox-demons and liao tribes ate men, fled whenever they appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they always climbed first. The easterners feared them, and finding their appearance so strange—and remembering old tales that fox-demons and liao tribes ate men—they fled whenever they appeared.

sentences.zh: 農夫收其船杖，與高志之進義興援吳喜。

translations.literal: Nongfu took their boats and gear and with Gao Zhizhi advanced on Yixing to reinforce Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Nongfu took their boats and gear and with Gao Zhizhi advanced on Yixing to reinforce Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 二月一日，喜乃度水攻郡，分兵擊諸壘柵。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month Xi crossed the water to attack the commandery, dividing forces to strike the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month Xi crossed the water to attack the commandery, dividing his forces to strike the stockades.

sentences.zh: 農夫雖至，眾力尚少，兵勢不敵。

translations.literal: Though Nongfu had come, his numbers were still few and his strength no match.
translations.idiomatic: Though Nongfu had arrived, his numbers were still few and his strength no match.

sentences.zh: 喜乃與數騎登高東西指麾，若招引四面俱進者。

translations.literal: Xi then took a few horsemen to a height and gestured east and west as if summoning advance on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Xi then took a few horsemen to a height and gestured east and west as if summoning armies advancing on every side.

sentences.zh: 東軍大駭，諸營一時奔散，唯龍驤將軍孔叡一柵未拔。

translations.literal: The eastern army was thrown into great panic; every camp scattered at once—only Grand Marshal Kong Rui's one palisade was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army panicked; every camp scattered at once—only Grand Marshal Kong Rui's palisade was not taken.

sentences.zh: 喜以殺傷者多，乃開圍緩之。

translations.literal: Xi, because those killed and wounded were many, then opened the siege and eased it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, seeing that many had been killed and wounded, lifted the siege and eased the pressure.

sentences.zh: 其夜，庾業、孔叡相率奔走，義興平。

translations.literal: That night, Yu Ye and Kong Rui led one another in flight; Yixing was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yu Ye and Kong Rui fled in succession, and Yixing was pacified.

sentences.zh: 劉延熙投水死，有人告之，乃斬尸，傳首京邑。

translations.literal: Liu Yanxi threw himself into the water and died; someone reported it, and they beheaded the corpse and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanxi drowned himself; when someone reported his death, the authorities beheaded the corpse and sent the head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 義興諸縣唯綏安令巢邃秉節不移，不受偽爵。

translations.literal: Of all the counties in Yixing, only the magistrate of Suian, Chao Sui, held to his integrity without wavering and did not accept a false title of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Among the counties of Yixing, only Chao Sui, magistrate of Suian, held firm to his integrity and refused to accept a rebel title of nobility.

sentences.zh: 時齊王率軍東討，與張永、劉亮、杜幼文、沈懷明等於晉陵九里西結營，與東軍相持。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi led his army east in punitive expedition; with Zhang Yong, Liu Liang, Du Youwen, Shen Huaiming, and others he encamped west of Jiuli at Jinling, facing the eastern army in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Qi led his army east on campaign; with Zhang Yong, Liu Liang, Du Youwen, Shen Huaiming, and others he encamped west of Jiuli at Jinling and faced the eastern army in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 義興軍既為吳喜等所破，奔散者多投晉陵，東軍震恐。

translations.literal: The Yixing army having been broken by Wu Xi and others, many of the scattered fugitives fled into Jinling; the eastern army was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The Yixing army having been shattered by Wu Xi and his forces, many fugitives fled into Jinling, and the eastern army was seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 上又遣積射將軍江方興、南臺御史王道隆至晉陵視賊形勢。

translations.literal: The emperor further sent the rapid-fire archer general Jiang Fangxing and the Southern Secretariat censor Wang Daolong to Jinling to observe the rebels' disposition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further dispatched the rapid-fire archer general Jiang Fangxing and the Southern Secretariat censor Wang Daolong to Jinling to reconnoiter the rebel positions.

sentences.zh: 賊帥孫曇瓘、程捍宗、陳景遠凡有五城，互相連帶；

translations.literal: The rebel commanders Sun Tanxuan, Cheng Hanzong, and Chen Jingyuan held five walled strongholds in all, linked one to another;
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commanders Sun Tanxuan, Cheng Hanzong, and Chen Jingyuan held five fortified towns in all, mutually linked;

sentences.zh: 捍宗城猶未固。

translations.literal: Hanzong's fort was not yet firmly built.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzong's fort was not yet firmly established.

sentences.zh: 其月三日，道隆與齊王、張永共議：「捍宗城既未立，可以籍手。

translations.literal: On the third of that month, Daolong deliberated with the Prince of Qi and Zhang Yong: "Since Hanzong's fort is not yet established, we may take advantage of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: On the third of that month, Daolong conferred with the Prince of Qi and Zhang Yong: "Since Hanzong's fort is not yet built, we may seize the opportunity.

sentences.zh: 上副聖旨，下成眾氣。

translations.literal: Above it will accord with the sage's intent; below it will fulfill the army's ardor.
translations.idiomatic: It will satisfy the imperial will above and rally the troops' spirit below.

sentences.zh: 」道隆便率所領急攻之，俄頃城陷，斬捍宗首。

translations.literal: Daolong then led his forces in a swift assault; in no time the fort fell, and Hanzong's head was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong then led his troops in a swift assault; the fort fell in moments, and Hanzong's head was taken.

sentences.zh: 劉亮果勁，便刀楯，朝士先不相悉，上亦弗聞，唯尚書左丞徐爰知之，白太宗，稱其驍敢。

translations.literal: Liu Liang was by nature fierce and bold and would take up sword and shield; the court gentlemen had not known one another before, and the emperor had not heard of him—only the Left Deputy Director of the Secretariat, Xu Ai, knew of him and reported to Emperor Taizong, praising his boldness and valor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang was by nature fierce and bold, ever ready with sword and shield. The court had not known him, nor had the emperor heard of him—only Xu Ai, Left Deputy Director of the Secretariat, knew of him and reported to Emperor Taizong, praising his daring and valor.

sentences.zh: 至是，每戰以刀楯直蕩，往輒陷決，張永嫌其過銳，不令居前。

translations.literal: From this time on, in every battle he charged straight through with sword and shield; wherever he went, defenses broke; Zhang Yong resented his excessive rashness and would not allow him to advance in the van.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, in every battle he charged straight through with sword and shield, breaking whatever lay before him; Zhang Yong, finding him too reckless, would not let him lead the van.

sentences.zh: 賊連柵周亙，塘道迫狹，將士力不得展，亮乃負楯而進，直入重柵，眾軍因之，即皆摧破。

translations.literal: The rebels had linked stockades all around; the embankment roads were cramped and narrow, and the soldiers' strength could not be deployed. Liang then shouldered his shield and advanced, piercing straight into the inner stockades; the whole army followed him, and all were smashed and overrun.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had linked stockades all around; the embankment roads were narrow, and the troops could not deploy their strength. Liang shouldered his shield and advanced straight into the inner palisades; the whole army followed, and everything was smashed and overrun.

sentences.zh: 袁標遣千人繼至，齊王與永等乘勝馳擊，又大破之，屠其兩城。

translations.literal: Yuan Biao sent a thousand men in reinforcement; the Prince of Qi and Yong and others seized victory to charge in pursuit, again inflicting a great defeat and slaughtering two of their forts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Biao sent a thousand men in reinforcement; the Prince of Qi and Zhang Yong and others pressed the victory in pursuit, inflicting another great defeat and slaughtering two of their towns.

sentences.zh: 曇瓘率眾數百，鼓噪而至，標又遣千人繼之，眾軍駭懼，將欲散矣。

translations.literal: Tanxuan led several hundred men, beating drums and shouting as they came; Biao again sent a thousand in support; the armies were seized with terror and were on the verge of scattering.
translations.idiomatic: Tanxuan led several hundred men, beating drums and shouting as they came; Biao sent another thousand in support; the armies were seized with terror and were on the verge of breaking apart.

sentences.zh: 江方興率勇士迎射之，應弦倒者相繼，曇瓘因此敗走。

translations.literal: Jiang Fangxing led valiant warriors to meet them with arrows; men fell in succession at the twang of the bowstring, and Tanxuan thus was routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fangxing led valiant warriors to meet them with arrows; men fell one after another at the twang of the bowstring, and Tanxuan was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 吳喜軍至義鄉，偽輔國將軍、車騎司馬孔璪屯吳興南亭，太守王曇生詣璪計事，會信還，云：「臺軍已近。

translations.literal: Wu Xi's army reached Yixiang. The false General of the State-supporting Army and Chief of the Chariotry, Kong An, was encamped at the Southern Pavilion of Wuxing; the grand prefect Wang Tansheng went to An to discuss affairs. A messenger returned, reporting: "The imperial army is drawing near.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's army reached Yixiang. The rebel General of the State-supporting Army and Chief of the Chariotry, Kong An, was encamped at the Southern Pavilion of Wuxing; the grand prefect Wang Tansheng went to consult with An. A messenger returned with word: "The imperial army is close at hand.

sentences.zh: 」璪大懼，墮床，曰：「懸賞所購，唯我而已，今不遽走，將為人禽。

translations.literal: An was greatly terrified, falling from his bed, and said: "The bounty posted seeks none but me alone; if I do not flee at once, I shall become another man's captive bird.
translations.idiomatic: An was seized with terror and fell from his bed, crying: "The posted bounty seeks none but me; if I do not flee at once, I shall become another man's prey.

sentences.zh: 」左右聞之，並各散走。

translations.literal: When his attendants heard this, each scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants heard this and scattered, each fleeing on his own.

sentences.zh: 璪與曇生焚燒倉庫，東奔錢塘。

translations.literal: An and Tansheng burned the storehouses and fled east to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: An and Tansheng burned the storehouses and fled east to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 喜至吳興，頓置郡城，倉廩遇雨不然，無所損失。

translations.literal: Xi reached Wuxing and encamped at the commandery seat; the granaries, though touched by rain, did not ignite, and nothing was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Xi reached Wuxing and encamped at the commandery seat; rain fell on the granaries but they did not catch fire, and nothing was lost.

sentences.zh: 初，曇生遣寧朔將軍沈靈寵率八千人向黃鵠嶠，欲從候道出蕪湖，迎接南軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tansheng had dispatched the General of Nimble Might, Shen Lingchong, leading eight thousand men toward Huangque Ridge, intending to take a bypath via the Houdao route to Wuhu to welcome the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tansheng had dispatched the General of Nimble Might, Shen Lingchong, with eight thousand men toward Huangque Ridge, intending to take the Houdao bypath to Wuhu and welcome the southern army.

sentences.zh: 廣德令王蘊發兵據嶮，靈寵不得進，屯住故鄣。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Guangde, Wang Yun, raised troops and seized the defiles; Lingchong could not advance and halted at Guyang.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Guangde, Wang Yun, raised troops and held the defiles; Lingchong could not advance and encamped at Guyang.

sentences.zh: 曇生既走，靈寵乃與弟靈昭、軍副姚天覆率偏裨以下十七軍歸順。

translations.literal: After Tansheng had fled, Lingchong together with his younger brother Lingzhao and the army deputy Yao Tianfu led seventeen subordinate armies from colonels downward to submit and pledge allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: After Tansheng fled, Lingchong, together with his younger brother Lingzhao and the army deputy Yao Tianfu, led seventeen subordinate armies from the colonels down to submit.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，擢為鎮東參軍事，因率所領東討。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong commended this, promoted him to Gentleman-Adjutant of the Army Pacifying the East, and had him lead his troops east in punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong commended this, promoted him to adjutant of the Army Pacifying the East, and had him lead his troops east on campaign.

sentences.zh: 喜分遣軍主沈思仁、吳係公追躡璪等。

translations.literal: Xi separately dispatched the army commanders Shen Sirren and Wu Jigong to pursue Kong An and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xi separately dispatched the army commanders Shen Sirren and Wu Jigong in pursuit of Kong An and his party.

sentences.zh: 陸攸之、任農夫自東遷進向吳郡，臺遣軍主張靈符即晉陵。

translations.literal: Lu Youzhi and Ren Nongfu advanced from Dongqian toward Wu Commandery; the court dispatched the army commander Zhang Lingfu from Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youzhi and Ren Nongfu advanced from Dongqian toward Wu Commandery, while the court dispatched the army commander Zhang Lingfu from Jinling.

sentences.zh: 其月四日，齊王急攻之。

translations.literal: On the fourth of that month, the Prince of Qi pressed the attack urgently.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth of that month the Prince of Qi pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 其夜，孫曇瓘、陳景遠一時奔潰。

translations.literal: That night Sun Tanxuan and Chen Jingyuan collapsed and fled all at once.
translations.idiomatic: That night Sun Tanxuan and Chen Jingyuan broke and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 諸軍至晉陵，袁標棄郡東走。

translations.literal: When the armies reached Jinling, Yuan Biao abandoned the commandery and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies reached Jinling, Yuan Biao abandoned the commandery and fled east.

sentences.zh: 晉陵既平，吳中震動。

translations.literal: Jinling having been pacified, Wu region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: With Jinling pacified, the Wu region was shaken.

sentences.zh: 吳興軍又將至，顧琛與子寶素攜其老母泛海奔會稽，海鹽令王孚邀討不及。

translations.literal: The Wuxing army was again approaching; Gu Chen and his son Baosu, carrying their aged mother, fled by sea to Kuaiji; the magistrate of Haiyan, Wang Fu, invited pursuit but could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing army was again approaching; Gu Chen and his son Baosu took their aged mother and fled by sea to Kuaiji; the magistrate of Haiyan, Wang Fu, moved to intercept them but could not overtake them.

sentences.zh: 太宗以四郡平定，留吳喜統全景文、沈懷明、劉亮、孫超之、壽寂之等東平會稽，追齊王、張永、姚道和、杜幼文、垣恭祖、張靈符北討，王穆之、頓生、江方興南伐。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, seeing the four commanderies pacified, left Wu Xi to command Quan Jingwen, Shen Huaiming, Liu Liang, Sun Chaozhi, Shou Jizhi, and others to pacify Kuaiji in the east; he ordered the Prince of Qi, Zhang Yong, Yao Dahe, Du Youwen, Yuan Gongzu, and Zhang Lingfu north on punitive expedition; Wang Muzhi, Dunsheng, and Jiang Fangxing south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: With the four commanderies pacified, Emperor Taizong left Wu Xi in command of Quan Jingwen, Shen Huaiming, Liu Liang, Sun Chaozhi, Shou Jizhi, and others to pacify Kuaiji in the east, while the Prince of Qi, Zhang Yong, Yao Dahe, Du Youwen, Yuan Gongzu, and Zhang Lingfu were sent north on campaign and Wang Muzhi, Dunsheng, and Jiang Fangxing south.

sentences.zh: 其月九日，喜等至錢唐，錢唐令顧昱及孔璪、王曇生等奔渡江東。

translations.literal: On the ninth of that month, Xi and others reached Qiantang; the magistrate Gu Yu and Kong An, Wang Tansheng, and others fled across the river to the east.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of that month Xi and his forces reached Qiantang; the magistrate Gu Yu, Kong An, Wang Tansheng, and others fled across the river to the east.

sentences.zh: 喜仍進軍柳浦，諸暨令傅琰將家歸順。

translations.literal: Xi continued his advance to Liupu; the magistrate of Zhuji, Fu Yan, brought his family to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xi continued his advance to Liupu; Fu Yan, magistrate of Zhuji, brought his family and submitted.

sentences.zh: 喜遣鎮北參軍沈思仁、彊弩將軍任農夫、龍驤將軍高志之、南臺御史阮佃夫、揚武將軍盧僧澤等率軍向黃山浦。

translations.literal: Xi dispatched the Army-Adjutant of the Army Pacifying the North, Shen Sirren, the Powerful Crossbow General Ren Nongfu, the Flying Dragon General Gao Zhizhi, the Southern Secretariat censor Ruan Tianfu, the Valiant Martial General Lu Sengze, and others with troops toward Huangshan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Xi dispatched Shen Sirren, adjutant of the Army Pacifying the North, the Powerful Crossbow General Ren Nongfu, the Flying Dragon General Gao Zhizhi, the Southern Secretariat censor Ruan Tianfu, the Valiant Martial General Lu Sengze, and others with troops toward Huangshan Ford.

sentences.zh: 東軍據岸結寨，農夫等攻破之，乘風舉帆，直趣定山，破其大帥孫會之，於陳斬首。

translations.literal: The eastern army entrenched on the shore in a stockaded camp; Nongfu and others broke through it, raising sails with the wind, drove straight for Mount Ding, defeated their grand commander Sun Huizhi, and beheaded him in battle array.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army entrenched on the shore; Nongfu and his men broke through, raised sail with the wind, and drove straight for Mount Ding, defeating their grand commander Sun Huizhi and beheading him on the field.

sentences.zh: 自定山進向漁浦，戍主孔叡率千餘人據壘拒戰。

translations.literal: Advancing from Mount Ding toward Yupu, the garrison commander Kong Rui led more than a thousand men to hold a fortified rampart and resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing from Mount Ding toward Yupu, the garrison commander Kong Rui led more than a thousand men to hold a fortified rampart and resist.

sentences.zh: 佃夫使隊主闕法炬射殺樓上弩手，叡眾驚駭，思仁縱兵攻之，斬其軍主孔奴，於是敗散。

translations.literal: Tianfu had the squad leader Que Faju shoot and kill the crossbowmen atop the tower; Rui's troops were seized with terror; Sirren unleashed his troops in assault, beheading their army commander Kong Nu, and thus they were routed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu had the squad leader Que Faju shoot down the crossbowmen on the tower; Rui's troops panicked; Sirren unleashed his men in assault, beheaded their army commander Kong Nu, and they broke and scattered.

sentences.zh: 其月十九日，吳喜使劉亮由鹽官海渡，直指同浦；

translations.literal: On the nineteenth of that month, Wu Xi sent Liu Liang across the sea from Yanguan, striking straight for Tongpu;
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of that month Wu Xi sent Liu Liang across the sea from Yanguan, striking straight for Tongpu;

sentences.zh: 壽寂之濟自漁浦，邪趣永興；

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi crossed from Yupu by a devious route toward Yongxing;
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi crossed from Yupu and took a devious route toward Yongxing;

sentences.zh: 喜自柳浦渡，趣西陵。

translations.literal: Xi himself crossed from Liupu, pressing toward Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Xi himself crossed from Liupu and pressed toward Xiling.

sentences.zh: 西陵諸軍皆悉散潰，斬庾業、顧法直、吳恭，傳首京都。

translations.literal: All armies at Xiling utterly collapsed and fled; Yu Ye, Gu Fazhi, and Wu Gong were beheaded and their heads sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: All armies at Xiling broke and fled; Yu Ye, Gu Fazhi, and Wu Gong were beheaded and their heads sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 東軍主卜道濟、督戰許天賜請降。

translations.literal: The eastern army commander Bu Daoji and the battle overseer Xu Tianci requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army commander Bu Daoji and the battle overseer Xu Tianci offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 庾業，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Ye was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ye was a native of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 父彥達，以幹局為太祖所知，為益州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yanda, known to Emperor Taizu for his capacity for practical affairs, served as Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanda, known to Emperor Taizu for his practical ability, served as inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，官至豫章太守，太常卿。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Shizu he rose to Grand Prefect of Yuzhang and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Shizu he rose to grand prefect of Yuzhang and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 劉亮、全景文、孫超之進次永興同市，遇覬所遣陸孝伯、孔豫兩軍，與戰破之，斬孝伯、豫首。

translations.literal: Liu Liang, Quan Jingwen, and Sun Chaozhi advanced and encamped at Yongxing Tongshi, encountering the two armies that Xu Ji dispatched, Lu Xiaobo and Kong Yu; they fought and defeated them, beheading Xiaobo and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang, Quan Jingwen, and Sun Chaozhi advanced and encamped at Yongxing Tongshi, where they met the two armies Xu Ji had dispatched under Lu Xiaobo and Kong Yu; they defeated them in battle and beheaded Xiaobo and Yu.

sentences.zh: 會稽聞西軍稍近，將士多奔亡，覬不能復制。

translations.literal: Kuaiji, hearing the western army drawing nearer, saw many officers and soldiers desert; Xu Ji could no longer control them.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuaiji heard the western army drawing near, officers and soldiers deserted in great numbers, and Xu Ji could no longer hold them.

sentences.zh: 二十日，上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，覬以東西交逼，憂遽不知所為。

translations.literal: On the twentieth, the magistrate of Shangyu, Wang Yan, raised troops to attack the commandery; Xu Ji, pressed from east and west, was frantic with worry and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth the magistrate of Shangyu, Wang Yan, raised troops to attack the commandery; Xu Ji, pressed from east and west, was frantic with anxiety and knew not what to do.

sentences.zh: 其夕，率千餘人聲云東討，實趣石瀃。

translations.literal: That evening he led more than a thousand men, proclaiming an eastern expedition, but in fact made for Shibian.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he led more than a thousand men, proclaiming an eastern campaign, but in truth made for Shibian.

sentences.zh: 先已具船海浦，值潮涸不得去，眾叛都盡，門生載以小船，竄於脊山村。

translations.literal: He had already prepared boats at the sea shore; the tide ebbed and he could not depart; his followers all deserted him; a student retainer carried him in a small boat and he hid in Jishan village.
translations.idiomatic: He had already prepared boats at the seashore, but the tide ebbed and he could not depart; his followers all deserted him; a student retainer carried him in a small boat, and he hid in Jishan village.

sentences.zh: 偽車騎從事中郎張綏先遣人於錢唐詣喜歸誠，及覬走，綏閉封倉庫，以待王師。

translations.literal: The false attendant-in-ordinary of the chariotry, Zhang Sui, had already sent men to Qiantang to pledge allegiance to Xi; when Xu Ji fled, Sui sealed the storehouses and granaries, awaiting the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel attendant-in-ordinary of the chariotry, Zhang Sui, had already sent men to Qiantang to pledge allegiance to Xi; when Xu Ji fled, Sui sealed the storehouses and granaries to await the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，晏至郡，入自北門，囚綏付作部，其夜殺之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first, Yan reached the commandery, entering by the north gate; he imprisoned Sui and handed him to the convict labor section; that night he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first Yan reached the commandery and entered by the north gate; he imprisoned Sui and handed him over to the convict labor office, and that night had him executed.

sentences.zh: 執尋陽王子房於別署，縱兵大掠，府庫空盡。

translations.literal: He seized Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, in a separate office and let the soldiers loot on a grand scale until the treasury storehouses were utterly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, in a separate office and let the troops loot on a grand scale until the treasury and storehouses were utterly emptied.

sentences.zh: 若邪村民錄送偽龍驤將軍、車騎中兵參軍軍主孔叡，將斬之。

translations.literal: Villagers of Ruoye delivered up the false Flying Dragon General and Chief Retainer of the Chariotry and army commander Kong Rui; they were about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers of Ruoye delivered up the rebel Flying Dragon General, chief retainer of the chariotry and army commander Kong Rui, who was about to be executed.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「吾年已過立，未沾官伍，蒙知己之顧，以身許之。

translations.literal: Rui said: "I have already passed the age of manhood, yet never touched the official registers; relying on my patron's regard, I pledged my body to his service.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said: "I have already passed thirty, yet never entered the official registers; honored by my patron's regard, I pledged my life to his service.

sentences.zh: 今日就死，亦何所恨！

translations.literal: To die today—what is there to regret!
translations.idiomatic: To die today—what is there to regret!

sentences.zh: 」含笑就戮。

translations.literal: He went to execution with a smile on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He went to his death with a smile.

sentences.zh: 孔璪叛投門生陸林夫，林夫斬首送之。

translations.literal: Kong An, having rebelled, fled to his student retainer Lu Linfu; Linfu beheaded him and presented the head.
translations.idiomatic: Kong An fled to his student retainer Lu Linfu; Linfu beheaded him and presented the head.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，脊山民縛覬送詣晏，晏謂之曰：「此事孔璪所為，無豫卿事。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second, the villagers of Jishan bound Xu Ji and delivered him to Yan; Yan said to him: "This affair was wrought by Kong An; you have no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second the villagers of Jishan bound Xu Ji and delivered him to Yan; Yan said to him: "This was Kong An's doing; you had no part in it.

sentences.zh: 可作首辭，當相為申上。

translations.literal: You may draw up the principal confession; I shall intercede for you above."
translations.idiomatic: Draw up the principal confession, and I shall plead your case above."

sentences.zh: 」覬曰：「江東處分，莫不由身，委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳！

translations.literal: Xu Ji said: "Every disposition in Jiangdong was mine alone; to shift blame and beg for life—that is conduct fit for men of your kind!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji said: "Every decision in Jiangdong was mine alone; to shift blame and beg for your lives—that is the way of men like you!"

sentences.zh: 」晏乃斬之東閣外。

translations.literal: Yan then beheaded him outside the eastern pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then beheaded him outside the eastern pavilion.

sentences.zh: 臨死求酒，曰：「此是平生所好。

translations.literal: Before death he asked for wine, saying: "This was what I loved all my life.
translations.idiomatic: Before his death he asked for wine, saying: "This was what I loved all my life.

sentences.zh: 」時年五十一。

translations.literal: He was fifty-one years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等並詣喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。

translations.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others all came to Xi to confess guilt; Xi pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and the others all came to Xi to confess their guilt; Xi pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 琛子寶素與父相失，自縊死。

translations.literal: Chen's son Baosu, separated from his father, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's son Baosu, separated from his father, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 東軍主凡七十六人，於陳斬十七人，其餘皆原宥。

translations.literal: Eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded in battle array, the rest were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded on the field, and the rest were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 初，遣庾業向會稽，追使奉朝請孫長度送仗與之，並令召募。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu Ye was dispatched to Kuaiji, a pursuing messenger was sent with the Court Gentleman Sun Changdu to deliver weapons to him, with orders likewise to raise recruits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yu Ye was dispatched to Kuaiji, a messenger was sent with the court gentleman Sun Changdu to deliver weapons to him and likewise to raise recruits.

sentences.zh: 行達晉陵，袁標就其求仗，長度不與，為標所殺。

translations.literal: When they reached Jinling en route, Yuan Biao sought weapons from him; Changdu would not yield them and was killed by Biao.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Jinling on the way, Yuan Biao sought weapons from him; Changdu refused, and Biao killed him.

sentences.zh: 追贈給事中。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was ennobled with the title Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄧琬遣臨川內史張淹自南路出東陽，淹遣龍驤將軍桂遑、征西行參軍劉越緒屯據定陽縣。

translations.literal: Before this, Deng Wan had dispatched the Interior Minister of Linchuan, Zhang Yan, southward toward Dongyang; Yan sent the Flying Dragon General Gui Yuan and the Campaigning-West Army Adjutant Liu Yuexu to occupy and hold Dingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Deng Wan had dispatched Zhang Yan, interior minister of Linchuan, south toward Dongyang; Yan sent the Flying Dragon General Gui Yuan and the Campaigning-West army adjutant Liu Yuexu to occupy Dingyang County.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王休若遣沈思仁討之，思仁遣軍主崔公烈攻其營，斬幢主朱伯符首，桂遑、劉越緒諸軍並奔逸。

translations.literal: Prince of Baling Xiaoxiu dispatched Shen Sirren to attack them; Sirren sent the army commander Cui Gonglie to assault their camp, beheading the standard-bearer Zhu Bofu; Gui Yuan, Liu Yuexu, and all their armies scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaoxiu of Baling dispatched Shen Sirren to attack them; Sirren sent the army commander Cui Gonglie to assault their camp and beheaded the standard-bearer Zhu Bofu; Gui Yuan, Liu Yuexu, and all their forces fled.

sentences.zh: 晉安太守劉瞻據郡同逆，建安內史趙道生起義討之，聚徒未合。

translations.literal: The Grand Prefect of Jinan, Liu Zhan, held the commandery in league with the rebels; the Interior Minister of Jianan, Zhao Daoqi, rose in loyal revolt to attack him, but had not yet gathered his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, grand prefect of Jinan, held the commandery with the rebels; Zhao Daoqi, interior minister of Jianan, rose in loyal revolt to attack him, but had not yet gathered his followers.

sentences.zh: 七月，思仁遣軍主姚宏祖、鮑伯奮、應寄生等討破瞻，斬之於羅江縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Sirren dispatched the army commanders Yao Hongzu, Bao Bofen, and Ying Jisheng and others to defeat Zhan; he was beheaded at Luojiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Sirren dispatched the army commanders Yao Hongzu, Bao Bofen, and Ying Jisheng and others to defeat Zhan and beheaded him at Luojiang County.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬先遣新安太守陽伯子及軍主任獻子襲黟縣，縣令吳茹公固守，力不敵，棄城走，伯子等屯據縣城。

translations.literal: Deng Wan had first sent the Grand Prefect of Xin'an, Yang Bozi, and the army commander Ren Xianzi to raid Yi County; the magistrate Wu Rugong held firm in defense, but his strength was unequal and he abandoned the city and fled; Bozi and others encamped and held the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan had first sent Yang Bozi, grand prefect of Xin'an, and the army commander Ren Xianzi to raid Yi County; the magistrate Wu Rugong held firm, but his strength was unequal and he abandoned the city and fled; Bozi and his men occupied the county seat.

sentences.zh: 茹公與臺軍主丘敬文、李靈賜、蕭柏壽等攻圍彌時，八月乃克，斬伯子、獻子首。

translations.literal: Rugong, with the imperial army commanders Qiu Jingwen, Li Lingci, Xiao Baisou, and others, besieged for a long interval; only in the eighth month was it taken, and the heads of Bozi and Xianzi were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Rugong, with the imperial army commanders Qiu Jingwen, Li Lingci, Xiao Baisou, and others, besieged them for a long time; only in the eighth month was the city taken, and Bozi and Xianzi were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 張淹屯軍上饒縣，聞劉胡敗，軍副鄱陽太守費曇欲圖之，詐云：「得鄧琬信，急宜諮論。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan encamped his army at Shangrao County; hearing of Liu Hu's defeat, the army deputy, the Grand Prefect of Poyang, Fei Dan, wished to plot against him, falsely reporting: "A letter has come from Deng Wan; urgent counsel is required.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan encamped his army at Shangrao County; when he heard of Liu Hu's defeat, his army deputy Fei Dan, grand prefect of Poyang, wished to plot against him and falsely reported: "A letter has arrived from Deng Wan; urgent counsel is required.

sentences.zh: 」欲因此斬淹。

translations.literal: He wished thereby to behead Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He intended thereby to behead Yan.

sentences.zh: 淹素事佛，方禮佛，不得時進。

translations.literal: Yan had long been devoted to Buddhism; he was in the midst of worshipping the Buddha and could not come promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had long been devoted to Buddhism; he was in the midst of worship and could not come at once.

sentences.zh: 曇復誑云捕虎，借大鼓及仗士二百人，淹信而與之。

translations.literal: Dan again deceived him, claiming they were hunting a tiger, and borrowed a great drum and two hundred armed soldiers; Yan believed him and lent them.
translations.idiomatic: Dan deceived him again, claiming they were hunting a tiger, and borrowed a great drum and two hundred armed soldiers; Yan believed him and lent them.

sentences.zh: 曇因率眾入山，饗士約誓，揚言虎走城西，鳴鼓大呼，直來趣城；

translations.literal: Dan then led his men into the mountains, feasted the soldiers and bound them by oath, proclaiming that the tiger had fled to the west of the city; beating drums and shouting loudly, they came straight toward the city;
translations.idiomatic: Dan then led his men into the mountains, feasted the soldiers and bound them by oath, proclaiming that the tiger had fled west of the city; beating drums and shouting, they came straight for the town;

sentences.zh: 城門守衛，悉委仗觀之，曇率眾突入，淹正禮佛，聞難走出，因斬首。

translations.literal: the gate guards all cast aside their weapons to watch; Dan led his men in a sudden rush; Yan was in the midst of worshipping the Buddha, heard the disturbance and fled out, and was thereupon beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: the gate guards all cast aside their weapons to watch; Dan led his men in a sudden rush; Yan was at worship, heard the disturbance and fled out, and was thereupon beheaded.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自江左以來，舉干戈以圖宗國，十有一焉，其能克振者，四而已矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Since the establishment of the realm south of the Yangtze, those who have raised weapons against the imperial clan number eleven; of those able to triumph and restore order, only four.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Since the court moved south of the Yangtze, eleven times men have taken up arms against the imperial house; of those who succeeded in restoring order, only four.

sentences.zh: 元皇外守虛器，政由王氏；

translations.literal: Emperor Yuandi outwardly guarded an empty vessel; government lay in the hands of the Wang clan;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuandi outwardly held an empty throne; government lay in the hands of the Wang clan;

sentences.zh: 蘇峻事雖暫申，旋受屠磔；

translations.literal: Su Jun's affair, though briefly prospering, was swiftly subjected to slaughter and dismemberment;
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's rebellion, though briefly successful, was swiftly crushed and dismembered;

sentences.zh: 桓玄宣武之子，運屬橫流；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan was the son of the Martial Proclaimer; his fate coincided with a torrent in flood;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was the son of Huan Wen, the Martial Proclaimer; his fortune met a flood-tide of chaos;

sentences.zh: 世祖仗順入討，民無異望。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, relying on righteousness, entered in punitive expedition, and the people harbored no other expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu marched in on the side of righteousness, and the people harbored no other hope.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆漆顙夷宗，作戒於後，何哉？

translations.literal: All the rest daubed their foreheads with lacquer and had their clans extirpated, serving as warnings to posterity—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: All the rest were marked with lacquer on the forehead and had their clans extinguished, serving as warnings to posterity—why is this?

sentences.zh: 夫勝敗之數，實由眾心，社廟尊嚴，民情所係，安以義動，猶或稱難，況長戟指闕，志在陵暴者乎！

translations.literal: As for the calculus of victory and defeat, it truly lies in the hearts of the multitude; the altars of state are august, bound to the people's sentiment—when one moves with righteousness, it is still called difficult; how much more when long halberds point at the palace gates and the will aims at overthrow!
translations.idiomatic: Victory and defeat depend on the hearts of the people; the altars of state are august and bound to popular sentiment—even when one moves with righteousness, it is still called difficult; how much more when long halberds point at the palace gates and the aim is tyranny!

sentences.zh: 泰始交爭，逆順未辨，太宗身劋悖亂，事惟拯溺，國道屯詖，宜立長君，太祖之昭，義無不可。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era rivalry broke out; rebel and loyal had not yet been distinguished; Emperor Taizong himself had been cut by the turmoil; his task was solely to rescue the drowning; the state road was blocked in calamity—it was fitting to establish a mature lord; by the precedence of Taizu, there was none that could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era the rivals clashed and rebel from loyal was not yet clear; Emperor Taizong himself was wounded in the turmoil; his task was solely to rescue the drowning; the state was in dire straits and a mature ruler should be established—by Taizu's precedent, nothing was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 子勛體自世祖，家運已絕，當璧之命，屬有所歸。

translations.literal: Zixun's person derived from Emperor Shizu; his house's fortune was already spent; the mandate to receive the royal jade seal had its due destination elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun sprang from Emperor Shizu's line, but his house's fortune was spent; the mandate to receive the jade seal belonged elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 曲直二途，未知攸適。

translations.literal: The crooked and the straight—two paths whose goal was not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong—two paths whose destination was not yet known.

sentences.zh: 徒以據有神甸，擅資天府，宗稷之重，威臨四方，以中制外，故能式清區宇。

translations.literal: They relied merely on holding the divine domain, monopolizing the resources of heaven's storehouse; the weight of the ancestral altars exerted awe over the four quarters—using the center to control the periphery, thus they could bring order to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They relied merely on holding the sacred capital, monopolizing the imperial treasury; the weight of the ancestral altars awed the four quarters—using the center to control the periphery, and thus could bring order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王所居，目以眾大之號，名曰京師，其義趣遠有以也。

translations.literal: Where emperors dwell is called by a title denoting vast multitude—the name "capital"; its meaning and import extend far, and for good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Where emperors dwell is given a title denoting vast multitude—the name "capital"; its meaning extends far, and with good reason.
